Afterwards Xianyun and Zhongli share a brief talk about the past and future and she plans a feast to introduce her new disciple Shuyu to Ganyu and Shenhe.

48.content:
Chiwang Terrace (also: Chiwang Terrace (Quest Domain), Chìwàng-tái, Chiwang Peak): Chiwang Terrace is an ancient terrace of ritual on Mt. Laixin, the sacred mountain of Chenyu Vale in southern Liyue, where the vale's spirit veins meet. It is above the clouds and open to the sky, and it is where the old people of the vale were said to speak with the heavens. It became central when the adeptus Fujin and the Traveler stopped her old friend Lingyuan from rewriting the spirit veins there.

Its design matches an altar remembered from the lost civilisation of Lang-Gan, which suggests the terrace is a keepsake of that people, who fled the Chasm and settled in Chenyu Vale. It is known to the wider world only through the vale's local lore and a few adepti.

Geography: The terrace stands on Mt. Laixin, called "the sacred mountain" because the spirit veins of Chenyu Vale converge there; whoever controls the mountain can reshape the land of the whole vale. In the world quest it is a separate quest domain reached by a ritual gate, with the sky and cloud sea around it. Nearby are the cave shelters and murals of Chizhang Wall, and the Votive Rainjade at Carp's Rest, whose offerings are unlocked through a follow-up quest.

The terrace is a raised, open stone platform where the spirit veins can be read as flowing lines of adeptal energy. Mt. Laixin as a whole is a restricted area that opens only through the 4.4 world quest series.

History: Lan Yan, whose family comes from Chenyu Vale, says the vale's ancient people used the terrace to commune with the heavens. The wiki ties it to the Lang-Gan altar where Zibai was honoured; see the uncertainties on whether it is a copy or the original. After the Chasm was created by a Celestial Nail, the refugees of Lang-Gan carried their traditions to Chenyu Vale, where later adepti such as Fujin taught the Rainjade Rite of jade offerings.

In the 4.4 quest "An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade", Lingyuan, a suanni adeptus who longs for the untamed vale of the distant past, had been quietly altering the spirit veins for ages, which spread miasma as a side effect. Fujin, a golden carp spirit who loved humans, opened the gate to the terrace with a ritual, and the Traveler destroyed the Miasmic Simulacra Lingyuan used to redirect the flow until she yielded. Fujin then spent all her gathered strength healing the soil and water and reverted to her carp form.

Atmosphere: A quiet height of weathered stone above a sea of cloud; wind, mist and jade-green light over the vale; a place that feels like a stage made for prayer, with the slow hum of spirit veins under the feet. Anything held there is about promises made to heaven and land.

Quests: "An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade" (4.4), the third quest of "Chenyu's Blessings of Sunken Jade", unlocks the terrace. It is also mentioned in Act I of "A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Lingyuan has promised not to hinder Fujin's work, the spirit veins are calm, and the terrace is a quiet relic of older rites.

Fujin remains in carp form. Remaining miasma in Chenyu Vale is a separate problem for visitors.

49.comment: Chiwang Terrace: Chiwang Terrace and the Lang-Gan altar
49.content: Chenyu Vale tradition says the ancient people communed with the heavens at Chiwang Terrace. The wiki and the 6.3 event link it to the jade altar of Lang-Gan, where lanterns and offerings were presented to the Three Moons and to Zibai. Whether the terrace is a rebuilt copy or the original altar carried from the Chasm is left open by canon. The event happened during Lantern Rite 2026.

50.comment: Chiwang Terrace: Chiwang Terrace in the Lantern Rite story
50.content: During the Lantern Rite event "A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon" (6.3, later kept as a replayable story quest), a photograph of the moon with a bite taken from it, shot above Chiwang Terrace, linked the terrace to the Chasm in the investigators' minds. Zizhi, a remnant of Zibai's soul, said the altar looked just like the one used in Lang-Gan to honour Zibai, and a vision showed the people of Lang-Gan releasing lanterns at such an altar under a Trilunar Syzygy before the Celestial Nail fell.

51.content:
Chizhang Wall (also: Chizhang, Chìzhāng Chéngyuán, Ancient City of Chizhang, Huangcong Grounds): Chizhang Wall is a stretch of ruined rampart and cave shelters in southern Chenyu Vale, north of Mt. Xuanlian. The wiki names it the remains of the ancient city of Chizhang, governed by the Mistress of Chenyu Vale. Painted murals and scattered "Records of the Ancestors" tell of villagers saved by a great adeptus, of jade offerings made at Chiwang, and of a people who once left the Chasm.

A Solitary Suanni now haunts the ground. The place matters mostly as an archive: what survives on its walls is the best surviving picture of the vale's ancient people.

Geography: Chizhang Wall lies in the Southern Mountain part of Chenyu Vale, north of Mt. Xuanlian. It is broken stone wall, ruined foundations and a set of cave shelters in the hillside, some with painted murals. A Solitary Suanni is the area's only notable enemy.

The caves include a mural cave in the northwest (called Huangcong Grounds), a shelter in the northeast whose key panel was removed, and a southeast shelter whose hidden mural is sealed by a jade device. The achievements "The Mural Veil" and "A Ruined Tale" are earned by cleaning and finding them.

History: Fujin says the caves were shelters built by the adepti during the Archon War, so ordinary people caught between floods and fighting would have a safe place. The murals show the people of the vale with their adepti and with the Votive Rainjade rite.

The Records of the Ancestors describe villagers chased by mountain beasts and rescued by a great and beautiful adeptus; a "divine rite" was approaching, the jade was to be divided so that wicked spirits could not take it, and a part was to be offered at Chiwang so the heavens would hear; the courtyard was sealed on the adeptus's orders. A later fragment speaks of someone painting on this wall as lasting testimony.

The hidden southeast mural shows the people of Chenyu Vale leaving the Chasm with a Celestial Nail in the background, tying the vale's founders to the destruction of the Lang-Gan region. The most important section of the northeast mural, showing Fujin and the Herblord, was taken to the Adeptus's Repose; Fujin, seeing it for the first time, could only guess why, suspecting the old mountain mistress's anger toward those who defected.

Atmosphere: Moss over old paint, shadow in the caves, a feeling of reading a diary left in the open. The wall is quiet and dignified, closer to a memorial than to a fortress.

Dangers: A Solitary Suanni patrols the area; the sealed mural cave opens only through the jade mechanism.

Quests: Fujin shows the Traveler these murals in "An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade" (4.4), before they move on toward Chiwang Terrace.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 an abandoned, silent ruin with preserved murals and no inhabitants.

52.comment: Chizhang Wall: Murals and Records of the Ancestors
52.content:
The murals show the people of Chenyu Vale with the Votive Rainjade and with their adepti, and the secret mural shows their departure from the Chasm under a Celestial Nail. The Records of the Ancestors are three groups of ancient text fragments: a rescue by a great adeptus, a jade offering at Chiwang, and a mourning writer who paints on the wall. Treat the fragments as partial, damaged accounts, not full chronicles.

Fujin, who built these shelters, had never seen the mural herself, so her reading of its damage is speculative.

53.content:
Chunming Teaworks: The Chunming Teaworks is the tea workshop of Qiaoying Village in Chenyu Vale. Most of the village's picked tea leaves are sent here to be processed, and its map description says its reputation reaches far beyond the village.

It is run by the veteran Ding Sr. with the younger Ding Jr., and it blends age-old methods with newer machines for drying leaves and roasting tea.

Practice: Fresh leaves need several careful steps before they can become tea. According to Ding Sr., the workshop handles sunning, baking and stirring the leaves in a pan to drive off excess moisture, which deepens the fragrance and makes the tea easier to store. Some varieties are then taken back by the farmers for further work such as piling and fermenting.

Stirring used to be done in a huge tea cauldron that Ding Sr. says was some kind of adeptal mechanism. The workshop now uses faster machines to meet demand, and he stresses that more heat and speed mean quality control matters even more, which is why people with thirty-odd years of experience, like him, supervise. He advises visitors to stay in the village about a month to see the process from picking to the table.

Ding Sr. says Ding Jr. still has about a decade of learning ahead of him. After the quest "An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade", Ding Jr. says he always believed the legends of the Carp Adeptus were true. If a visitor tramples the leaves drying in the middle of the room, Ding Sr. scolds them, reminding them the leaves are for everyone's teacups and that Uncle Luo may be angry enough to have them evicted from the village.

People: Ding Sr. is the experienced overseer; Ding Jr. is his junior in the craft. Both are ordinary villagers with no established family or story beyond the workshop.

Status as of 7.1: A working workshop as of 7.1.

Its map description credits it as perhaps the reason Qiaoying Village's tea is so famous.

54.content: Scene use: a visitor is greeted as a would-be tour guest; Ding Sr. gladly explains each step of the processing and is protective of the leaves. The machine room contrasts with the village's traditional image.

55.content:
Cinnabar Cliff: Cinnabar Cliff is a surface subarea of the Chasm in Liyue. It is called a tourist spot, though locals reportedly never go there, and it holds a Statue of The Seven, a Geo Elemental Monument and hostile Fatui Skirmishers.

A quest domain from the Archon Quests, the Unknown Sanctuary, is placed here on the map even though it belongs to Sumeru's story. A self-styled hero called Tang Wuchou, who is really a Treasure Hoarder, stands here.

Geography: Features are a Statue of The Seven, a Geo Elemental Monument, Geograna, Spoutrocks, Unique Rocks and Unique Rock Pillars. Cor Lapis, Qingxin and Violetgrass grow here.

It sits within the Chasm's surface area above the Underground Mines. The Chinese name is Dansha Cliff, the word dansha meaning cinnabar.

People: Tang Wuchou, a Treasure Hoarder, is found here in the open world; the wiki gives him the self-proclaimed title Guhua Hero, with a question mark, and an idle line imagines a garden of Glaze Lilies. After the world quest The Missing Miner, the miner Uncle He can be found here too.

Per the wiki's trivia, Cinnabar Cliff is considered a tourist spot but locals never go there, citing the quest Says He Who Seeks Stone.

Quests: The Unknown Sanctuary is a quest domain used in the Archon Quests "A Lamenter at Fate's End" and "Portended Fate". Its description says hilichurls were seen heading there, faithful and unwavering, and a companion tells the Traveler he has never seen anything like it. The domain's enemies are hilichurls and slimes of several elements.

The wiki flags the domain as a Sumeru quest domain placed on the Chasm's map at Cinnabar Cliff. It is in the Liyue map but belongs to Sumeru content; do not move the setting of those quests to Liyue.

As gameplay, the domain is a short run of teleports between platforms with waves of Hydro, Electro, Pyro and Cryo Slimes, including large and mutant ones, plus optional hilichurls that vanish when they or the player step into the portal. It holds four chests.

Dangers: A Blazing Axe Mitachurl is the elite enemy. Common foes are Fatui Skirmishers (Geochanter Bracers, Anemoboxer Vanguards and Electrohammer Vanguards), Rock Shield Hilichurl Guards and Geo Slimes.

Atmosphere: An exposed cliff by the Chasm with a lone Statue of The Seven, Fatui patrols and the occasional hoarder. This is a suggested scene mood drawn from the feature list, not a quoted description.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1.

56.content:
Clear Pool and Mountain Cavern: Clear Pool and Mountain Cavern is a Domain of Blessing north of Mt. Aocang in Liyue: an ancient altar in a hidden stone cave where monsters that fear Geo guard Artifacts. Its in-game text says Mt. Aocang looks like pretty scenery but hides a cave "connecting to the heavens" that breathes out clouds.

Inside, the ley lines are tuned to Geo. Every party member deals extra Geo damage, and the three trials are all called "Stone Chamber". The enemies are Treasure Hoarders, rock-shield hilichurls and mitachurls, and finally a Ruin Guard.

The domain's description adds that the saying "where the clouds emerge" was not derived from this cave. The Chinese name carries the sense of the mountain's deeply hidden wonders.

Geography: The entrance is on the northern side of Mt. Aocang, in the Minlin area of Liyue. Mt. Aocang is the mountain where the adeptus Cloud Retainer (Xianyun) lived in seclusion after the Archon War. Outside the cave, nearby, a ruins treasure with a pillar of light tells the story of a disciple who received a Vision and is linked to a similar one at Guyun Stone Forest.

Beneath the pretty pools and cliffs lies the stone cave. It is a classic domain: a closed, walled arena reached through an altar gate rather than an open wilderness.

Dangers: Gameplay rules, labelled as such: the ley line disorder gives all party members +75% Geo damage across the three trials; levels II and III also grant a Geo DMG bonus. Recommended element is Geo. Stage one has Treasure Hoarder Crushers and Pugilists, stage two has Rock Shield Hilichurl Guards and Rock Shieldwall Mitachurls, and stage three a single Ruin Guard.

Rewards are Artifacts from Bloodstained Chivalry, Noblesse Oblige, Gambler and Scholar. In a scene, treat it as a tight, echoing stone arena with pillars of earthy light.

Trial structure, as gameplay detail: stage one asks for 12 opponents (six Crushers, six Pugilists) in 300 seconds, stage two for 10 opponents (eight guards, two Shieldwall Mitachurls) in 360 seconds, and stage three for the single Ruin Guard in 360 seconds. Recommended levels run 69, 80 and 90 for Adventure Rank 35, 40 and 45 respectively. The level names are all "Stone Chamber", which probably reflects the Geo bonus rather than any place in the story.

Atmosphere: Cool, damp stone, still pools, thin clouds drifting through cave openings, and the hum of Geo energy in the walls.

Status as of 7.1: Permanent and unchanged as of Version 7.1.

57.comment: Clear Pool and Mountain Cavern: Mt. Aocang and the Cloud Retainer
57.content: Mt. Aocang is a mountain in Liyue's Minlin region, remembered as the retreat of the adeptus Cloud Retainer after the Archon War and until the events of "A Thousand Moonlit Miles". The domain lies to its north and is not described as belonging to her.

key: Abode of Retaining the Clouds by Borrowing the Wind
58.content:
Cloud Retainer's Abode (also: Abode of Cloud Retainer, Abode of Retaining the Clouds by Borrowing the Wind): Cloud Retainer's Abode is the hidden home of the adeptus Cloud Retainer (later called Xianyun) at the top of Mt. Aocang in Liyue. It is a space of rotating platforms, bridges, wind currents and elemental mechanisms that she says she built and designed herself, and visitors reach it only by laying out a food offering.

It appears twice: in the Archon Quest Custodian of Clouds (Version 1.0), where the Traveler and Paimon come to tell her of the death of Rex Lapis, and in the world quest An Adeptal Summons, where she sends them to fetch her old blueprints. Outside those quests the entrance only notes that the adeptus does not want guests.

The place is also a showcase of her mechanical craft. She says Guizhong and Rex Lapis commended her work, and in the second quest she dismisses the Jade Chamber as dull beside her own inventions.

Geography: The abode lies at the top of Mt. Aocang in the Minlin area of Liyue. Visitors find a barrier the Traveler cannot pass at first, a pond with a round stone table at its centre, and a door that opens once an offering has been accepted.

Inside, the domain is a chain of floating stone platforms joined by bridges that rotate when a device is activated. The way alternates between slimes and hilichurls, timed Pyro Monument puzzles, and wind currents that lift the party to the next platform. At the end Cloud Retainer waits on an archway in crane form.

Gameplay detail: it is a quest domain with five chests (two common, two exquisite, one precious) and a recommended Pyro element. Characters who can gain height (Geo constructs, wind or flight abilities, blink skills) can glide past the platform puzzles. In An Adeptal Summons the same space becomes a time trial in which the party carries her blueprints across the platforms.

Places: Notable spots are the stone table in the middle of Mt. Aocang's pond, the abode's door, the moving platforms and the final archway.

The table has three stone chairs with carved names: Retainer (with a wine jar before it), Guizhong (a bowl and chopsticks) and Rex (an empty place). Canon does not explain them; they sit beside her remark that Guizhong and Rex Lapis admired her work. The pots around the pond hold cooking traces and recipe notes used in the offering quest. A stone tablet up the stairs reads that the Free Adeptus, the Unfettered, performs no action and sets no rule.

People: The occupant is the adeptus Cloud Retainer, whose human-form name is Xianyun. She is a crane adeptus who values quiet, mechanical invention and good food, and deals with mortals strictly on her own terms. Her disciple Shenhe is listed by the wiki as affiliated with the abode.

Xianyun says mortal pilgrims once left food at the Mt. Aocang altar and some turned up asking to be disciples. To disperse them she posted a sign demanding ninety-nine different dishes over ninety-nine days, each with Qingxin as the main ingredient, and the crowd left. Moon Carver, an old adeptus acquaintance, is the one who sent the Traveler to her in the first quest.

She also recalls building a Snowdrift Mechanism on the mountain for skiing with Guizhong and another adeptus, until Moon Carver sent it off the rails into a snow bank; she later added safety features at the cost of speed. These anecdotes come from her voice-overs and show the mountain as a place of shared play before it became a place of seclusion.

History: Xianyun's profile and the Mt. Aocang page place her isolation on the mountain after the Archon War and until A Thousand Moonlit Miles. She says she built the abode herself.

In Custodian of Clouds she meets the news of Rex Lapis' assassination with anger and speaks of quashing Liyue first and then consulting the other adepti. Because the Traveler arrived with a Sigil of Permission and an accepted offering, which she treats as a contract, she holds back; she says the sigil's power has mostly faded and that she must investigate the claims herself. She says the adepti guarded Liyue Harbor under Rex Lapis for 37 centuries, and that Moon Carver's summons is the reason for what follows.

In An Adeptal Summons she asks the Traveler to bring blueprints she left, behind a seal, at her Dwelling in the Clouds, a separate floating island near Qingyun Peak. She uses them to make a point against the Jade Chamber. Per the Dwelling's own text, that island began as her private sanctuary, was later used by other adepti for a trial, and is again in her care. In Version 4.4's A Thousand Moonlit Miles she leaves in human form to check on her disciples in Liyue Harbor, and afterwards takes up residence in the city.

Culture: Offerings are the key. A dish laid at the table earns a hearing; in the world quest a single dish buys only a short audience. The recipes the Traveler finds by the pots are Jewelry Soup, Matsutake Meat Rolls and Mora Meat.

Her speech sets the tone: she refers to herself as "one" or "this adeptus", addresses visitors formally, and turns sharp once the business is finished.

Atmosphere: A calm mountain pond under thin cloud, a laid table with nobody at it, and a closed door; inside, creaking mechanisms, drifting platforms and sudden wind currents, all under the eye of an unseen and faintly irritable adeptus.

Dangers: The main hazard is falling into the void and the occupant's temper, not guards. Slimes and a few hilichurls patrol the platforms. Failing the timed challenge in An Adeptal Summons, or falling off, sends the party out of the domain.

Travel: Climb Mt. Aocang to the pond and table, offer food, and enter through the abode's door. Outside the two quests the domain cannot be entered.

Quests: Custodian of Clouds (Archon Quest, Chapter I Act I, Version 1.0) and An Adeptal Summons (world quest, requires Farewell, Archaic Lord). Xianyun's A Thousand Moonlit Miles (4.4) opens at Mt. Aocang.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 the abode is available only as a quest domain, and Xianyun lives in Liyue Harbor. Mt. Aocang is still used by the adepti in later content: Zhongli, Xianyun, Madame Ping, Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver gather there at a Lantern Rite, and seal it off during a later quest.

59.content: Cloud Retainer is the adeptus name of Xianyun, a crane adeptus who built the abode on Mt. Aocang. She prizes mechanical invention, her privacy and food offerings. Her own entry holds her biography; this one covers only her home.

60.comment: Cloud Retainer's Abode: Mt. Aocang offerings
60.content: Visitors to the pond at Mt. Aocang earn an audience with Cloud Retainer by cooking the dishes whose recipes lie by the nearby pots. Pilgrims who once came to be disciples were told to bring ninety-nine different Qingxin dishes over ninety-nine days.

61.content:
Cuijue Slope: Cuijue Slope is a stark hillside in Minlin, Liyue, ringed by nine tall stone pillars around a central temple. Walking near them turns the sky dim and grey. Local lore offers almost nothing about them beyond a tablet saying they were raised to hold nine human desires at bay, so that war would never return, and that whoever breaks them should take the treasure inside and protect Liyue.

Opening the pillars needs Stones of Remembrance, which the player gets by making offerings at Liyue's Statues of the Seven. The treasure chamber's chief prize is a very old ring.

Geography: A subarea of Minlin. The Nine Pillars of Peace stand in a valley with a temple at the centre. Near the pillars the sky turns dark and grey and the land outside the slope takes on an unnaturally dim look, an effect that fades with distance. From the slope, Dragonspine and Wangshu Inn can be seen in the distance.

In an early test build of the game the pillars stood closer together and the valley was shallower and dry, with no special sky effect; the current layout is the released one. The wiki records Pyro Regisvine as the area's boss and lists Cor Lapis, Qingxin and Violetgrass as local specialties.

Places: The Nine Pillars of Peace (a point of interest in their own right) and the ruined temple at their centre.

The temple's entrance is built in a style the wiki says is otherwise seen only in Chenyu Vale (for example at Chizhang Wall), and its door bears an insignia found nowhere else. Inside, greenish-blue lighting, unlike any other ruin, leads to a chamber with a large Pan Chang knot ringed by four more, and two yaksha statues guarding the doorway to the treasure room.

History: The tablet at the centre states the purpose in the builders' own voice. All turmoil comes from human vice; nine pillars are raised to suppress conflict so that armies are never again raised against each other. Inside the temple a second inscription names the nine desires: greed, nostalgia, vision, jealousy, anger, lust, self-aggrandizement, competition and turmoil. They can "heal the world, or do it great hurt," and the pillars are laid down to end the conflicts that plague it. A warning follows: if a later visitor breaks the pillars and enters, war will consume the world again, so any reader who does so should take the treasure and bring peace to Liyue.

Who built them and when is not stated. A note on the Chinese text says the last line reads more literally as "defend Liyue in the eight directions" than "bring peace." The wiki notes that the mask on each pillar, where a Stone of Remembrance is set, resembles a squashed yaksha mask like Xiao's, and that Stones of Remembrance come from offerings made to Liyue's Statues of the Seven, suggesting a link to Morax; this is the wiki's inference, not an in-game statement.

Atmosphere: Oppressive and ceremonial: grey sky, silent stone, a sealed temple, and an inscription that frames treasure-hunting as a duty and a risk at once.

Dangers: Ordinary hilichurls, Fatui skirmishers, Treasure Hoarders and Abyss mages roam the slope. Inside the temple the Traveler faces an inactive Ruin Guard that wakes when approached, plus Geovishap Hatchlings and a Ruin Hunter in waves.

Quests: Nine Pillars of Peace (World Quest, available once the Prologue's first act is done). The player sets nine Stones of Remembrance, wins the chamber's prize and then chooses whom to sell the Dull Ring to, Bolai or Linlang, both in Liyue Harbor.

The ring is described as ancient yet well preserved, set with a fine gemstone, with an inscription inside the band: "Disaster runs rampant throughout the world, and all who live do so in agony." Linlang recognises the place as the ruin with nine pillars and a central tablet and says few dare to hunt treasure there.

The quest asks the player to pick a buyer: Linlang pays 200,000 Mora, while Bolai pays 180,000 Mora and five Adeptus' Temptation dishes. The choice is purely a gameplay reward decision and has no story consequence.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the slope is unchanged and still open to exploration. No later story content was found that alters it.

62.comment: Cuijue Slope: Nine Pillars of Peace
62.content: The pillars are a sealed monument whose builders meant them as a lock on human conflict. Breaking one by inlaying a Stone of Remembrance cracks the mask on its face and breaks away a section to reveal glowing geometry beneath. The temple's chamber holds the treasure and the Dull Ring. The inscriptions treat the pillars as a deliberate gamble: a peace maintained by sealing away what could end it.

63.content:
Dihua Marsh (also: Marsh of Rustling Reeds): Dihua Marsh is a wetland of rivers and silvergrass shaped by the Bishui River in Bishui Plain, Liyue, between the Stone Gate to the north and Wangshu Inn to the south. It lies on the main road between Mondstadt and Liyue, so merchant caravans stop and rest here. A Statue of the Seven stands at its northern end.

The name comes from the silvergrass (dihua) that grows in the shallows. The marsh is also remembered as the final resting place of many wandering fighters.

Geography: An alluvial plain made by the Bishui River, with a web of rivers supporting a wide ecosystem of plants and animals. Stone Gate lies to the north, Wangshu Inn to the south and Sal Terrae to the east. A waterfall in the northwest is well known to travelers, and the marsh sits near Mt. Qingce. The area's local specialty is Cor Lapis.

The official map description calls the area fertile, rich in aquatic plants and natural resources. The area's design drew on Guilin's scenery and architecture, according to the developers' travel-themed documentary cited by the wiki.

The wiki's trivia notes that dihua means Amur silvergrass, a cool-temperate grass of northeast Asia, and should not be confused with the similar Chinese silver grass. Besides Overstretched, the marsh hosts random events (Blocked Road, Hilichurl Nest, Key Supplies) and a fishing commission, Fishing Jiangxue.

Places: The Statue of the Seven on the northern end, along the main road, and Wangshu Inn, a tall inn that the official description calls a symbolic structure visible from all directions.

People: Open-world residents include the Millelith soldier Qiaoxi and several travelers and merchants, among them Hui, Hulu, Mengmeng, Strong and Yu.

Wangshu Inn's keepers are Verr Goldet and her husband Huai'an, agents of the Liyue Qixing who help Xiao in his work (see Wangshu Inn). Many caravan merchants pass through.

Travel: The marsh is the road from Mondstadt into Liyue, so caravans rest in its shallows and at the inn rather than push on into the hills. Official text describes the setting as awe-inspiring to newcomers.

Dangers: Hilichurl camps (fighters, shooters, grenadiers, Anemo samachurls), a Cryo Whopperflower and a Cryo Abyss Mage.

In the world quest Overstretched, Qiaoxi near the bridge in the middle of the marsh asks the Traveler to clear a nearby hilichurl camp that includes a Rock Shieldwall Mitachurl.

Atmosphere: The viewpoint text calls it a place where the sifting of the swaying silvergrass joins the croaking of frogs, and where many a wandering fighter has come to rest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the marsh is unchanged and remains a rest stop on the road between Mondstadt and Liyue. No later story content was found that alters it.

64.comment: Dihua Marsh: Wangshu Inn at Dihua Marsh
64.content: Wangshu Inn stands within Dihua Marsh, built tall for visibility. Zhongli calls it a strategic location that must be defended, and the inn has existed since at least the years after the Cataclysm, nearly 500 years ago. Seen from the top, it reaches all the way to Mt. Qingce and Jueyun Karst in clear weather. Its fuller history belongs to its own entry.

65.content:
Domain of Guyun: The Domain of Guyun is an Electro-themed Domain of Blessing on the largest island in Guyun Stone Forest, in Liyue's Sea of Clouds. Ancient ley line altars here guard Artifacts behind rounds of slime and Abyss enemies. Its description speaks of delusions and disappointments of an ancient ambition to lead humanity, gathered in the caverns under Guyun.

It has six levels, with ley line disorder built around Electro-Charged, Overloaded and Superconduct reactions. The level names are all "Spring", the translation of Jingzhe, the season when thunder wakes the sleeping insects.

Guyun Stone Forest itself is an archipelago of seven large islands. Legend says Rex Lapis beat a god and sea monster named Osial here and that the jagged cliffs are the stone lances he used. Those who sleep at Guyun may dream Osial's memories, though whether that comes from Osial or something else is unknown.

Geography: The domain lies on the largest of the seven islands in Guyun Stone Forest. The northernmost island houses the Geo Hypostasis.

A ruins treasure near Mt. Aocang is said to be related to one at Guyun and tells of a disciple who received a Vision.

Dangers: Gameplay rules, labelled as such: ley line disorder boosts Electro-Charged damage by 150% with 100% larger area at levels I and IV, and makes Overloaded (II, V) or Superconduct (III, VI) trigger an Energy Blast that damages nearby opponents. Recommended element is Electro; Cryo helps at level VI.

Enemies progress from Hydro and Pyro slimes to Cryo slimes with a Mitachurl, then hilichurls with Hydro Samachurls and an Abyss Mage, a Ruin Guard (with a central Pyro Elemental Node that periodically empowers enemies), and finally Fatui Skirmishers beside a Ruin Guard. Rewards are Artifacts from Archaic Petra, Retracing Bolide, Brave Heart and Lucky Dog.

Mechanics detail (gameplay, not lore): levels I to IV have you defend a Domain Monolith while clearing 28, 22, 20 and 20 enemies; level V is a 120-second fight against one Ruin Guard; level VI gives 420 seconds against three opponents. Energy Blasts deal Physical damage scaled to the level (about 1,126 at II up to about 4,811 at VI). The recommended level range is 34 to 90, with Adventure Rank 20 as the entry floor.

Atmosphere: Thin air, low clouds, crackling static, and sheer stone pillars; the altar's walls feel old and a little bitter.

Status as of 7.1: Permanent and unchanged as of Version 7.1.

66.comment: Domain of Guyun: Osial and the Guyun legend
66.content: Legend places Rex Lapis' defeat of the god-and-sea-monster Osial at Guyun Stone Forest, with the cliffs as remnants of his stone lances. Roald's diary suggests that anyone who spends a night there may experience Osial's memories of that defeat.

key: the nameless fishing village near Wangshu Inn
67.content:
Downriver (also: Downriver village, Xiàchuān, the nameless fishing village near Wangshu Inn): Downriver is an abandoned fishing village in Minlin, Liyue, a little west of Wangshu Inn. Its remaining houses are empty and falling apart. The village matters in canon as the place that took in the orphaned Beidou as a small child and later drove her out, long before she became captain of the Crux.

It is a Point of Interest rather than a settlement anyone lives in. Its name was first spoken in Beidou's hangout quest "Life on the High Seas" (the story event "When the Crux Shines Bright"); before that, the place appeared on the map and through two signboard messages left by former residents.

Geography: In Minlin, west of Wangshu Inn and visible from the inn. A scatter of old, weathered fishing houses; the village chief's former house is the best-known of them.

History: Fishing families moved here from an older village called Upriver, bringing generations of fishing know-how. Beidou arrived as a homeless child of about five or six and was taken in by the village chief. Roughly a year or two later the chief died of illness during winter, the catch and harvest shrank, and the villagers blamed her and drove her out. Over time everyone else left too.

The name Downriver came from this link to Upriver; Beidou says Upriver is long gone and that soon nobody may remember either name. In her telling, the village was never impressive but was lively and home to several families, and she learned a lot about fishing from them.

Her account of her arrival: she had been wandering the streets, found half a Rice Bun and was robbed of it by a stray dog, and chased it into this neighbourhood. Fishermen who saw her stop her and fed her. The dog collapsed and did not get up again, with the bun still in its mouth. The villagers were wary of the dirty child, but the chief took pity on her and brought her to their home.

When the chief fell ill and died, the harvest was already worsening and the fishermen's catch was dwindling. Without the chief to settle things, neighbours began blaming one another, with rumours that some families had been overfishing. In the end they turned on Beidou, calling her bad luck and pointing to the dog's death on her first day, then the chief's death, then the fish dying out. She told them she was not a curse, only Beidou. They shouted that Nandou controls life and Beidou controls death, and chased her away. She says that was when she learned her name was a constellation, and that Alcor, one of its stars, was an omen of death.

Beidou shares this with the Traveler during the hangout, and recounts it with wry humour rather than bitterness. Told the Traveler might be cursed too (the Anemo and Geo Gnoses were both taken soon after arriving), she laughs it off and offers to share the blame, which the hangout presents as the two of them being "scapegoats looking out for each other". This is hangout material: it is canon but was told to the Traveler in private, so ordinary Liyue residents are not assumed to know the story.

Atmosphere: Silent and sun-bleached: sagging roofs, empty doorways, water close by and no voices. Beidou calls it a place that has "certainly seen better days".

Places: Two signboards are the only written traces of the villagers. One, addressed "To Zhong", says fishing has grown harder, sales have dropped, and the villagers have decided to leave as a group and look for work elsewhere. Another message, also to Zhong, complains that the writer's letters were never answered and says the girl has left some things for Zhong in the usual place, by the main house.

The "girl" in the second message is not identified in the text. Players commonly connect these notes to Beidou's story, but canon does not say that the girl is Beidou, nor who Zhong is; see uncertainties.

Dangers: Nothing specific in canon beyond decay. Treat it as a quiet, safe, melancholy stop on the road near Wangshu Inn.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Downriver is still empty and crumbling. No later event is recorded there.

68.content: Beidou, captain of the Crux, was a homeless child of about five or six when she was taken in at Downriver by the village chief. After the chief died and the fish dwindled, the villagers blamed her and drove her out, using the saying that Nandou controls life and Beidou death. She revisits the ruined village with the Traveler in "Life on the High Seas".

69.content:
Dragon-Queller (also: Hidden Dragon Tree): The Dragon-Queller is a huge tree with glowing blue veins standing near Mt. Hulao at Nantianmen in Liyue. It is the seal that holds the Geo dragon Azhdaha, whom Morax and the adepti imprisoned there long ago after his erosion made him a danger to people. The developers describe the tree as Azhdaha's own tail.

Geography: The tree rises beside Mt. Hulao in the Nantianmen area of Liyue's Minlin region. Its branches carry a cold, moonlight-coloured glow, and one great blue branch at its tip points straight toward Liyue Harbor and cannot be climbed. Bright yellow flowers grow around its base; the same flowers are found in the lair of the Primo Geovishap. Its roots reach deep into the earth and, according to the dragon's own account, connect to the ley lines. A tunnel beneath it leads to the dragon's prison, which is entered as a domain.

The domain description calls the prison a bed of rock carved into the very heart of the world, a coffin that has held Azhdaha across the long years.

Places: Stone Monolith: a tablet set before the tree by the adeptus Mountain Shaper as a warning to passers-by. Its text, paraphrased, thanks the merciful adepti for life enduring in Heaven and Earth and states that an evil dragon lies here and must not be disturbed.

Beneath the Dragon-Queller: the prison itself, reached through the tunnel under the tree. Players fight Azhdaha there as a weekly boss; the story treats the fight as a memory of the encounter, because Azhdaha was re-sealed.

The domain entrance is marked with the elements Azhdaha will absorb inside, and his Cryo, Pyro, Electro and Hydro attacks mark characters who lack a shield. These are game mechanics, not in-world statements.

History: Azhdaha, an ancient earth dragon born of elemental crystallisation, once befriended Morax and humanity. Erosion made him forget Morax and lash out, and miners damaging the ley lines of the Chasm worsened his suffering. Morax and the adepti Mountain Shaper, Moon Carver and a third, unnamed adeptus fought him in a battle that began in the Chasm and ran north to Nantianmen, where, with the willing acceptance of his remaining conscience, they sealed the eroded dragon in the Dragon-Queller. The clash of elemental energy in that battle also created Dragonfall.

Centuries later the seal weakened. Azhdaha projected a portion of his power as the girl Jiu, and she drew a group of miners from the Chasm to the tree to break the seal with their pickaxes from outside. In Zhongli's story quest No Mere Stone (Version 1.5) the Traveler, Paimon and Zhongli, with an expert named Kun Jun, followed the trail. Kun Jun proved to be Azhdaha's benevolent half. The party was pulled into the prison, and Azhdaha was defeated and re-sealed. His benevolent consciousness thanked Zhongli and left Kun Jun's body; Zhongli assured it Liyue would be ready if the dragon ever woke again.

Details of the sealing, per the quest: Azhdaha, once blind, had asked Morax to let him see the surface, and Morax unearthed him, gave him sight and warned that he would be sealed again if he ever endangered Liyue's order. The sealing split the eroded dragon into a crazed body and a benevolent consciousness; the latter helped Morax seal the former. Jiu's anger at Morax's supposed betrayal drove the later attempt to break out. Zhongli noted that Dragonfall had been mined to obscurity centuries ago, so Kun Jun's interest in it was unusual for the present day.

Atmosphere: A still, cold place. The tree glows with a moonlit light, the earth around it feels thick with held-back power, and the monolith's plain warning is the only human sign. During the miners' disappearance, Geovishaps and other creatures nearby were unusually aggressive.

Dangers: The seal itself is the danger: if it breaks, Azhdaha can draw on the ley lines again and attack Liyue.

Travel: The tree stands in the Nantianmen area near Mt. Hulao, on the way toward Lingju Pass, and its tip branch points at Liyue Harbor.

Quests: No Mere Stone (Zhongli Story Quest, 1.5), whose final part is Amidst Chaos, the Rock Is Unmoved, is the main source. The domain unlocks on its completion.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the dragon remains resealed after the events of 1.5. No later content found in this research changes the seal's state.

70.content:
The Dragon-Queller is the blue-veined tree beside Mt. Hulao at Nantianmen that seals the crazed Geo dragon Azhdaha. A Mountain Shaper tablet at its foot warns people not to disturb the evil dragon beneath.

The seal was nearly broken in the Zhongli story quest No Mere Stone, when Jiu led missing miners to dig at it. Azhdaha was beaten and resealed.

71.content: The prison chamber under the Dragon-Queller, entered by a tunnel at the tree. It is a bed of rock carved into the heart of the world. The Trounce Domain relives Azhdaha's fight as a memory; in the story he has been resealed.

72.comment: Dragon-Queller: Azhdaha at the Moonchase Festival
72.content: During a flashback in the Moonchase Festival event, Azhdaha is shown gazing at the night sky with Marchosius riding on his shoulder. This is limited-time event content and does not show the Dragon-Queller.

73.content:
Dunyu Ruins (also: Dùnyù-líng, Fleeing Jade Mausoleum): The Dunyu Ruins are old ruins sunk in a dead lake in Lisha, a region of Liyue. They are hilltop terraces, stairways and a Statue of the Seven's camp, with a Geo totem that drains the lake, and one of three places where the quest item "Nameless Treasure" is hidden. Little is known of who built them.

A Treasure Hoarder's notes suggest the ruins are tied to adepti who died in an ancient war, but this is not confirmed.

Geography: Ruins on terraces around a lake in Lisha. Walls, stairs, Ruins Torches and rock piles are scattered between buildings. Activating the Geo totem after lighting torches drains the lake to reveal the Geoculus, a barrier guarded by three Seelie courts, and a chest with a Nameless Treasure. The expedition description says the ruins are suspended in time inside the dead lake.

Local specialty: Cor Lapis. The surrounding Lisha region also holds the Chasm entrance and Qingxu Pool, whose underground ruins hold another Nameless Treasure.

People: The astronomer Ziwei and the miner Iron Ingot are the named NPCs here. Treasure Hoarders and the Fatui roam the ruins.

History: Little is certain. The Treasure Hoarder Liuliu wrote in a Ruins Investigation Log that research suggested the ruins are linked to adepti who fought and died in an ancient war and that "treasure is hidden within the rocks, concealed beneath the waters". Liuliu also heard mournful groans at night, put down to the north wind blowing past Nantianmen.

Three Nameless Treasures (from Lingju Pass, Qingxu Pool and Dunyu Ruins) fit together into a single carved object. Linlang, an antiques dealer, reads it as the story of the dragon Azhdaha: three adepti, the Mountain Shaper (a crane) and Moon Carver (a deer) among them, created a cavern realm and sealed him inside. The third adeptus's image has been deliberately ground away. This does not prove the Dunyu Ruins belonged to that era.

Atmosphere: Still water over old stone, wind through broken arches, a camp near a statue, and the feeling of being watched that Liuliu wrote about; a place that rewards patience and a cool head.

Dangers: Fatui Skirmishers (Pyroslinger Bracer, Cryogunner and Hydrogunner Legionnaires, Anemoboxer and Electrohammer Vanguards), Treasure Hoarders, slimes, and elite Ruin Guards and Fatui Pyro Agents.

Quests: "Hidden in Nameless Treasures", a Hidden Exploration Objective whose items come from Lingju Pass, Qingxu Pool and these ruins.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins are a minor exploration site with no developing story.

74.content: Linlang tells the Traveler the three artefacts are old Liyue work and mentions that Soraya, a researcher, might be interested. She believes the full set tells how Azhdaha was lured into a cavern and sealed, and wonders who ground away the third adeptus's image, and why.

75.content:
Dwelling in the Clouds (also: Jadevoid): The Dwelling in the Clouds is a small floating island high above Qingyun Peak in Minlin, Liyue, built on a foundation of Plaustrite. It was made by the adeptus Cloud Retainer as a private place to meditate, and is reached by solving the Three Cranes Puzzle on the peak below.

Its memorial text, written in Cloud Retainer's voice, says it was meant as a sanctuary away from the world; the adepti later took it over to seek ultimate truth in seclusion and, with Taishan Mansion sealed, returned it to her.

Lore: Cloud Retainer built it long ago for meditation and reflection. Other adepti, with Rex Lapis' approval, later persuaded her to offer it as the site of the trial of "heaven" for those seeking the adepti's path, and she added a small pavilion. Its Plaustrite foundation and the trial of crossing the void to follow that path gave it the name "Jadevoid", a name that came to cover all places where the adepti reside.

Cloud Retainer left her blueprints for a manmade floating island at the Dwelling, hoping someone with a matching affinity would find them; when nobody did, she had the Traveler retrieve them in the quest An Adeptal Summons. Because few can now follow the adepti's path, the island is in her care again. Her note adds that she wants to go back into the world for a while, starting with Guili Plains, which she calls the Plains of Returning and Departing.

Zhongli visited the Dwelling in the Clouds on the fifth day after completing the quest The Stars Inscribe the Year's Wishes.

Travel: The island is unlocked by the Three Cranes Puzzle on Qingyun Peak, whose monument speaks of the one who may ascend kowtowing atop three mountains and of auspicious signs sent by three divine birds. Qingyun Peak is also home to the adeptus Moon Carver.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is a quiet retreat held by Cloud Retainer; no later events have changed it.

76.content:
Emerald Maple Inn: The Emerald Maple Inn stands west of the Statue of The Seven and overlooks Luhua Pool, in the Sea of Clouds area of Liyue. Its owner, Mr. Zhu, struggles to attract customers because of its remote location.

Mona used to be a regular before moving to Mondstadt, because the prices were low.

People: Mr. Zhu is the innkeeper and sells simple dishes and tea. He greets visitors warmly but is quickly drawn into complaining that he picked a bad spot: it lies between the Wangshu Inn and Liyue Harbor, so travellers from the north stop at the Wangshu Inn, while those coming from the south typically arrive only after drinking heavily in the Harbor. He says he wishes he had listened to his father and stayed home.

He says he will keep the inn going as long as he can, and will otherwise sell it for whatever it fetches. He also says he is not a top-tier talent and, if it comes to it, will return home and take over the three jade mining facilities his father left him. His signboard invites guests cordially to the Emerald Maple Inn.

In Mona's Astrolabos story quest, "Astrology and the 50-Year Pact", the Traveler and Paimon accompany Mona to say farewell to Mr. Zhu before she leaves Liyue, then help recover his lost nephrite ring from slimes. The detail that Mona frequented the inn comes from that quest context.

Status as of 7.1: Still open as of 7.1, as quiet as ever.

77.comment: Emerald Maple Inn: Mr. Zhu's luck
77.content: Mr. Zhu's running joke is that opening an inn here was a terrible idea. Play him as courteous but resigned, hopeful for any guest, and prone to a sigh when asked about business.

78.content:
Fanmu Carpenter (also: Fanmu Carpenter's): Fanmu Carpenter is a carpentry workshop in Qingce Village, owned by Master Lu. In the game he sells blueprints for furnishings.

He calls it one of the oldest carpentry workshops in the village. Its Chinese name is read Fanmu-tang.

History: By Master Lu's account the workshop began as the property of his grandfather's grandfather and has stayed in the family ever since. He says it built the residence of Chang the Ninth and the village mill, and that even the Qixing come to it when they need furniture made to order.

Master Lu says he is getting old and his joints suffer after a lifetime in the workshop, so he wants an apprentice to pass on the craft and secure the shop's future. If the player says they would like the job, he is doubtful because the player seems restless and travel-bound, and tells them to do what they must first and return later.

Dayu, a young but capable carpenter, is the official apprentice per the wiki: he had worked for the carpenter who built the stage for Yun Jin's premiere at the rebuilt Jade Chamber, which prepared him for Master Lu's first official job for him, rebuilding the stage of the Heyu Tea House. Master Lu also offers a Genius Invokation TCG match, a gameplay feature, and says playing cards is relaxing.

People: Master Lu is genial, proud of the family trade, and boasts that he can build anything from a yo-yo to a house. Dayu is the younger carpenter in his orbit.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

79.comment: Fanmu Carpenter: Master Lu and the apprenticeship
79.content: Master Lu wants an apprentice. He is warm and weary, speaks fondly of the family workshop, and will say anyone may come back and take up the craft if he is still around.

80.content:
Feiyun Slope: Feiyun Slope is Liyue Harbor's prosperous merchant district and the way into the city for anyone arriving by the main road from the north. It sits between Chihu Rock to the southeast and Yujing Terrace to the west, and climbs in tiers of boulevard, bookshops, teahouses and bank offices. Wealthy merchants, guild servants, clerks of the Ministry of Civil Affairs and foreign traders all do business here.

The in-game viewpoint text describes it as where merchants who have "made it" live in comfort and carefree prosperity, with lights that never go out. The Ministry of Civil Affairs, Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and the Snezhnayan Northland Bank all have premises on the slope.

Geography: Feiyun Slope is the centre of Liyue Harbor, connecting the other two districts. Visitors from the north road arrive through its entrance; from there a boulevard rises in levels. The northern wharf, with a Maritime Authority office, is at the lower edge, and the Northland Bank and Heyu Tea House are on the top level.

Wanwen Bookhouse is on a middle level. A distinct Snezhnayan merchant area lies near the entrance. A bridge links the slope to Chihu Rock, and a crossroads at its western end links to Yujing Terrace, the island with Bubu Pharmacy and the road toward the Guizhong Ballista.

Places: - Entrance: Baiju Guesthouse, Xigu Antiques, peddlers and the ship owner Bibo.
- Boulevard: Liuli Pavilion and Xinyue Kiosk (two eateries), Mingxing Jewelry, shops and the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.
- Ministry of Civil Affairs: the city's civil administration.
- Wanwen Bookhouse (middle level), Northland Bank and Heyu Tea House (top level).

- Wangsheng Funeral Parlor buries Liyue Harbor's dead and also performs funeral rites for adepti. Its current director is Hu Tao, with Zhongli as consultant and Ferrylady as undertaker.
- The Ministry of Civil Affairs answers to the Liyue Qixing, directing departments that run public safety, festival budgets and records, and calling on the Millelith as needed. Its staff here include the clerk Zhao and the soldier Jiayi.
- Northland Bank is the Snezhnayan bank's local branch, managed by Andrei with Ekaterina at the reception and guarded by Nadia and Vlad.
- Heyu Tea House is run by Fan Er'ye and features the storyteller Tea Master Liu Su.
- Wanwen Bookhouse is run by Jifang; Bolai owns Wanyou Boutique on the northern wharf.

A servant of the Feiyun Commerce Guild, Xu, stands near the Ministry. The Guild itself is the trading house of Xingqiu's family, which traces its roots to Yilong Wharf in Chenyu Vale; its silk, books and tea trade reaches as far as Sumeru. A merchant named Ixkotii appears on the boulevard after the quest Incandescent Ode of Resurrection.

People: Merchants such as Changshun and Bolai; shopkeepers Linlang and Xingxi; Jifang; Fan Er'ye; the fortune teller Qiming (at night); the undertaker Ferrylady; the Northland Bank staff; clerks and Millelith soldiers such as Cai Le, Cai Xun and Yicheng; and the foreign merchant Ivanovich.

Hu Tao is the 77th director of Wangsheng, and Zhongli works there as a consultant. Tea Master Liu Su tells stories at Heyu Tea House, and the Adventurers' Guild has a recruiter, Tiantian, on the boulevard.

Governance: The Ministry of Civil Affairs, an organ of the Liyue Qixing, administers the city from here. It watches for dangerous people through lists compiled by Yelan, issues bounties, seals dangerous areas such as the Chasm mines after an accident and organises the Lantern Rite budget and safety.

Millelith soldiers stand at the entrance, by the Ministry and along the boulevard. Foreign firms such as the Northland Bank operate here, and Snezhnaya's Fatui use the bank's branches abroad as bases.

Culture: Feiyun Slope shows Liyue's trading culture at its most prosperous: guild servants, shop owners, clerks, and foreign merchants, with opera and storytelling at Heyu Tea House and fine meals at Liuli Pavilion and Xinyue Kiosk.

The Ministry of Civil Affairs, based on the slope, plans the Lantern Rite's budget and fireworks.

Atmosphere: Lights that never go out, a steady hum of bargaining and a sense of ease. It feels richer and more orderly than Chihu Rock, with foreign merchants mingling among guild clerks and Millelith.

Dangers: Almost none physically. Social and political risks dominate: Fatui business at the Northland Bank, sharp contract terms, and the Millelith's suspicion of outsiders when security is tight (as during the Rite of Descension crisis).

Travel: The main road from the north ends at the district's entrance. From here a bridge leads to Chihu Rock and a crossroads to Yujing Terrace. A northern wharf with a Maritime Authority office lies along its edge.

Quests: - Of the Land Amidst Monoliths (Archon Quest, 1.0): the Traveler speaks to Linlang, Bolai and other locals before the Rite of Descension, and after fleeing the Millelith is told by Childe to go to the Northland Bank.
- A New Star Approaches (Archon Quest, 1.1): the Northland Bank is the scene of Zhongli's contract with Signora, and Wangsheng Funeral Parlor is where the Traveler asks after him.

The Ministry of Civil Affairs is also where the Qixing's civil staff, including the clerk Zhao, work.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Feiyun Slope remains Liyue Harbor's busiest commercial district. No content from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes it.

The Northland Bank still operates here, and the Qixing still govern through the Ministry of Civil Affairs. Hu Tao runs Wangsheng with Zhongli as consultant.

81.comment: Feiyun Slope: Ministry of Civil Affairs
81.content: A government body under the Liyue Qixing, headquartered in Liyue Harbor and made up of various departments. It handles intelligence and records, public safety on roads, villages and festivals, the Lantern Rite's budget and fireworks, and keeps watch lists that include dangerous individuals, among them the Traveler and some reclusive adepti. Yelan, officially in its employ, is in practice an intelligence agent who works closely with Ningguang. It sealed the Chasm mines after an accident.

82.content: Liyue Harbor's funeral parlor, which also conducts rites for adepti. Hu Tao is its 77th director and Zhongli its consultant; Ferrylady is the undertaker seen on the boulevard at night. The wiki notes that Wangsheng has ties to the Fatui; Childe says it ostensibly does not take on shady work such as assassination. During the Rite of Parting arrangements the Traveler asks Ferrylady where Zhongli has gone.

83.comment: Feiyun Slope: Northland Bank and the Gnosis
83.content: The Northland Bank is Snezhnaya's bank, with branches around the world that the Fatui sometimes use as bases. In the Liyue branch, on Feiyun Slope's top level, Childe sends the Traveler there to clear their name after the Rite of Descension, and after Osial's defeat the Traveler sees Zhongli hand his Gnosis to the Fatui Harbinger Signora under their "contract". Zhongli there reveals he is Rex Lapis, who has dwelt in the world for over six thousand years, and that he feigned death to test whether Liyue could manage without him. He calls the pact his "contract to end all contracts" and declines to say what the Cryo Archon gave in exchange.

84.content:
Fengtai General Goods: Fengtai General Goods is the general store of Yilong Wharf in Chenyu Vale, run by Fengtai. It stocks everyday items and local specialties, and sells commemorative jadeware.

It is open at all times of the day and its stock restocks at different intervals.

People: Fengtai welcomes customers with a cheerful pitch about everyday items and commemorative jade jewelry. He says there is a build-to-order jadeware service, but it requires a reservation and the time taken depends on the design's complexity. He believes that "you don't choose a piece of jade, it chooses you".

Fengtai trained under Deyin, a jade artisan of Qiaoying Village. Deyin told him that a carver must suffer no distraction, so in Chenyu Vale the selling and the making of jade are strictly separate. Deyin gives some of his jade works to Fengtai to sell on his behalf, which is why the shop stocks them.

Fengtai adds that there might be a hidden artisan in any house you pass, quietly shaping jade. He is the disciple who sells, not the carver.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

85.comment: Fengtai General Goods: Jade carving in Chenyu Vale
85.content: In Chenyu Vale makers and sellers are separate so craftsmen can focus on the work. Fengtai represents the selling side for his master.

key: The Ancient Battlefield of Fuao Vale
86.content:
Fuao Vale (also: Fu'ao Valley, The Ancient Battlefield of Fuao Vale): Fuao Vale is a surface subarea of the Chasm in Liyue. It contains the Lost Valley, a domain on ancient ritual grounds that Ruin Machines have taken over, and a viewpoint whose caption says the site was the battlefield where Rex Lapis fought Azhdaha.

A sign here warns visitors to treat a relic of those old battles, left by Rex Lapis, with care. The valley's Chinese name is usually glossed as Valley of the Prostrate Ao, the Ao being a legendary turtle.

Geography: Features: the Lost Valley domain entrance, Unique Rocks and Unique Rock Pillars, a Pressure Plate and a Mountainator blasting cannon. Cor Lapis, Qingxin and Violetgrass grow here.

The domain is revealed by placing Geo constructs between the golden Unique Rock and a rock pillar and striking the pillar so a resonant quake runs through the minerals. In the game this is a puzzle, not story.

History: The Lost Valley's description says the ritual grounds were buried beneath the earth during a cataclysm that tore heaven and earth apart, raised again when an alien object fell, and finally uncovered by a destructive battle that came of a betrayal. Those who once used the place are gone.

The linked wiki lore connects these events to the War of Funerary Flame, the Celestial Nail that struck the Chasm and Azhdaha's later clash with Morax. A world-quest viewpoint calls the vale the site of the deadly battle between Azhdaha and Rex Lapis, written by a young adventurer who says they are awed by it. Treat that as an in-world account, not a map of the whole story.

Chasm lore also holds that Azhdaha suffered when miners disturbed the ley lines, and that Morax, the adepti Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver and a third adeptus fought down to the Chasm's depths, creating the Dragonfall. Whether that fight began in Fuao Vale is not stated.

Quests: The viewpoint "The Ancient Battlefield of Fuao Vale" appears once the world quest Surreptitious Seven-Star Seal Sundering reaches about step 8.

Dangers: Enemies near the valley include Geo Samachurls, Anemo Slimes and Treasure Hoarder Scouts. Inside the Lost Valley domain, Ruin Machines have overrun the ritual site.

Atmosphere: A sunken battlefield valley of golden rock, silent ritual ground and warning notices, with a sense of awe at old divine violence. This is a suggested scene mood drawn from the viewpoint's wording.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1.

87.content: The Lost Valley is a Domain of Blessing in Fuao Vale that gives artifacts when cleared. In-world it is described as ancient ritual grounds buried in a cataclysm, lifted by the descent of an alien object, uncovered by the battle after a betrayal and now held by Ruin Machines from outside.

88.content:
Glaze Peak: Glaze Peak is a rocky subarea on the surface of the Chasm in Liyue. Spoutrocks, loose rock piles and tall unique rock pillars mark it, and its slopes hold Cor Lapis, Qingxin and Violetgrass.

The Chinese name is Liuli Peak.

Geography: Features are Rock Piles, Seelie, Spoutrocks, Unique Rocks and Unique Rock Pillars. Gatherable specialties are Cor Lapis, Qingxin and Violetgrass.

It belongs to the Chasm's surface, the wide whorl of rock above the mines that were closed after unexplained accidents and are being reopened by the Liyue Qixing. The wiki records no description or point of interest for the peak itself.

Glazed Sand Crystal, used to make porcelain, is named in the Chasm's lore as a Chasm specialty, but it is not listed among this peak's gatherables, so do not tie it to Glaze Peak.

History: Canon gives this peak no history of its own. Its setting is the Chasm, where before the War of Funerary Flame the ancient human civilisation of Lang-Gan lived, and where legends say a falling fragment and an Abyssal invasion later struck. See the Chasm entry for those accounts.

Dangers: A Stonehide Lawachurl is the elite enemy. Dendro Slimes and Treasure Hoarders (Hydro and Pyro Potioneers) roam as common foes.

Atmosphere: Open rock under a wide sky, with Seelie flickering among stone pillars and hoarders camped in the crevices. This is a suggested scene mood drawn from the feature list, not a quoted description.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1.

89.content:
Golden House (also: Liyue Mint, Teyvat Mint): The Golden House is Liyue's mint, and the only mint in Teyvat. Every Mora coin in circulation was struck here. It stands on Mt. Tianheng above Liyue Harbor. The Liyue Qixing run it, a steward manages it, and Millelith soldiers guard it. Minting needed the Geo Archon's power, so the mint has stood idle since Rex Lapis "died" and gave up his Gnosis. The Mora that already exists stays in circulation.

During the Liyue Archon Quest the Qixing hid Rex Lapis' body, the Exuvia, inside the Golden House. The Fatui Harbinger Childe broke in to take the Gnosis from it, fought the Traveler there and found the body empty.

Places: Inside, the building is even more lavish than its exterior and holds great piles of Mora. It has at least two levels: during the duel in Heart of Glaze, Childe smashed through the floor and the fight continued on the level below. The Exuvia was laid out in the hall where the duel began.

Guards stand at the entrance and turn away anyone without business there. To the steward, the vaults are "the source of all wealth" and the lifeblood of the economy. Locals call it simply the Liyue Mint, or even the Teyvat Mint.

People: Gongming is the steward. She is proud and wary, insists visitors state their business, and calls the place one of paramount importance to Liyue. The guards are Millelith soldiers, among them Youxu, Zexuan, Zhe'yuan and Zheng.

Youxu, younger brother of the Millelith instructor Fengyan, is eager for a chance to prove himself. After the break-in he is bitter that his unit had been redeployed into the city when the adepti came, so he missed the one real incident on his watch. Zexuan transferred to the post because he loved the clatter of coins being struck. He now misses that sound, although mountains of Mora still sit inside.

Governance: The mint belongs to the Liyue Qixing's administration. Before the Archon Quest, Gongming noticed that some of her recent orders from the Qixing went far beyond her usual authority. They were part of the measures the Qixing took after Rex Lapis' apparent death: the Exuvia was moved here, and Childe later said the Qixing had stopped the mints.

History: Mora is named after its creator, Morax, known in Liyue as Rex Lapis, and the Golden House struck it with his power. After his body fell at the Rite of Descension, the Qixing secretly moved the Exuvia here. Using what he learned from the preparations for the Rite of Parting, Childe found the hiding place. He knocked out the Millelith guards and was waiting by the body when the Traveler and Paimon arrived. Childe fought the Traveler, reached into the Exuvia and found no Gnosis in it. He assumed the Traveler had taken it, used his Foul Legacy transformation and smashed the fight down to the lower floor. He lost, realised the Exuvia had been a decoy, and left to carry out his backup plan: releasing Osial. Afterwards Zhongli revealed himself as the Geo Archon and gave the Gnosis to Signora for the Tsaritsa. At the Rite of Parting he told Paimon that existing Mora would not vanish, but the Golden House would have to cease operations for a long time.

Earlier in the same act, a coded notebook in the Jade Chamber, written as a book cipher keyed to Customs of Liyue, spelled out that the Fatui would strike the Golden House. After the break-in Gongming took inventory and found not a single Mora missing, which baffled her. Childe also used his Electro Delusion during the duel before the Foul Legacy transformation.

Childe accused the Traveler of either reaching the Gnosis first or deliberately leaking the Golden House's location to him. He later admitted they could have had no connection to the Gnosis and that Signora's report on them had underrated them.

Economy: In-world, Mora is the currency accepted throughout Teyvat. It is also a catalyst for physical transformation, which is why crafting and forging consume it. Since the Golden House was Teyvat's sole mint, its closure means no new coin enters circulation. Zhongli called this a serious financial problem and, characteristically, left it for the Qixing to debate.

Neuvillette once called Mora the "flesh and blood" of Morax. In Snezhnaya (7.1), Paimon asks whether Northland Bank or the Golden House holds more Mora. Vesna answers that she has never been to the Golden House, and adds that Northland Bank safeguards many other valuable assets besides Mora.

Atmosphere: The building is hushed and gleaming, full of gold and heaps of coin. Its guards are visibly anxious and admit they are on edge. Since the shutdown, the clatter of minting has stopped and only the stockpiles and sentries remain. One guard calls it, without exaggeration, the most important place in Liyue.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Golden House still stands under guard but does not mint Mora.

The Geo Gnosis went to the Tsaritsa through Signora, and no canon source up to 7.1 shows minting resuming or another way of minting being found.

90.comment: Golden House: The Duel in the Golden House
90.content:
Heart of Glaze is part 4 of the Archon Quest act A New Star Approaches (Chapter I, Act III). With Liyue Harbor in turmoil between the Qixing and the adepti, the Traveler realised that Childe had gone to the Golden House after the Exuvia. Inside, the Millelith guards lay unconscious and Childe was waiting by the body. He fought the Traveler for the pleasure of the fight. After reaching into the Exuvia and finding no Gnosis, he unleashed his Foul Legacy transformation, then lost and released the sealed god Osial on Liyue Harbor with mass-produced Sigils of Permission.

The Trounce Domain "Enter the Golden House" frames a rematch with Childe as the Traveler's memory of this duel ("Memories: The Golden Shadow"). It is a combat replay, not a new canon event.

91.comment: Golden House: Golden House in Genius Invokation
91.content: In the Genius Invokation TCG (added in 4.0), the Golden House location card says that all the contracts circulating through the land are forged there. This is a poetic in-world description of the mint and Mora, not a new fact about its function.

key: Plains of the Returning and Departing
92.content:
Guili Plains (also: Plains of Returning and Departing, Plains of the Returning and Departing, Ruins of Guili): The Guili Plains are a stretch of ruins and open country in the Qiongji Estuary area of Liyue. This was the centre of the Guili Assembly, an ancient realm ruled jointly by Guizhong, the God of Dust, and Morax, who is now Rex Lapis and lives incognito as Zhongli. About 3,700 years ago, during the Archon War, a great battle laid it waste and Guizhong died. Morax then led the survivors south of Mt. Tianheng to found Liyue Harbor. The plains are now a deserted wilderness of broken stone, frequented by hilichurls, Treasure Hoarders and the occasional scholar.

The name comes from the two gods: the "Gui" of Guizhong and a "Li" from the name Morax went by at the time. It is read as "the Plains of Returning and Departing." The ruins still hold stone tablets and jade plates inscribed in the Assembly's era, including Guizhong's Four Commandments.

Geography: The plains are a subarea of the Qiongji Estuary, the coastal country north of Mt. Tianheng and Liyue Harbor. The main road between Mondstadt and Liyue Harbor runs past them. To the north lie Wangshu Inn and the Dihua Marsh. The Conch Lodge country of Yaoguang Shoal is on the nearby coast, and Mingyun Village is further east. Violetgrass grows here.

At its height, the Guili Assembly reached far beyond the plains. Stone Tablet Compilations says its farming towns stretched so far that one could walk to Stone Gate without leaving the paths between the fields. The plains themselves are its old centre. During the limited-time Moonlight Merriment event (2.1), Keqing quotes an old text placing the Assembly "60 miles to the northwest", seemingly measured from Liyue Harbor.

Places: - **Ruins of Guili**: the scattered ruins of the old settlement, with a viewpoint looking over them. Five inscribed stone tablets (north, east, middle-south, southwest and west) and two more ruin inscriptions record the Assembly's founding and fall. Four jade plates in the northern, eastern, southern and western ruins each explain one of Guizhong's Four Commandments.
- **Domain of Forsaken Ruins**: a one-time domain hidden in the area. Its description calls it a cloud-wrapped paradise that one finds only by luck, serene outside and dangerous within.

- **Karma-Heavy Cavern**: a cavern in the plains that draws monsters corrupted by sinister energy. It is the quest domain of Xiao's story quest (1.3).
- A ruin guarded by a Ruin Guard holds a "wishing bonfire" bait, which leads into the world quest Share Not Your Treasures (see quests).
- A wooden house by the sea, home of Minamoto Kotomi, an elderly mother living alone (see people).

History: Stone Tablet Compilations: Vol. I, compiled by the historian Zichang from ancient tablets, tells the story. Guizhong, the Lord of Dust, was Rex Lapis' ally and built the Guizhong Ballista on Mt. Tianheng. She brought her people north of the mountain and taught them farming, and farming towns spread across the land. She told Rex Lapis that her people had left their home yet felt as though they had returned home. So she named the area the Plains of the Returning and Departing, and he praised her for it. In the Archon War the adepti fought to defend the plains, but the war ravaged them and Guizhong was killed. Rex Lapis then led the people south of Mt. Tianheng for good, and the plains became a wilderness.

The tablets in the ruins tell it differently. In their version the people gathered to farm, then Guizhong descended and gave them four commandments. Afterwards a Geo god descended, brought the people of Liyue to this place and shepherded them together with her. One fragment describes the final battle on the plains, "where black dust choked the heavens and a thousand rocks splintered." Madame Ping's tale of the Stove God, told during a limited-time event, adds a few details. People from the city had built a dwelling on the plains and named it the Guili Assembly. A flood then took it, and the survivors went south to Liyue Harbor. The journey was short, but a terrible storm lasted for a dozen days, and the adepti stayed with the people throughout.

The weapon text of Memory of Dust records how Guizhong died. Among the Glaze Lilies she told Morax that their journey together had ended, and asked him to forget the puzzle-dumbbell she had once given him as a pledge and challenge. Then her form dissolved into dust. Over the years the wild Glaze Lilies dwindled until none were left. The viewpoint text alludes to this when it remembers a thriving city "where a certain flower bloomed in abundance."

People: Nobody lives in the ruins proper. The scholar Soraya, a researcher from the Sumeru Akademiya, studies them and venerates Guizhong's memory. Bao'er poses here as an archaeologist digging on the battlefield where, she says, the Geo Lord won a decisive victory. In fact she is a Treasure Hoarder. Millelith soldiers, among them Fugui and Zhenxiang, guard the Mondstadt–Liyue Harbor road nearby. Fugui sits in the shade drinking tea and offering free face readings to passers-by.

Minamoto Kotomi, whose son wrote of the Sakura Blooms of "your homeland" (Inazuma), lives alone in a wooden house by the sea in the plains. Her son's last letter, recovered in Beidou's hangout, explains that he buried a check for all his savings so it would not be stolen from her house. Wiki listings of Guili Plains NPCs also include several people around the coast and the Sea of Clouds edge, such as Granny Chu and Miss Bu at the Conch Lodge and Mr. Zhu of the lonely Emerald Maple Inn. In the game's area divisions some of these are counted under neighbouring areas.

Culture: Guizhong's Four Commandments are the plains' lasting legacy: "Teach with wisdom, be bound by virtue, fortify the bones, unite in ambition." Their convergence was to be called the Guili Assembly. Soraya reads them as Guizhong's wish for her people to be wise, moral, strong and united in protecting their home.

The jade plates gloss each commandment. Unity of ambition means being steadfast and immovable. Wisdom is like water, nourishing everyone and reflecting the truth. Strengthened bones keep a body supple when the time comes. Virtue grows like a tree that flourishes even in shade. Someone who refused to leave the ruined land hid a treasure at the point where the four ruins "converge," so that later generations hunting for it would learn the commandments.

Atmosphere: Wind over grass and broken masonry, quiet except for hilichurl camps and the scrape of Treasure Hoarders' shovels. The ruins feel like a graveyard of a happier age. Most travellers only pass through on the road between Wangshu Inn and Liyue Harbor. Liyue folk still tell competing stories about what happened here.

Dangers: Hilichurl camps (including Mitachurls and Samachurls), slimes, Treasure Hoarders who dig in the ruins and set traps for treasure-seekers, Cryo Abyss Mages and dormant Ruin Guards around the old structures.

Ruin Guards stand watch over some of the old chambers; Treasure Lost, Treasure Found ends with a fight against three of them at the final ruin. (Separately, Guizhong is said to have collected Khaenri'ahn machines for study, though canon does not link those to these guards.) In Xiao's story quest, hilichurls tainted by his karmic debt gathered in the Karma-Heavy Cavern. In 5.7, Rifthounds were found here collecting god remains.

Travel: The plains sit beside the main road from Mondstadt to Liyue Harbor, south of Wangshu Inn and north of the harbour, so they are easy to reach on foot. The Millelith post on the road makes the highway itself relatively safe; the ruins away from it are not.

Quests: - Treasure Lost, Treasure Found (1.0 world quest): Soraya and the Traveler copy the ruin inscriptions, reconstruct the Assembly's story and follow the Four Commandments to a hidden treasure. Soraya concludes that the commandments are the real treasure.
- The Lost Relic / A Little Raid (commissions): Bao'er's "lost relic" errands, which expose her as a Treasure Hoarder.
- Share Not Your Treasures (1.0 world quest): a "wishing bonfire" turns out to be a Treasure Hoarder trap, and their notes point to loot buried on Cuijue Slope.

- Butterfly's Dream (Xiao, 1.3): the Traveler tracks corrupted hilichurls to the Karma-Heavy Cavern in the plains and meets Xiao there.
- Guili Plains Treasure Hunt (Beidou hangout, 2.3): Beidou and the Traveler follow a poem about "ruins long forsaken" to a sailor's hidden savings, and deliver his last wishes to his mother in the plains.
- Sinister Undercurrent and Special Training (Skirk, 5.7): after meeting the Traveler at Wanmin Restaurant, Skirk has them come to the plains, investigates there with them and then takes them through an Abyssal rift to train.
- Smaller content: the commission A Novel Idea (Chang the Ninth seeks inspiration here) and the Gliding Challenge event quest Fly High.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Guili Plains remain uninhabited ruins under Liyue's protection. Nothing of the Assembly survives except stones, inscriptions and memory.

Zhongli still lives in Liyue Harbor, and Guoba, the diminished Stove God Marchosius, lives with Xiangling. In 5.7, Skirk found that god remains sealed beneath the plains had been dug up and taken; Rifthounds were found there collecting remains. No later version reports further change here.

93.content: Guizhong's Four Commandments survive on the stones of the Guili Plains: teach with wisdom, be bound by virtue, fortify the bones, unite in ambition. Their convergence "shall be known as the Guili Assembly." A jade plate in each of four ruins (north, east, south, west) explains one commandment. Someone who stayed behind after the Assembly fell hid a treasure where the four meet, so that treasure-seekers would carry the words forward. Soraya and the Traveler recovered both in Treasure Lost, Treasure Found.

94.comment: Guili Plains: The Fall of the Guili Assembly
94.content:
About 3,700 years ago, in the Archon War, a battle on the Guili Plains destroyed the Assembly. The tablets recall black dust choking the heavens and a thousand rocks splintering.
