The adepti could not hold back the war, and Guizhong was killed. A flood followed, and Morax, Marchosius and the adepti led the survivors south of Mt. Tianheng through more than ten days of storm to found Liyue Harbor. Morax raised the Millelith there. The enemy in that battle is never named.

Folk explanations differ: a war between gods, a war between humans or a natural catastrophe. Soraya reasoned that, with two gods watching over it, whatever destroyed the Assembly must have been beyond even the gods' power to withstand. Bao'er's patter calls the plains the site of the Geo Lord's decisive victory, but she is a Treasure Hoarder posing as an archaeologist.

95.comment: Guili Plains: Soraya, Scholar of Guili
95.content: Soraya is a Sumeru Akademiya researcher who studies Liyue's history, especially Guizhong. She leaves the fieldwork in the Guili ruins to the Traveler and admits she tires after a few seconds of running. She despises Treasure Hoarders for selling relics. After the Four Commandments were recovered, she said that if she met Guizhong she would recite them perfectly, to show that the people had not forgotten.

96.comment: Guili Plains: Rifthounds and God Remains at Guili
96.content: In Skirk's story quest (5.7), the Traveler, whose soul had been partly stolen, met Skirk at Wanmin Restaurant and was told to find her on the Guili Plains. There Rifthounds were gathering god remains, the buried, curse-laden remnants of gods fallen thousands of years ago. Skirk found that some of the remains sealed in the plains had been dug up and removed. She linked this to a power-siphoning entity of at least god-level strength, which was also draining god remains in Sumeru's desert and Stella Fortuna in the sky. She opened an Abyssal rift there and took the Traveler to her own domain to train them.

97.comment: Guili Plains: Beidou's Guili Plains Treasure Hunt
97.content: In one branch of Beidou's hangout (2.3), Beidou bought a hard-to-read treasure map, and she and the Traveler searched the Guili Plains. They drove off digging Treasure Hoarders and recruited the Golden Alligator's gang. Then they decoded a poem about gazing at "ruins long forsaken" beneath a red-leaved tree at dusk. The treasure was a check for a sailor's savings, buried so it would be safe for his mother, Minamoto Kotomi, who lives alone by the sea in the plains; the Traveler calls it "the last will of a faithful son." In the "Sakura Blooms Upon Guili Fell" ending, Beidou sends the Traveler to take her the check and a Sakura Bloom from her homeland.

98.content: In Xiao's story quest Butterfly's Dream (1.3), hilichurls tainted by Xiao's karmic debt troubled the area around Wangshu Inn. A fraud named Starsnatcher failed to drive them off. The Traveler tracked the tainted hilichurls to a cavern in the Guili Plains, where Xiao, his body still burdened by karma, purged them.

99.comment: Guili Plains: Guili in Later Memory
99.content: Zichang, the historian who compiled Stone Tablet Compilations, preserved the Guili story for later readers. Jinggui, a Liyue warrioress now preserved among the "Uplifted" in the Temple of Space (seen in 6.5), recalls once driving bandits out of the Guili Plains alongside the swordsman Guhua. In a letter to the Traveler after her 6.3 debut, Zibai writes that she went to see where Liyue Harbor's people came from after the floods and found that the old traces had faded from sight.

100.content:
Guizhong Ballista (also: Obscuro Vulpes Mechanism): The Guizhong Ballista is a huge ancient crossbow on Mt. Tianheng in Liyue. The God of Dust, Guizhong, designed it with the adepti, Cloud Retainer among them, to defend Liyue against dangerous enemies. It can fire by itself at anything it sees as a threat.

Geography: It stands among old ruins at Mt. Tianheng in the Sea of Clouds, at the pass that the Guili Assembly once guarded. A supply post nearby holds spare parts. Structural pieces such as the beams and bow limbs are lacquered and folded away in a store room, and the fine parts (trigger, fasteners, fletchings, bowstring) sit in a separate container.

The machine fires autonomously at anything nearby it perceives as hostile, including Treasure Hoarders who approach the ruins.

Places: Supply post and maintenance notice: a notice outside the post explains that the Ballista is a work of divine conception made real by mortal craftsmen, and asks any future repairer to treat each part as their own body, in case an ancient evil returns to threaten the land.

History: Guizhong first designed the machine under the name Obscuro Vulpes Mechanism, and Rex Lapis judged it superior to Cloud Retainer's own mechanical creation. Guizhong and Cloud Retainer disagreed about ideals, but after Guizhong fell in the Archon War, Cloud Retainer finished the Ballista in her memory. It was built to defend against invaders from Tianheng Pass; the Guili Assembly moved its people north of the mountain.

The maintenance notice, left for the future, presumes that after centuries of peace someone with the right skill and character will be summoned to repair it, should the ancient evil return.

Guizhong's wider interest in machines is recorded in her biography: she apparently collected Khaenri'ahn machinery such as Ruin Machines for research. The Ballista is the work most linked to her name.

Atmosphere: A weathered siege-weapon slumbering over a quiet ruin. The wood is old and lacquered, and the notices left by its makers speak of duty and long peace.

Dangers: It can fire on intruders by itself. Treasure Hoarders have broken it before in order to reach treasure hidden in the ruins.

Travel: The site lies on Mt. Tianheng in the Sea of Clouds, Liyue. After the Cocogoat quest the Traveler returns here while looking for a way to reach the Jade Chamber.

Quests: Pursuing the legendary adeptibeast Cocogoat for Qiqi, the Traveler, Paimon and Zhongli arrive hoping to use the Ballista as a scanner. They find it broken, Zhongli repairs it with gathered maintenance parts, and the activation draws the ire of the Treasure Hoarders led by Freckle Huang, who had damaged it. The hoarders are driven off. Later the Ballista is found mysteriously repaired in a day, and the Millelith guard it while the Qixing investigate until Keqing intervenes in a dispute with Paimon.

In the Archon Quest, once Tartaglia has unleashed Osial to draw out Morax, Ningguang summons replica Ballistae at the Jade Chamber with Cloud Retainer's modifications. The Fatui attack them and Osial destroys them. Later, after Beidou warns Ningguang of Beisht, the Liyue Qixing build improved ballistae on a small southern island of Guyun Stone Forest, operated by Millelith under Keqing; they hurt Beisht severely and most survive the fight.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the original Ballista remains at Mt. Tianheng. The wiki records no change after Beisht's defeat, other than the presumed dismantling of the temporary copies.

101.content:
The Guizhong Ballista is the ancient autonomous crossbow on Mt. Tianheng, designed by Guizhong with the adepti and finished by Cloud Retainer after Guizhong's death. It exists to defend Liyue from the worst enemies.

Replica ballistae fought Osial at the Jade Chamber and Beisht at Guyun Stone Forest. The originals' maintenance notice asks for a skilled, devoted craftsman if war returns.

102.content:
Guyun Stone Forest (also: Guyun Tower): Guyun Stone Forest is an archipelago off Liyue's coast: seven large islands and smaller ones, crowded with jagged stone pillars that legend says are the remains of the lances Rex Lapis hurled to pin the sea god Osial to the ocean floor. People in Liyue say it is more a vista to behold than a place to visit. It holds the Domain of Guyun, a Geo Hypostasis on its northernmost island and, anchored off its shore, the Crux fleet's flagship Alcor.

The in-game text calls the pillars "proud, lonely stone mountains" and says that sensitive listeners sometimes hear a strange, stirring rhythm coming from the deep below. The expedition notes add that the forest is said to be a graveyard of the old gods. The Chinese name means "Lone Cloud Pavilion"; some English voice-over lines call it Guyun Tower.

Geography: Seven large islands and small offshoots in the sea off Liyue Harbor. The northernmost island houses the Geo Hypostasis and an island in the southwest the Domain of Guyun. Tall stone pillars rise from the islands. The shallow seas around them yield sea salt.

Hilichurls live on some of the small islands. Local specialties include Cor Lapis, Noctilucous Jade, Qingxin and Starconch. Roald, the adventurer, counted six giant stone pillars when he came ashore and found the shade cool and the beach crabs large. The Alcor is moored just off the islands.

Places: - The Geo Hypostasis' island in the north.
- The Domain of Guyun in the southwest, an altar of ley lines.
- The Alcor, flagship of the Crux fleet, anchored offshore.
- Ruin-treasure monuments on the southern islands.

A sequence of monuments on the southern islands tells the story of a disciple who trained from childhood to fight monsters and sought a Vision; the monuments at Guyun and Mt. Aocang belong together. At the smallest southern islands, Guizhong Ballistae were once installed to fight a sea monster.

People: The crew of the Alcor, including the chief mate Juza, the navigator Huixing, the ironworker Suling, the bookkeeper Mora-Grubber, the surgeon Yinxing, and sailors such as Furong, Xu Liushi and Sea Drake. Captain Beidou normally commands the ship but has often returned to Liyue Harbor, leaving it to her crew.

Hilichurls hold some of the small islands, and the adventurer Roald has visited. Keqing commanded Millelith here during the Beisht crisis.

Culture: Liyue folk treat Guyun as a place to look at rather than visit. The tale of Rex Lapis' victory over Osial and other sea monsters is a much-loved legend, and Liyue folk tell it in different versions.

Zhongli is said to recommend sea salt from the shallow seas of Guyun for cooking, according to Xiangling. Beidou recalls that one Lantern Rite eve, as her ship limped back to port in a storm, she looked toward Guyun Stone Forest and saw an adeptus floating in the air in the form of a young boy, and took it as proof that there are those who watch over Liyue.

History: Guyun is the battlefield where, about two thousand years ago in the Archon War, Rex Lapis defeated the god Osial, the Overlord of the Vortex, a sea monster who could raise waves as tall as Liyue's mountains. Rex Lapis pinned him to the sea floor with giant lances of stone, and the pillars are said to be what remains.

Liyue's sources differ on the detail: that he used the sacred lance Vortex Vanquisher to pierce the rainbow of Osial and nail him to the deep sea's centre; or that he carved a polearm out of the rocky land and drove it through the monster, and wind has since worn it into the pillars. Zhongli calls his conflict with Osial an old grudge, long gone.

Osial remained sealed for roughly two thousand years until Childe used Fatui-made Sigils of Permission in 1.1 to free him and lure out the Geo Archon. The Jade Chamber was dropped on him and he was resealed.

Atmosphere: Cool shade under towering pillars, sea wind and the sound of waves, with beaches below. Those who sleep here are said to dream of being the sea monster, pinned and furious.

Dangers: Hilichurls and shooters, Abyss mages, Fatui agents, Geovishap hatchlings, Ruin Guards, and the Geo Hypostasis. Osial's strength did not fade in two thousand years of imprisonment, so the seal over him matters.

Spending the night is considered a bad idea because of the nightmares of Osial's impaling.

Travel: Roald borrowed a boat to reach the islands; in practice they are reached by boat and by gliding between them. The Alcor lies just off the islands, and the Domain of Guyun is in the southwest.

Quests: - A New Star Approaches (Archon Quest, 1.1): Osial, freed by Childe, is fought at the Jade Chamber and resealed beneath the sea off Guyun.
- Where the Heart Finds Rest (Interlude Chapter, 2.4): Beisht, Osial's "wife", attacks, and Keqing commands ballistae here.

A world quest, A Lone Ship in Guyun, is triggered by boarding the Alcor.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Guyun Stone Forest is a silent archipelago with Osial resealed and the Alcor anchored offshore. No content from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes it.

Osial was resealed at the end of the 1.1 Archon Quest, and Beisht was driven off in the 2.4 Interlude.

103.comment: Guyun Stone Forest: Osial and Rex Lapis' Stone Spears
103.content: Osial, the Overlord of the Vortex, was a god and sea monster of the Archon War, strong enough to raise tsunamis tall as mountains. Rex Lapis defeated him at Guyun and pinned him with stone spears, which became the pillars of Guyun Stone Forest. In 1.1 Childe freed him with Fatui Sigils of Permission to lure out the Geo Archon; the adepti and Millelith fought him and Ningguang dropped the Jade Chamber on him. A fragment of the spear, a Monolith Fragment, was recovered afterwards. Osial's "wife" Beisht later sought revenge.

104.content: The Alcor is the flagship of the Crux fleet, anchored off Guyun Stone Forest. Beidou usually captains it but lately lets her crew run it. Boarding it begins a world quest, A Lone Ship in Guyun.

105.comment: Guyun Stone Forest: The Disciple's Monuments
105.content: At Guyun, monuments left by a disciple say he trained from childhood with a fellow disciple to fight evil, and that the two sought refuge here to train and to seek Visions. When the fellow disciple received a Vision, he asked whether monsters are truly evil by nature; the author answered that monsters wreak havoc and joked that too much meditation had addled him. He resolved to keep hunting monsters alone, even without a Vision. A matching series at Mt. Aocang is written by the other disciple, who received the Vision and began to doubt.

106.comment: Guyun Stone Forest: Beisht at Guyun
106.content: In 2.4, Beisht, who hated the Jade Chamber for defeating her husband Osial, was lured out to the waters off Guyun. Ningguang rebuilt the Jade Chamber, Beidou warned her of Beisht's presence, and Keqing led the Millelith at Guyun Stone Forest, where Guizhong Ballistae there and on the Alcor attacked Beisht. Shenhe leapt into the vortex after Beisht, and afterwards the fleet reported that the sea monster had left Guyun and the waters had returned to normal. Keqing said the Millelith's casualties were within the expected range.

107.content:
Hanfeng's Ironmongers (also: Hanfeng Ironware): Hanfeng's Ironmongers is a blacksmith in Liyue Harbor, marked on the map with a forging icon. It was founded by Hanfeng, nicknamed "Cold Blade", and is now run by his son, Master Zhang.

Its map description says Liyue has known the smithy for hundreds of years, that it is a favourite with the people of Liyue, and that with the right materials it never disappoints a customer. It quotes the saying "May the flames spread to all, and never be extinguished".

People: Master Zhang is the blacksmith; he sells basic weapons and will forge to order if the customer brings the right materials. He says repairs are free, and asks to be told whenever a customer finds good ore. Through repairing people's gear he has built up a network that feeds him tips about ore, including odd crystal ore veins he cannot yet work.

Hanfeng, the founder, has retired to Qingce Village, where he works the fields below his house. He misses his son and worries that he is devoted only to work; he even tries to matchmake the Traveler with him. He is also uncle to Suling. He says he built the business from nothing, that his body has grown too weak to lift a hammer, and that he still absentmindedly gathers iron chunks out of habit.

Hanfeng says his apprentices in the Harbor would have been the Traveler's age, and that he dislikes the Harbor's bustle. He asks the Traveler to tell his son that his father is safe and well.

Status as of 7.1: Open and operating as of 7.1.

108.comment: Hanfeng's Ironmongers: Master Zhang and Hanfeng
108.content: Hanfeng retired to Qingce Village, while his son, the blacksmith Master Zhang, runs the Liyue Harbor forge. They rarely meet and each worries about the other.

109.content:
Heyu Tea House (also: Heyu Teahouse): Heyu Tea House is a teahouse in the upper part of Liyue Harbor, on Feiyun Slope, just below the Northland Bank and the upstairs part of Xinyue Kiosk. Yun Jin and the Yun-Han Opera Troupe perform there. Its owner is Fan Er'ye, a retired opera star who bought the place with the wealth from his performing days.

Besides opera, the house has a storyteller, Tea Master Liu Su. Fan Er'ye is there at all hours and is passionate about the stories and shows on his stage.

Places: Fan Er'ye describes the house to the Traveler: the stage, the tables and chairs, private rooms upstairs, performers and kitchen staff. He says he made it what it is. The stage is the focus; the Yun-Han Opera Troupe performs there, and a storyteller tells tales for customers.

It stands in the upstairs region of Liyue Harbor, below the Northland Bank and beside the Xinyue Kiosk.

During the limited-time Lantern Rite event Fleeting Colors in Flight, Fan Er'ye says that every time he sees Miss Yun perform it reminds him of Ruoxin (event dialogue, not part of the permanent game).

People: Fan Er'ye is the boss. Tea Master Liu Su is the storyteller. Yun Jin directs the Yun-Han Opera Troupe, which performs here, and Changhu and Gentry Maocai are also seen there by day. Granny Ruoxin, now of Qingce Village, once performed at the house with Fan Er'ye.

By day Fan Er'ye is so absorbed in the storyteller that he shushes the Traveler until it ends; even news of Rex Lapis' death after the Rite of Descension is, at first, something he will worry about "after the story ends". He insists the Traveler call him simply Er'ye.  At night he welcomes visitors and talks about the house.

History: Ruoxin fell in love with an adventurer and planned to leave her luxurious life for Mt. Qingce. He left on an expedition and never came back, and she now lives in Qingce Village. Fan Er'ye wishes he had had the courage to tell her how he felt.

The Yun-Han Opera Troupe was established by the time of Yun Jin's grandfather. The troupe is associated with the Yun family, who once forged weapons and later turned to Liyue opera as a family tradition. Several of its veterans joined while her grandfather led it.

Culture: The teahouse is part of Liyue Harbor's opera and storytelling life: a place to watch Liyue opera, listen to a storyteller and drink tea in company.

Atmosphere: Audiences who stop talking to follow the performance, and a boss who shushes anyone who interrupts the story.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Heyu Tea House is open, with Fan Er'ye as owner and Yun Jin's troupe performing there.

Fan Er'ye can be found there at all times of the day, and his dialogue changes with the time. No change of ownership is recorded.

110.comment: Heyu Tea House: Fan Er'ye and Granny Ruoxin
110.content: Fan Er'ye, owner of Heyu Tea House, is a retired opera singer and actor of renown who performed with Ruoxin, now called Granny Ruoxin of Qingce Village. He admits he wishes he had told her how he felt. Ruoxin fell for an adventurer who never returned from an expedition.

111.content:
Hezhe Post (also: Hezhe Station): Hezhe Post is where the Communications Office conducts its business at Yilong Wharf in Chenyu Vale. It handles registration, inspection and shipping applications for people and goods entering, leaving or moving within Liyue.

The Communications Office is one of the Eight Trades under the Liyue Qixing, and specialises in transportation.

Practice: Fangju lists four main tasks of the post: registering people and goods entering and leaving; inspecting and, if necessary, quarantining them; taking applications for delivery inside Liyue's borders; and providing ad-hoc storage. Outlanders who want to do business in Liyue and arrive at the wharf register here, and staff inspect and disinfect their goods.

The post evaluates the quantity of goods and the distance to the destination, then sends manifests to transport units or to partners at the Secure Transport Agency, which do the actual hauling. It can store goods in a warehouse if no final destination is planned, and can act as proxy to apply for a business permit, although that is less efficient than applying in Liyue Harbor. Fangju says the wider Office also handles road, bridge, waterway and dock construction, and encourages visitors to consider working there; staff face monthly performance evaluations.

Lixing, who works for the Communications Office, evaluates and optimises transport plans for set routes. The Office cannot cover all of Liyue, so some work is outsourced to local Secure Transport Agencies, whose varied equipment makes timing hard to control; standardising it would need investment these small agencies cannot afford. Lixing is often found muttering about transfer points along the route from Lumidouce Harbor to Liyue Harbor.

People: Fangju and Lixing are Communications Office staff; Fangju is a steady, cautious clerk who describes himself as a lowly staff member and recommends the Ministry of Civil Affairs for more detail. Sai Jinzhuan also stands near the post and has idle lines about disobedient underlings.

Status as of 7.1: Open and active as of 7.1.

112.comment: Hezhe Post: Registering at Yilong Wharf
112.content: The post is the bureaucratic front door to Chenyu Vale for foreign merchants: register, be inspected, then choose delivery or storage.

113.content:
Hidden Palace of Guizang Formula (also: Guizang Formula Hidden Palace, Huaqing Guicang Hidden Palace): The Hidden Palace of Guizang Formula is a hidden treasure chamber under Luhua Pool, in the Qiongji Estuary of Liyue. From the surface it looks like an ordinary clear pond. Entry is sealed behind an old mechanism and a riddle-like inscription, and the palace holds two separate trials: "Voyage to the Sanguine Sky" and "Travels of the Moonlit Venturer".

It belongs to a trio of similarly named hidden palaces. The sister sites are the Hidden Palace of Lianshan Formula and the Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula. All three borrow their names from ancient divination systems, which is the only link between them that the game spells out. It is a one-time domain, so a traveller can clear each of its challenges for first-time rewards only once.

Geography: The entrance lies at Luhua Pool, a calm body of water in the Qiongji Estuary. A platform near the pool carries a circular mechanism. The game's description of the site stresses the contrast between the still surface and the hoard said to lie below, enough to drive a person mad, and adds that few who can decipher its secrets remain.

Tall unbroken stone pillars and broken ones stand around the platform, with Pyro monuments beneath them. This layout is the heart of the entry puzzle (see travel).

Atmosphere: Use it as a quiet, mildly eerie ruin: still water, weathered stone and an air of old secrets. The inscription at the mechanism says, in paraphrase, that anyone who follows in the footsteps of the immortals must kowtow before the treasure's gate. A wrong guess makes the puzzle reset, so a scene here rewards patience and observation more than force.

The original Chinese hint reads closer to "follow the traces of those who live forever, and knock on the door of the hidden chamber", which stresses retracing a path rather than simply bowing.

Travel: Activating the Pyro monuments that stand beneath the tall unbroken pillars, and only those, undoes the seal. Lighting a wrong monument resets the puzzle. Once the seal is broken the two domain entrances open.

The first challenge is recommended from adventurer rank 30 and the second from rank 35 (game progression requirements, not world lore).

History: Nothing in game text says who built the palace or why. The name echoes "Guicang", one of the ancient "Three Changes" divination texts of Chinese tradition, used here as a naming theme for three hidden palaces; this is an etymological note, not stated in-world history.

No character in the story discusses it, and it has no connection to a specific Archon Quest or named historical figure.

Quests: No story quest takes place here. Unlocking it grants an achievement named after the palace. The two inner domains are optional gameplay challenges.

The sister palaces (Lianshan Formula and Zhou Formula) use the same naming theme. The Guizang palace's two trials are linked to adventurer ranks 30 and 35, so it sits among the early-to-mid game exploration rewards. The Traveler and Paimon have no recorded in-world reaction beyond puzzling out the mechanism.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, unchanged since its addition in 1.0. It does not figure in the Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content.

114.comment: Hidden Palace of Guizang Formula: Guizang Formula challenges
114.content: The two trials inside the Hidden Palace of Guizang Formula are "Voyage to the Sanguine Sky" and "Travels of the Moonlit Venturer". They are combat challenges that pay out treasure on first clear; treat them as self-contained trials with no recorded in-world story.

115.content:
Hidden Palace of Lianshan Formula (also: Lianshan Formula): The Hidden Palace of Lianshan Formula is a Domain of Forgery near Mingyun Village in Liyue, a thundering ancient sacrificial altar full of Electro slimes that rewards weapon ascension materials. Its description says the Lianshan Formula once raised endless storms inside the mountain, and that the rumbling outside the gate calls curious souls.

Its name is one of three "Hidden Palace of [Name] Formula" places, taken from the old Chinese divination arts Guicang, Lianshan and Zhou Yi (the Three Changes). Tradition, relayed by Lan Yan in the limited event Springtime Charms, says the Two Sages of Lianshan, two of the legendary Eight Adepts, used a hidden palace in the mountains south of Stone Gate as a place of retreat. The wiki ties that to this domain; the quest itself says only that it is the traditional belief.

The Two Sages practised the secret art of Lianshan and preferred to live in seclusion; very little else survives about them. The mainstream account holds that they were human, not adepti, and so likely died long ago.

The domain's rules, as gameplay detail: Adventure Rank 15 to 40 and recommended levels 15, 36, 59 and 80 for its four levels. Enemies are Electro Slimes (including Large and Mutant), then a Fatui Electro Cicin Mage at level III and two at level IV, with time limits from 360 to 480 seconds.

Geography: The entrance sits near Mingyun Village in Qiongji Estuary, within Liyue. Thunder can be heard outside the gate. Inside, huge Electro energy courses through the altar, and dispersed Electro constantly drains Energy from anyone there.

Dangers: Gameplay rules, labelled as such: every party member gains 75% Cryo DMG (levels I to IV), with Cryo the recommended element; the enemies are Electro-based. Level names (Thundercloud, Thundering Ruins, Trial Grounds of Thunder) fit the storm theme.

Rewards depend on the weekday: Monday gives the Guyun Pillar series (Luminous Sands, Lustrous Stone, Relic and Divine Body from Guyun), Tuesday the Mist Veiled Elixir series, and Wednesday the Aerosiderite series.

Atmosphere: Heavy, dry air, storm light flashing in ancient stone halls, and thunder like a pulse in the walls.

Status as of 7.1: Permanent and unchanged as of Version 7.1.

116.comment: Hidden Palace of Lianshan Formula: Two Sages of Lianshan
116.content:
In the limited event Springtime Charms (Version 5.3), the Two Sages of Lianshan are named as two of the Eight Adepts (with the Three Hermits of Guicang and the Three Beasts of Tao Dou). The mainstream story says the Guicang Hermits and Lianshan Sages were human. A hidden palace in the mountains south of Stone Gate is traditionally believed to have been their cultivation retreat.

Keqing notes that little survives about them besides the secret art they practised. Do not give them personalities, names or events beyond this.

117.content:
Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula (also: Zhou Formula Hidden Palace): The Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula is a Domain of Blessing on Wuwang Hill, in the Bishui Plain of Liyue. Its entrance text says a secret ritual that hides one gate out of eight, cutting off the route by which evil could escape, was performed here long ago and sealed demons inside this labyrinth. Rumor says the method of fitting pillars with Zhou Formula still seals an evil chi. Today it is a Hydro-themed trial where Artifacts are earned by defending a ley line monolith from Pyro-empowered monsters.

Its name is one of three "Hidden Palace of [Name] Formula" domains, drawn from the old Chinese divination arts Guicang, Lianshan and Zhou Yi (the Three Changes). It is the one whose English name does not match its Chinese name, which means roughly "Hidden Palace that Assumes Responsibility for Wuwang", a reference to the formulas used to seal the serpent at Wuwang Hill.

Wuwang Hill's own reputation supplies the mood. The sky above it stays dull grey day and night, blue ghost lights drift through the forest, and Liyue folk treat it as a place for tests of courage. The Records of Jueyun explain "Wuwang" as meaning prudence, and the hill as the place where even the prudent are punished.

The Hydro bonus here is a gameplay echo of the story: the monsters fight with Pyro, which Hydro quenches, and the domain's own text tells the player to use Hydro against their "raging blaze". Recommended element Hydro; Adventure Rank 30 to 45; recommended levels 59, 69, 80 and 90 across four levels. Issue 2 of the in-game Teyvat Times named the first-tier Frost II trial (the old name of Roaring Fire) as the one travellers most often failed.

Geography: The domain stands at the top of Wuwang Hill, a subarea of the Bishui Plain in Liyue, on the hill that rises near Qingce Village. A large rock initially blocks the entrance, as at Cecilia Garden. To open it a traveller lights four ruins torches around the hill (one beside the Geo Monument, one inside a wind barrier, one at a hilichurl camp up the slope, and one north-east of that camp, where a Pyro Abyss Mage appears) and then activates the Geo Monument. Once it is open, the Electro cicins that wandered the area no longer appear.

Near the hill's top peak a pool is ringed with statues and an incomplete inscription about a being whose bones, spirit, form and soul were wrecked while its flesh survived, with a statue left "to watch in each direction": the wind-swept ruin, the snow-capped peak, the adepti's abode and the city of Liyue. Four statues, facing Stormterror's Lair, Dragonspine, Mt. Aocang and Liyue Harbor respectively, solve it. The text echoes how the Chi was divided and pinned in Qingce, but canon does not state that it concerns this domain's seal.

History: The domain's description is the only direct account: a secret ritual that conceals one gate of eight was carried out here long ago and sealed demons in the labyrinth, and rumor says an evil chi is held by the method of fitting pillars with Zhou Formula. Nobody is named as the performer.

The ritual closely resembles the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method of Liyue lore, a secret art for suppressing evil spirits and even gods by using eight key nodes of the ley lines, closing one gate so evil cannot escape. In this lore the Gate of Death currently lies at Wuwang Hill. That identification comes from the Springtime Charms event material, not from the domain text.

Mortal history here is recent and bleak. In the Springtime Charms story a few months before the event, fetor was found leaking across the boundary between life and death near Wuwang Hill, and the Ministry of Civil Affairs, with Hu Tao of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, set out to redo that boundary with the Art of Homa carried by the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method. Hu Tao herself held the Gate of Death. Separately, the Wuwang Hill Disaster over a decade earlier, in which Hu Tao's father failed to complete a similar rite and died of fetor while a flood devastated a nearby village, is why the hill has been fog-bound since. These are limited-event revelations.

People: No one lives in the domain. The Wuwang Hill area has been avoided since the disaster, and local folk tales (told by children of Qingce Village) say a sea monster once lured the young people of Wuwang away with a whale-like song and drowned them, until only elders were left.

Records of Jueyun adds that the ley lines recorded the hopes and dreams of those who died and recreated them from elemental energy, which can trap travellers much as it trapped the old villagers. Treat this as an in-world legend.

Dangers: Gameplay rules, labelled as such: the ley line disorder gives every party member a 75% Hydro DMG bonus at all four levels, and levels III and IV also grant a Hydro DMG bonus. The enemies are Pyro slimes, hilichurl fighters and berserkers, Blazing Axe Mitachurls, Dendro Samachurls and a Pyro Abyss Mage. At levels II to IV an elemental node empowers enemies with Pyro or Electro until the buff is removed by reactions such as Vaporize.

Rewards are Artifacts from Crimson Witch of Flames, Lavawalker, Defender's Will and Martial Artist. The first stage is a defend-the-monolith fight against 20 Pyro slimes; the later stages are timed, with limits from 60 to 360 seconds.

Atmosphere: Low grey sky, drifting blue ghost lights, thin fog on the hillside, and the heat of Pyro monsters against the damp of Hydro. It feels like a place where something is both held down and watched.

Quests: The domain is unlocked by the open-world puzzle on Wuwang Hill (light four torches, then the Geo Monument), and is also the subject of an achievement of the same name. It features in the lore of the limited-time event Springtime Charms only through the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method, not as a location.

Status as of 7.1: Permanent and unchanged as of Version 7.1. The Frost trials were renamed "Roaring Fire" in Version 4.8.

118.comment: Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula: Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method
118.content:
A secret Liyue art that suppresses evil spirits and even gods by activating an array across eight key nodes of the ley lines, each overseen by one person. The array master conceals one gate, erasing themselves from the ley lines, so that the remaining seven stand and evil cannot flee. Its best-known use is the Eight Adepts' sanctification of the god Tao Dou. The domain's own text describes a similar ritual at Wuwang Hill, but names no performer.

In Springtime Charms the gates were assigned: Life (Keqing), Death (Hu Tao, concealed), Repose (Qiqi and Baizhu), Concealment (Ganyu), Initiation (Ningguang and Lan Yan), Terrain (Xiao), Fright (Beidou and the Crux) and Injury (Yelan). The Gate of Death lies at Wuwang Hill.

119.comment: Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula: Chi of Qingce
119.content: A serpent god (also called Qingce in the ancient tongue) who nested where Qingce Village stands and was defeated by Morax; its spirit, bones, flesh, soul and form were each bound in a different direction to keep its power down. The domain text speaks only of "an evil chi" sealed by Zhou Formula, so do not assume it is this same being; the two stories rhyme but canon does not link them.

120.content:
Huaguang Stone Forest (also: Mist-Veiled Stone Forest): The Huaguang Stone Forest is a landscape of tall karst stone spires rising out of the clouds in Minlin, Liyue, hemmed in by three mountains: Mt. Aocang to the north, Qingyun Peak to the east and Mt. Hulao to the southwest. The in-game viewpoint says the place is forbidden to mortal steps and the kind of sight that draws those who yearn for the sky and who dwell in adepti realms.

It has no teleport waypoints of its own; travelers use those of the surrounding mountains. Two disciples of the declining Guhua Clan are found here searching for the adepti.

Geography: A subarea of Minlin whose pillars of rock stand like great pavilions above the clouds. Mt. Aocang lies north, Qingyun Peak east and Mt. Hulao southwest; the nearby waypoints on those mountains are the easiest way in. Local specialties include Cor Lapis, Jueyun Chili, Qingxin and Violetgrass.

The Chinese name Huaguang-lin is rendered by the wiki as "Brilliant Light Forest". The developers' travel-themed documentary credited by the wiki says the landscape took inspiration from Zhangjiajie National Forest Park in China.

People: Sun Yu and Little Que'er, disciples of the Guhua Clan, are found here for a time. Sun Yu has come to practise and, more importantly, to find the adepti and seek their counsel on how to revive the clan; Que'er accompanies him. Que'er is fiercely suspicious of strangers who approach, at first taking the Traveler for a mountain monster in disguise.

Per the wiki, Sun Yu later decides that staying in Liyue will not revive the Guhua Clan and leaves for Fontaine with a Fontainian merchant, after a later quest in which the Traveler trains with him. Que'er is distressed that he will not stay. The wiki flags both NPC pages as missing official profile text, so treat these details as quest-derived.

Dangers: Slimes of several elements, a Cryo Whopperflower and Geovishap Hatchlings.

Quests: No major story content is set here. The wiki lists the commission The Sparrow Studies the Blade for the area, and Sun Yu's presence here ends after a later quest named The Day the Sword Departs.

Atmosphere: Mist and cloud around bare stone towers, with the sense of being close to places where adepti dwell and mortals are not welcome. The few people who come here come to ask something of the adepti.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the forest is unchanged. The disciples' departure is the only story development tied to it, and no later content was found that alters it.

Places: The three surrounding mountains hold the waypoints: Mt. Aocang, Qingyun Peak and Mt. Hulao.

The official viewpoint for the area, "Mist-Veiled Stone Forest", is the source of the line about the spires poking out of the clouds like pavilions. The forest sits beside Mt. Hulao, whose adeptus Mountain Shaper keeps amber-trap flowers on his own mountain, but the stone forest itself has no recorded owner.

121.comment: Huaguang Stone Forest: The Guhua Disciples of Huaguang
121.content: Sun Yu and Little Que'er grew up together studying the Guhua Clan's martial arts. Sun Yu, devoted to the clan and eager to revive it, searches for an adeptus to advise him; Que'er follows him everywhere. Both are minor open-world NPCs. The Guhua Clan's base is Wangshan Hall on Mt. Lingmeng.

122.content:
Inverted City (also: The Inverted City, Upside-down city, Inverted Ancient City, Inverted Fountain, Diāndǎo Gǔchéng): The Inverted City is a ruin deep beneath the Chasm in Liyue: an ancient city whose buildings and a water pool hang upside down from the cavern ceiling. It is what remains of Lang-Gan, a city of Teyvat's unified civilisation governed by Zibai, after the Abyss tainted it and a Celestial Nail fell. The pool seems to soften the curse of immortality laid on the Khaenri'ahns.

It was sealed behind a purple barrier until the Traveler and Dainsleif reached it in Archon Quest Chapter II, where hilichurls came to live out their last days, the Black Serpent Knights stood guard, and the Abyss Order tried to turn the pool to its own purpose.

Geography: The city lies in the Nameless Ruins of the Chasm's Underground Mines, hanging above the cave floor with its terraces facing downward. Its crown is the upside-down water pool, with an altar-like structure and statues around it. Climbing the structure leads to the summit chamber.

Strange devices stand around the pool; the Abyss Order's amplifier was built into them. Statues near the pool look like those in front of the Dainichi Mikoshi in Inazuma (the wiki notes this without saying whether it is meaningful).

History: Before Khaenri'ah, this was a city governed by Zibai under Celestia's gaze. After the war of funerary flame the city was corrupted by the Abyss and a Celestial Nail sent to purify it landed on it, burying Lang-Gan and creating the Chasm. The ruin stayed buried and dark for thousands of years.

In "Requiem of the Echoing Depths" (2.6) Dainsleif noticed that hilichurls in the Chasm seemed to be gathering to die, because the environment eased the curse; he judged the city to belong to a civilisation older than Khaenri'ah. His former subordinates, now cursed Black Serpent Knights, guarded the dying hilichurls. In a vision at a hilichurl camp the Traveler saw their Sibling and an Abyss Herald discussing a plan to amplify the pool's properties and lift the curse from the gathered hilichurls. The amplifier's activation caused agony before the Traveler broke it, and the Black Serpent Knight Halfdan gave his life to hold it back.

The 2.6 quests never name the city. The identification with Lang-Gan comes from the 6.3 Lantern Rite story (see the Lang-Gan entry), and Zibai's role as the city's guide was only revealed then.

Atmosphere: Cold stone and inverted architecture, with the unsettling feel of a city seen in a mirror. Light drips down from the pool above; the air is hushed, with the heavy calm that makes tormented people want to lie down and rest.

Dangers: Ruin Guards, Abyss mages, Black Serpent Knights and Shadowy Husks in the surrounding ruins; the area was long sealed by a barrier.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the amplifier is destroyed, Halfdan is dead, and the pool remains a quiet relic. The Chasm itself is being reopened by the Qixing.

123.comment: Inverted City: The inverted pool and Dainsleif's curse
123.content: Dainsleif says the pool's cleansing quality eases the curse on Khaenri'ahns, on which he has been suffering for five centuries, but the effect could at most suppress it for a time. A true cleansing would cost the sufferer their life, since a god's curse acts on a deeper level of reality than the person.

124.content:
Jade Chamber (also: Ningguang's floating palace): The Jade Chamber is a palace that floats in the sky above Liyue Harbor. It is the home and office of Ningguang, the Tianquan of the Liyue Qixing. She paid an astronomical sum for Plaustrite, a stone that can levitate, to build it, and from it she keeps watch over Liyue's commerce and affairs. Being invited up to the Jade Chamber is the greatest honour among Liyue's merchants. In the Archon Quest Ningguang sacrificed it to crush the ancient god Osial. She later rebuilt it, and the new Chamber floats over the harbor again.

Its map description calls it a symbol of Ningguang's might and of Liyue Harbor's unyielding will. The Chinese name means "Chamber of Many Jades".

Places: Decks outside the palace gates look out over almost all of Liyue Harbor on a clear day. The main hall holds Ningguang's desk and her famous intelligence wall. This wall is covered in shipping schedules, profit-and-loss accounts, warehouse inventories, road-safety reports and diplomatic intelligence, all kept up to date. Visitors are carried up on a specially carved Plaustrite platform run by the guide Bu'yun.

Items on her desk include a scale engraved with words that call contract the unchanging bedrock on which Mt. Tianheng stands. The shelves hold an aquamarine porcelain vase inscribed "From The Crux", and her scrolls are written on paper as thin as insect wings. In the rebuilt Chamber a pot holds a very old piece of Plaustrite and a scarred green plant, which seems to have come from the first Chamber.

People: Ningguang does business here and allows only her three trusted confidants into the working rooms. These are the secretaries Baiwen, Baixiao and Baishi, who sort intelligence and pin summaries to the wall. Zhenhai serves as a guard. Guests come by invitation, and in the Archon Quest Ganyu delivered the Traveler's invitation for Ningguang.

In her character story, Ningguang leans on the railing looking over Liyue while her confidants fill the wall. She reaches her decision before they finish, shreds the papers and throws them out of the window. Merchants below read the falling scraps, her "snow", as a sign that big changes are coming to the business world. Once, a Sumeru alchemist who stumbled on records of an old noctilucous jade deal was invited up that same night for a talk.

Governance: The Chamber is Ningguang's personal property, not a Qixing office, but she runs much of her Tianquan work from it. The Qixing are said to monitor all of Liyue's goings-on from it. Liyue folk believe "Ningguang knows everything". Her real network is the harbor's children, whom she rewards with treats, and she checks their reports against other sources.

Rumour claims she has enchanted the Chamber to eavesdrop on private conversations across the city. Her character story presents this as rumour; the children are the truth.

History: The Traveler first came to the Jade Chamber at Ningguang's invitation in A New Star Approaches. Keqing told them the way up and the password: "Excuse me, do you sell the moon here?" Ningguang received their gift, talked about gods, archons and the Fatui, and a clue on her wall led to evidence that the Fatui were copying Sigils of Permission. When Childe released Osial, the Qixing and the adepti gathered on the Chamber. They fought from Guizhong Ballistae that Ningguang had replicated, manned by Cloud Retainer, Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver. Osial destroyed the ballistae. Ningguang then sacrificed the Chamber, which the Traveler helped send down onto the god, crushing him into the sea. She bid it farewell as an old friend and promised to meet again.

In The Crane Returns on the Wind (Interlude Chapter Act I, 2.4), Ningguang held a public contest for the rebuilding materials. She promised to answer honestly any one question from the first three people to supply them. The Traveler, Shenhe, Yun Jin and Beidou won. Shenhe hauled a huge piece of Sunset Vermillionite out of the adeptus Sea Gazer's abode. Master Zhang forged the Wonder Cores from Starsplinter Iron and Subrosium, and Shenhe made the Adepti Sigils that Cloud Retainer had sent her to provide. Ningguang had sped up the rebuilding to lure out Beisht, about whom Beidou had warned her, and was ready to sacrifice the Chamber again. This time Liyue's people fought instead of the adepti. The Chamber fired on Beisht, supported by Keqing, Ganyu, the Millelith and Beidou's fleet. Shenhe froze Beisht's tidal wave, the Chamber fired on her again, and the Traveler and Shenhe followed her into the vortex and defeated her. Ningguang then held a victory banquet on the Chamber, where Yun Jin performed "The Divine Damsel of Devastation".

Before Turning Point, a coded notebook in the first Chamber spelled out "The Fatui will strike the Golden House". Its numbers formed a book cipher keyed to Customs of Liyue: Receiving God, which lay on Ningguang's desk. Between the two Chambers, the Ministry of Civil Affairs cleared the larger wreckage from the harbor, and the Millelith soldier Kun enlisted the Traveler to fish out the smaller flotsam (Fishing For Jade). Baiwen later began preparing the reconstruction. She was looking for a rare book, "Meadow of Gems", and bamboo ornaments for the interior (Return of the Jade Chamber?).

Functionality: The Chamber floats on a great core of Sunset Vermillionite, the name for especially large pieces of Vermillionite, a variety of Plaustrite. Plaustrite has to be activated before it floats; until then it weighs about as much as ordinary stone. The Chamber is steered from a control compartment, where Wonder Cores combined with Adepti Sigils act as its control centre. In the battle with Beisht, Ningguang fired projectiles at her from the Chamber.

Ningguang explained that the Chamber beat Osial through both its tremendous weight and the energy stored inside it. The weight struck the god with enormous force, and the energy set off the explosion. Every stone, beam and ornament added to that weight.

Culture: To the merchants of Liyue, being received in the Jade Chamber is the highest honour, and visitors bring rich gifts to win Ningguang's favour. Her schedule is booked far ahead. Ningguang's ambition reaches well beyond Liyue. She has said the Chamber began as a single room and now clouds Liyue, and she hopes one day it will hang above all seven nations and cast its shadow across Teyvat.

Ningguang has told the Traveler that a carefully made home reminds her of the effort she put into the Chamber, and called it the Traveler's own "Jade Chamber". She invites them back for the finest tea.

Atmosphere: High above the harbor, the Chamber is lavish and orderly. Its intelligence wall is crowded with pages and its open decks look down on the whole of Liyue Harbor. Ningguang's paper "snow" drifts down from it onto the city.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the rebuilt Jade Chamber floats above Liyue Harbor again as Ningguang's residence and office, and visitors can be ferried up to it.

It is the second Jade Chamber. Some items from the first one's collection were never recovered.

125.comment: Jade Chamber: The Fall of the First Jade Chamber
125.content: In Turning Point (Chapter I, Act III) the Qixing and the adepti set aside their quarrel on the Jade Chamber to fight Osial, who had been released by Childe's Sigils of Permission. The Fatui sent soldiers through portals to wreck the ballistae; Keqing led the Millelith, and Xiao, Ganyu and Madame Ping blessed the Traveler. The adepti's combined shot failed and Osial smashed the ballistae and their platform. Ganyu insisted that the Chamber was their last line of defence and they could not give another inch; Ningguang answered that she would sacrifice it, and the Traveler drove a sword into it to send it crashing onto Osial.

126.comment: Jade Chamber: The Lost Jade Chamber Collection
126.content: When the first Chamber fell, much of Ningguang's collection sank into the sea near Guyun Stone Forest. She organised salvage, but many pieces passed into merchants' hands. In her hangout, The Jade Chamber's Returning Guest, she staged an auction so that she could identify and reclaim them. She admitted that she simply wanted her things back.

127.comment: Jade Chamber: Salvaging the Jade Chamber's Treasures
127.content: During the 2.4 Fleeting Colors in Flight event, the Traveler sailed Waveriders off Guyun Stone Forest to salvage the scattered flotsam and fought off Treasure Hoarders who were stealing pieces of it. This was a limited-time event, so not every Traveler will have taken part.

128.comment: Jade Chamber: Beisht and the Second Jade Chamber
128.content: In The Crane Returns on the Wind, Ningguang rebuilt the Chamber with materials gathered through a public contest, lured Beisht, Osial's wife, and fought her with the people of Liyue rather than the adepti. Cloud Retainer praised the Qixing's preparation as considerable progress since the Osial crisis, while noting Shenhe's important part in the victory.

129.content:
Jade Mystery (also: The Jade Mystery, Jiecui Hang): The Jade Mystery is a jade shop in Liyue Harbor run by the cheerful boss Shitou. Its Chinese name is read Jiecui-hang, roughly "the store that reveals jadeite".

Shitou sells ores, cut stones and uncut rocks that customers can gamble on, in the hope of finding valuable jade inside.

Practice: Shitou says the shop takes pride in generations of experience crafting jade finery and has quite a reputation in Liyue. The shop sells pieces cut from raw stone, though not exactly rare jade, and its stock refreshes every few days. He greets customers by telling them they look radiant and must be lucky today.

Shitou says business has slowed because the Ministry of Civil Affairs shut down the Chasm, cutting off supplies, so raw materials are now worth more than the finished goods. So he decided to sell the uncut rocks and let customers bet on them. In the daily commission "Diamond in the Rough...", the Traveler picks stones for him in a gambling game.

After Rex Lapis' death, Shitou muses on renaming the type of Noctilucous Jade used in the Rite of Parting in his memory, and cannot decide between "Parting Jade" and "Ascending Jade".

People: Shitou is the boss, bright and persuasive, and enjoys a card game with customers.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

130.comment: Jade Mystery: Shitou and Rex Lapis
130.content: Shitou comments on Rex Lapis' death after the Archon Quest chapter "The Fond Farewell": he hopes for the best for the Archon but says people must keep living, and wants to rename the jade used in the ceremony in his honour.

131.content:
Jademouth: Jademouth is a stretch of the Bishui River in Chenyu Vale, Liyue, flanked by enormous pieces of jade. Legend says an adeptus cast the jade down to protect the people of the vale from flooding.

Geography: Huge blocks of jade stand on both sides of the Bishui River in the upper part of Chenyu Vale. It is a subarea of the Upper Vale. The Version 4.4 preview text, in verse, refers to spring cries rippling through the vale, shrines leaving the northeast shores, and a whirlpool that never churns, with beautiful jade concealed within.

The preview verse is not a map description; it is a poetic lead-in for the new region and should not be used as a literal guide.

History: Legend says an adeptus cast the jade down to protect the people from flooding. Chenyu Vale lore, as cited by the wiki, ties this to the Archon War: the mistress of Chenyu Vale was at war with Morax and, near the end, loosed a flood along the Bishui River that would have drowned the vale. Her three adepti, the Herblord, Lingyuan and Fujin, rebelled; Fujin threw the Votive Rainjade into the water and so made Jademouth.

Afterwards the Herblord was greatly weakened, Fujin lost much of her power and sank into the sea, and the mistress was said to be sealed beneath Chenyu Vale beside the ruins of the lunar chariot. All of this is told through legend and book text, not through a first-hand witness.

The wider Chenyu legend of a jade slab that could summon sweet rain and was thrown into a river, probably the source of the name Chenyu ("Jade-Sinking"), is told in several incompatible ways, so Jademouth's origin should be treated as a story with variants.

Atmosphere: Cool green stone beside moving water, in a vale of tea terraces and mist. The place feels like a shrine to an old rescue.

Quests: No Jademouth-specific quest was identified in the pages read. The related story is in the Chenyu Vale region quests of Version 4.4.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1 in the sources read. The source material on this landmark is thin; this entry is short on purpose.

132.content:
Jademouth is the jade-flanked stretch of the Bishui River in Chenyu Vale. Legend says an adeptus threw the jade down to protect people from flooding; lore texts attribute it to Fujin and the Votive Rainjade.

It belongs to the story of the Chenyu mistress's last flood during the Archon War, in which her adepti turned on her to save the vale.

133.content:
Jiulue Teahouse: The Jiulue Teahouse is a teahouse in Yilong Wharf, owned by Baishu. It has a stage for performances and an outdoor dining area, and the indoor dining area, private seats and rooms are temporarily under renovation.

Its Chinese name is Jiulue Chaguan. It is decorated for the Lantern Rite festival in the Springtime Charms event.

People: Baishu is the boss, an expansive businessman who trades on good wishes and flattery. He is also behind many of the nearby inns. Quezhi is the waitress who offers a choice of tea with a performance or a quick work meal; Jiewu is the storyteller. Regular customers include the tea merchants Jiuguan and Fryslan and, at night, Lixing of the Communications Office.

Quezhi proudly lists the Yauwan and Sunglo teas Chenyu Vale is famous for, in every grade, plus export-quality Tianheng Bohea, Yunlai White Tea and Bishui Green Tea, which are popular in Liyue Harbor. Jiewu tells short tales about visitors, such as a Fontaine merchant who misjudged rinse water for fine tea and a Mondstadt poet in a wine contest, and promises to discuss storytelling craft in the evening.

Baishu says he started as an ordinary tea farmer who grew mediocre tea; Master Jiuguan's inspiration and the upgrade from tea cauldrons to machinery in Chenyu Vale let him build funds early, start a teahouse, and expand into inns and restaurants. He wants to support his former colleagues with money and publicity and to help more business people.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

134.content: Baishu went from tea farmer to owner of a teahouse, nearby inns and restaurants, and credits Master Jiuguan and the mechanisation of tea-making for his luck.

135.content:
Jueyun Karst (also: Jueyun Jian, Jueyun): Jueyun Karst is a realm of towering, cloud-ringed sandstone peaks in Minlin, northwestern Liyue, where the adepti, the immortal illuminated beasts who fought for Rex Lapis, have lived in seclusion since the Archon War. Mortals consider it sacred and seldom enter, though the brave or desperate still climb in search of adeptal blessings. Its great peaks each belong to an adeptus: Qingyun Peak to Moon Carver, Mt. Hulao to Mountain Shaper and Mt. Aocang to Cloud Retainer.

The Chinese name means roughly "Cloud-Terminating Place", for peaks that rise above the clouds. On maps "Jueyun Karst" also names one particular stretch of Minlin around the sunken Taishan Mansion, but people in Liyue use it for the whole adeptal highland.

Geography: Steep karst pillars and mountains wrapped in mist, with waterfalls and lakes. The map subarea lies between Taishan Mansion and Guili Plains. Around it rise Qingyun Peak, Mt. Aocang and Mt. Hulao, which ring the Huaguang Stone Forest. Wangshu Inn offers the classic distant view.

Nantianmen, where the Dragon-Queller tree holds the sealed dragon Azhdaha, lies further northwest in Minlin. Local products include Qingxin flowers, Cor Lapis and Jueyun Chilis, with Violetgrass in the stone forest. A plaustrite island, the Dwelling in the Clouds, floats high above Qingyun Peak.

The landscape was modelled on China's Zhangjiajie; the developers added trestle and suspension bridges between the mountains.

Places: Qingyun Peak (Moon Carver), Mt. Hulao (Mountain Shaper, guarded by amber-making "karst crawler" plants) and Mt. Aocang (Cloud Retainer, whose abode is reached from a stone table in a lake) each hide a sealed abode. Taishan Mansion is an ancient trial site, now flooded and sealed.

Mt. Aocang's table has three stone chairs engraved for Retainer, Guizhong and Rex. Moon Carver's abode lies past a censer at the foot of Qingyun Peak's steps. The Dwelling in the Clouds is Cloud Retainer's floating retreat. Huaguang Stone Forest is the valley of stone spires between the three peaks.

Inscriptions dot the area: a poem on the bridge over the Jueyun Karst lake and a tablet on the road to Qingyun Peak praise climbing above the clouds. A Qingyun Peak tablet calls Moon Carver Rex Lapis' disciple and the kindest adeptus, appearing as a stag. One on Mt. Aocang calls Cloud Retainer free and unfettered, acting without setting rules. Mt. Hulao's says Mountain Shaper builds his amber prison by harnessing nature.

People: The resident adepti are Moon Carver (a stag), Mountain Shaper (a red-and-orange crane) and Cloud Retainer (a crane, also called Xianyun). Mortals also come: herb gatherers who earn a living from plants found only here, chili pickers, pilgrims seeking blessings, Guhua Clan disciples in the stone forest, and Treasure Hoarders. Cloud Retainer has raised disciples in these mountains, including Ganyu in her youth and Shenhe, who arrived as a silent girl and became her student.

Named mortals include Qilang, an herb gatherer at Qingyun Peak who sells to Bubu Pharmacy; Manie, who picks Jueyun Chilis to cook for "the kids"; and Xin Cheng, a pilgrim who once demanded a blessing from Ganyu. Yuandai, a wild crane from Mt. Aocang that gained sentience, was taught by Cloud Retainer, though not formally as her disciple.

Culture: Liyue folk regard Jueyun Karst as sacred land that mortals should not enter. Entering without offending the adepti is said to be possible only for someone holding a Sigil of Permission, a talisman Rex Lapis once cast. Visitors leave food offerings, especially at Mt. Aocang's stone table.

An old warning in the Void-Pacing Stone Catalog says the wise never climb a mountain that has a master or quarry its rocks. Legend says seekers of the adeptal path had to pass trials of "earth" at Taishan Mansion and of "heaven" at the Dwelling in the Clouds. The heavenly trial gave rise to the word "Jadevoid", now used for any adeptus' dwelling.

When the Traveler met him, Mountain Shaper dismissed their guess about the amber as nonsense and explained that Mt. Hulao's amber comes from karst crawlers, flowers he planted to keep intruders out.

History: After the Archon War some two thousand years ago, most adepti withdrew to Jueyun Karst and watched over Liyue from afar. Cloud Retainer remembers the peaks ringing with music when the adepti gathered; now they are quiet, since most of her old friends died in the wars.

Some illuminated beasts are said to have asked Rex Lapis to turn them into stone statues instead of waiting for death. A tablet above Taishan Mansion says it was founded by royal decree. Rex Lapis chose to live among his people instead, so the way there was hidden and its treasure drowned. The Dwelling in the Clouds served the trial of heaven with Rex Lapis' approval and, with few seekers left, is back in Cloud Retainer's care.

Several hundred years ago the young herb gatherer Qiqi was caught in a battle between adepti and demons. The adepti revived her, and Mountain Shaper sealed her in amber when the power drove her wild.

Atmosphere: Silence, wind and birdsong; mist sliding between stone pillars; stone stairs, bridges, censers and offering tables high above the clouds. It feels watched and slightly forbidding, and a mortal can never be sure whether a nearby crane or stag is an ordinary animal.

Dangers: Sheer cliffs; hilichurl camps, slimes, whopperflowers and Treasure Hoarders; Geovishaps around Mt. Aocang; and Mountain Shaper's amber traps on Mt. Hulao, which seal anyone who steps on the hidden plants. The adepti dislike intruders and may treat them as thieves.

Travel: No road leads to the abodes. Each one is sealed by a barrier and opens only to those its adeptus admits, such as visitors whose offering is accepted. A Liyue portable cooking stove is advertised as ideal for scaling the heights of Jueyun Karst.

Quests: - Of the Land Amidst Monoliths (Archon Quest Chapter I Act I, 1.0): after Rex Lapis' apparent death, the Traveler seeks the adepti here to clear their name.
- Sea of Clouds, Sea of People (Ganyu's story quest, 1.2): Ganyu retreats to Mt. Aocang and trains to reclaim her adeptal side.

Lantern Rite events (4.4, 5.3, 6.3) move the adepti between the peaks and Liyue Harbor. The Taishan Mansion puzzle drains the water to unlock the domain.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Jueyun Karst remains the secluded home of the adepti and is still treated by mortals as sacred ground. Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper still keep their peaks.

Cloud Retainer moved to Liyue Harbor in human form as Xianyun before the 4.4 Lantern Rite but still keeps her abode on Mt. Aocang. The 7.0-7.1 Archon Quest takes place in Snezhnaya and shows no new events here.

136.comment: Jueyun Karst: The Traveler Seeks the Adepti
136.content:
After Rex Lapis was apparently killed at the Rite of Descension, the Traveler was accused. Childe of the Fatui gave them a Sigil of Permission and sent them to Jueyun Karst to win the adepti's word. At Qingyun Peak, Moon Carver met them and asked them to drive off the pursuing Millelith. Learning of Rex Lapis' death enraged him, and he sent them to the other adepti. On Mt. Hulao, the Traveler freed a man's brother from amber, and Mountain Shaper scolded them for helping a "thief". On Mt. Aocang, they offered dishes at the stone table and made their way through Cloud Retainer's abode. She spoke of quashing Liyue, but because they came bearing a Sigil of Permission and appealing to contracts, she agreed to investigate first. Xiao was found at Wangshu Inn.

The sigil Childe gave was a Fatui copy, not one of Rex Lapis' originals; such copies were later used to free Osial. The adepti then came down to confront the Qixing, fought Osial alongside the Millelith, and agreed to let mortals govern Liyue.

137.comment: Jueyun Karst: Rex Lapis' Survival and the Adepti
137.content: Rex Lapis was not dead: he had faked his death to step down, and lives in Liyue Harbor as Zhongli. The adepti accepted this, and at later Lantern Rites Moon Carver, Mountain Shaper, Cloud Retainer and Madame Ping have met him socially, at times on Mt. Aocang.

key: Illuminated Beast of the Sea of Clouds
138.comment: Jueyun Karst: Ganyu's Retreat to Jueyun
138.content: Ganyu, sent to deliver a letter from the Qixing to the adepti, lingered in Jueyun Karst. Seeing Ningguang's secretaries doing her work, she wrongly believed she had been replaced, and she doubted whether a half-qilin belonged among humans. At her request Cloud Retainer set her a trial near Mt. Aocang, and Xiao trained her at Nantianmen. A pilgrim, Xin Cheng, sought a materialistic blessing, which she refused. Back in the harbor, helping the official Huixin, whose family had looked up to her for generations, made her realise people valued her, and she resolved to keep working with the Qixing.

139.comment: Jueyun Karst: Jadevoid and the Trials of Heaven and Earth
139.content: Those seeking the adeptal path once faced two trials: "earth" at Taishan Mansion and "heaven" at the Dwelling in the Clouds, a plaustrite island above Qingyun Peak. Cloud Retainer built the Dwelling for meditation and lent it for the trial at Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper's urging, with the blessing of Rex Lapis, Guizhong and Streetward Rambler. The trial of crossing the void gave the name "Jadevoid", later applied to every adeptus' abode. Taishan Mansion is now sealed under water and has become a common treasure trove, its old altar now coursing with scorching Pyro energy.

140.comment: Jueyun Karst: The Mint on Mt. Aocang
140.content: During the 6.3 Lantern Rite event, a spirit called Zizhi possessed Mountain Shaper and sent him to plant masses of mint around Cloud Retainer's abode. He declared that once he had planted ten thousand, the peak would become "Mt. Mint-cang". The adepti blocked Zizhi's escape routes while the Traveler confronted him and dealt with her. Freed, Mountain Shaper admired the seedlings, assumed the Traveler had planted them and invited them to his garden on Mt. Hulao, until told the truth; Cloud Retainer then gave him a stern scolding.

141.content:
Karma-Heavy Cavern (also: Cavern of Karma): The Karma-Heavy Cavern is a cave in Guili Plains, Liyue, that draws creatures twisted by sinister energy. It is the setting of "The Purging of Evil", a Xiao story quest, in which the adeptus Xiao and the Traveler clear it of tainted hilichurls.

It is a quest domain, not a standing location: it is entered through the quest and used for one fight, not for exploration or trade.

Geography: The cavern sits in the Guili Plains region of the Qiongji Estuary. The quest begins with the Traveler tracking tainted hilichurls across the plains with Elemental Sight, and the trail leads to the cave. Platforms inside are cleared one after another.

"Karma-heavy" is how the quest and Xiao describe the place, not a name used by locals.

Atmosphere: Oppressive and unnatural: Paimon says it gives her goosebumps. Xiao tells his companions to stay calm and not to be affected by the lingering wrath of bygone gods.

Dangers: Hilichurls and creatures corrupted by an evil aura fill the cave. Xiao uses a rite called the Bane of All Evil to relieve the place of its karma. In gameplay terms (a game mechanic, not lore), the party is Xiao alone, and his Elemental Burst stays active, constantly draining his health while hits restore it.

In the story the creatures' mutation comes from Xiao himself, or more precisely from the karma he has accumulated through long service. This is why he first tries to go alone.

Quests: In "The Purging of Evil" (part 3 of Butterfly's Dream) Xiao is found having already slain tainted hilichurls. He admits his karma caused the changes and declines company, then lets the Traveler and Paimon come along. After the fight he learns about "Starsnatcher", a masked man posing as a wish-granting adeptus who exorcises demons with a Sigil of Permission without destroying them. Xiao concludes that this is why demons gather here and resolves to confiscate the sigil.

He explains that his art Dream Trawler can call forth the spirits of others, and asks the Traveler to gather a censer, seven lamps and something cold such as Mist Flower, suggesting the old shrines by the yaksha statues on the southern face of Mt. Tianheng. The story continues in later parts of the chapter.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing has changed. The cavern does not appear in Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content.

What Xiao says here is also a rare moment of openness: he dismisses a book about yakshas as literati fan fiction from a few hundred years ago and rejects sympathy, saying fallen comrades would see tears as a stain on their legacy. He distinguishes demons, whom he slays, from mortals, whom he does not kill.

142.comment: Karma-Heavy Cavern: Karma-Heavy Cavern and Xiao
142.content: In the Karma-Heavy Cavern Xiao purifies living things that carry demonic taint sourced from his own karma. He accepts suffering as the price of ages of slaughter, but says others should not suffer for a burden that ought to be his alone; he resolves to reflect on this.

143.content:
Lang-Gan (also: Langgan, Lánggān, ancient nation of Lang-Gan, Lang-Gan civilisation): Lang-Gan was a great nation of Teyvat's unified civilisation, on what is now the western coast of Liyue. Its people lived by the mines and were guided by Zibai, an angel who served Celestia as a Moon Envoy and whom they worshipped as a god of soil and grain. In the war of funerary flame the Abyss tainted it, and Celestia sent a Celestial Nail to purify it. Zibai died holding the Nail back so that her people could flee, and the impact made the Chasm.

The Inverted City and Nameless Ruins under the Chasm are what is left. Some survivors went east and founded Chenyu Vale, taking their old rites; Zibai was later remembered in Liyue as the White Horse Adeptus.

Geography: A coastal nation whose settlements ran from peak to peak across the crystal-veined mountains where the Chasm now yawns. Wiki-cited texts say it was a great and lovely land, made to bless the children of humanity. A weapon legend places it on the western coast before Mt. Tianheng rose.

The same legend says the Celestial Nail left "chasms deep as the whale dives". The nail itself is the Spiritstone, still visible in the Chasm's depths.

People: The Lang-Gan people mined jade and ore, and their lives and families revolved around the mines. Zibai taught them silk painting, farming, spinning and weaving. At the dawn of the nation she gave the longbow Yayu to the high priest, which gave him the right to lead as emperor. The people had no books; they kept history in ballads that poetry collectors later wrote down for the court.

Chenyu Vale families such as those of Yelan and Lan Yan descend from refugees who fled the Chasm. The elders of Qiaoying say the vale's ancestors came from a chasm to the south.

Culture: Lang-Gan honoured the Three Moons, and above all Zibai, at a finely carved jade altar, with offerings and sacrifices. Its people held the Three Moons in awe along with other civilisations of the Moon era such as Hyperborea, Arcadia, Sal Vindagnyr and Meropis. In memory visions, Lang-Gan's people released lanterns at the altar when a Trilunar Syzygy filled the sky.

Item texts imagine roasted millet and boar offerings and earthen drums. In the Lanternlit story Zhongli muses that some of Lang-Gan's jade may have become part of the foundations of Liyue Harbor; this is speculation, not a stated fact.

Governance: A priest-emperor ruled under Zibai's guidance; Zibai herself was the divine envoy of Celestia and the people's patron deity.

History: After the Eternal and Iridescent Moons shattered in the war of funerary flame, Abyssal corruption tainted Lang-Gan. The Heavenly Principles answered by sending Celestial Nails to heal the land. Istaroth advised Zibai to let it fall, but she refused to abandon her people, held the Nail back for a time at the cost of her life, and let the inhabitants flee. Istaroth preserved her soul, splitting it into the Three Deadly Selves. The refugees travelled east.

Some survivors settled in Chenyu Vale, carrying their jade altar, rites and the memory of the Chasm; the vale's murals at Chizhang Wall show their departure under a Celestial Nail. The Nail ultimately created the Chasm and buried Lang-Gan under the hills.

Millennia later, Liyue folklore turned Zibai into the White Horse Adeptus of the Eight Adepts. In the Lanternlit story the Traveler and Zhongli reunited the pieces of her soul, and Zibai was brought back. In the Archon Quest of 2.6 Dainsleif had already recognised the Inverted City as the work of an older civilisation, without knowing it was Lang-Gan.

Atmosphere: Memory of Lang-Gan comes as moonlight on jade: lanterns on a terrace, silver light over mountains, an unhurried people trusting their patron. Today it is a hush under the Chasm, a lost city glimpsed upside down.

Dangers: The ruins are under the Chasm's Underground Mines, with Abyss Order agents, Ruin Guards and corrupted mines. Nothing remains of the nation as a place to visit.

Travel: Not directly reachable; one sees its remains through the Inverted City and the Nameless Ruins in the Chasm.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Lang-Gan is a buried ruin and a memory; its descendants live in Chenyu Vale and beyond, and Zibai has been restored.

144.content: This account comes from the "A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon" story (Lantern Rite 2026, 6.3, since kept as a story quest), shown as a memory by Zizhi, the wrathful fragment of Zibai's soul. A Celestial Nail appeared in the sky over Lang-Gan. Istaroth told Zibai that everything tainted by the Abyss must be purified, Lang-Gan included, that this was heaven's will and that she was only an emissary; Zibai answered that her people honoured and prayed to her and that she would die among them rather than live with the guilt. Her Jadelight Canopy halted the Nail's descent for a time and the people fled. She fell and Istaroth caught her, splitting her soul into the Three Deadly Selves; the survivors looked up at the one remaining moon. Zizhi says the tainted remnants of the war falling from the sky devastated Lang-Gan and that the descendants of Lang-Gan made their home throughout Liyue.

145.content: Zibai is a Geo-wielding former angel and Moon Envoy who governed Lang-Gan and later became one of the Eight Adepts of Liyue. She taught Lang-Gan its crafts, was called the God of Soil and Grain, and gave the first emperor the Yayu bow. See her character entry for personality and later life.

146.comment: Lang-Gan: Lang-Gan's descendants in Chenyu Vale
146.content: Elders of Qiaoying say their ancestors came from a chasm to the south; Lan Yan says in a Chenyu Vale quest that her ancestors lived near the Chasm before moving. The Votive Rainjade rite, the Chiwang altar and the murals of Chizhang Wall carry their memory. Their old religion was lost; later generations accepted Rex Lapis's rule and became part of Liyue's people.

147.content: The name matches an ancient Chinese word, lánggān (琅玕), for a precious gemstone variously identified with blue-green malachite, coral, chalcedony, red spinel or red jade, which fits a nation tied to jade.

148.content:
Lianfang Dim Sum: Lianfang Dim Sum is a shop in Yilong Wharf run by Lianfang. It sells local food, cooking ingredients and recipes, and is open at all times of the day.

Its stock includes tea eggs, a tea brew, smoked squab and, per the wiki, recipes for them; Lianfang pitches them as simple, convenient foods you can even eat on board a ship.

Philosophy: Lianfang explains that Chenyu Vale's traditional dining is leisurely: sitting by the water with a pot of tea and a few dishes, drinking, enjoying the view and composing poems. But Yilong Wharf is a commercial port whose visitors want working meals they can finish quickly, so she adapts traditional dishes to suit them.

Her plan is to win visitors over with convenient local food and then guide them toward the unhurried, proper way of eating, promoting traditional cuisine as commerce grows. She says a chef named Baatjan improved the dishes with supplemental ingredients that ease seasickness while keeping their original taste, so some regulars buy snacks before boarding.

The wiki notes that the shop lacks the map marker of the General Goods shops.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

149.comment: Lianfang Dim Sum: Lianfang's working meals
149.content: Lianfang is proud of Chenyu Vale's leisurely dining traditions yet pragmatic about commercial reality.

150.content:
Lingju Pass: Lingju Pass is a mountain pass in Lisha, Liyue, made up mostly of old ruins and puzzle mechanisms. Legend says the ruins were once a stronghold of the Geo Archon Morax where mortals and adepti fought side by side, and a sign in the pass carries an anonymous poem about a divine order. The name is usually read as "divine law".

The pass hides one of the three Nameless Treasures that tell of the sealing of the Geo dragon Azhdaha, and a one-time domain lies close by.

Geography: A subarea of Lisha with ruins, a lake with a floating platform, and Geo-controlled puzzle monuments. The one-time Domain of the Wayward Path lies between Lingju Pass and Mt. Tianheng. Local specialties are Cor Lapis and Violetgrass.

Elite foes listed for the area include Ruin Guards, Blazing Axe Mitachurls and Abyss mages of several elements, alongside Fatui skirmishers.

Places: The ruined stronghold; a signboard bearing a poem (see history); the lake and its floating platform; the Domain of the Wayward Path nearby.

The lake puzzle uses four Geo monuments, each unlocked a different way: the northern one is free, the southern needs nearby Boom Blossoms triggered, the western needs two pressure plates, and the eastern needs an Anemo pinwheel. Completing them raises a wind current that lets the player glide to a fifth monument on a floating platform and open chests.

History: The wiki records a legend that Morax built the ruins as a stronghold where mortals and adepti fought together, and vague tales of Morax's divine law, lingju, which may connect to the poem on the sign. The poem reads, in summary, that a divine order governs the world, that everyone must die whether noble or wicked, rich or poor, and that the creator shows favour to none, so the faithful praise the divine rule in song.

Because the puzzle at Qingxu Pool says its ruins date from the Archon War, the wiki suggests Lingju Pass probably does too; this is an inference. A Nameless Treasure found here bears a pattern of the three adepti who helped Rex Lapis seal Azhdaha; Linlang identifies two of them as Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver, and the third has been deliberately ground away.
