Monuments at Guyun Stone Forest record the other disciple's view.

206.comment: Mt. Aocang: Yuandai and the Suspensus Somnium Mechanism
206.content: In A Thousand Moonlit Miles, Yuandai, an elderly woman suffering dementia, proves to have been a wild crane that gained sentience and was taken in by Cloud Retainer. Cloud Retainer prepared a ten-year potion of human mimicry for her. She fell in love with an exorcist from Mt. Tianheng, stayed with him after it lapsed and later lost her memory. Seeing Mt. Aocang frightens her; at the abode the Suspensus Somnium Mechanism helps her relive her memories, and she recognises Cloud Retainer. She reverts to a crane, without sentience. Her granddaughter Shuyu becomes Xianyun's first mortal disciple.

207.comment: Mt. Aocang: Lantern Rite Visits to Mt. Aocang
207.content: During 4.4's Lantern Rite event, Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper, who had taken human forms (Houzhang and Jiehu), flew a Fontainian motor kite near Mt. Aocang and lost it; Xianyun, who was running a kite workshop, caught it. In 5.3's event, Zhongli, Xianyun, Madame Ping, Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver talked here about a resolved fetor problem and Hu Tao, the director of Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. In 6.3's event, Zizhi possessed Mountain Shaper and sent him to plant mint on Mt. Aocang, so the adepti sealed it off for the Traveler to speak to Zizhi.

208.content:
Mt. Hulao (also: Amber-Prison Mountain): Mt. Hulao is a mountain in Minlin, Liyue, near the Dragon-Queller and Nantianmen, and the abode of the adeptus Mountain Shaper, a red-and-orange crane. Its slopes are guarded by karst crawlers, flowers he planted whose hidden roots wrap anything that steps on them in amber; breaking the amber frees whatever was trapped, whether treasure or an enemy. A large sealed cave near the pond is his dwelling, and when the Traveler first comes the adeptus is away.

It is where the Traveler meets Mountain Shaper in the first Archon Quest chapter. The name Hulao is rendered "Amber-Prison Mountain" by the wiki.

Geography: A subarea of Minlin. The path up the mountain winds past ambers; at the top stands a large talisman-sealed barrier in front of a pond and a sealed cave. The Huaguang Stone Forest lies to its northeast. Local specialties: Cor Lapis and Qingxin.

An in-world stone tablet on the mountain describes the Mountain Shaper's power as coming from inner enlightenment and outer knowledge: as the dragon spits what becomes amber and the swallow spits what becomes its nest, so the adeptus used nature's power to build an amber prison. Enemies include Hilichurl fighters, Dendro samachurls, Geo and Dendro slimes, and Cryo and Pyro Abyss mages.

Places: The sealed cave and pond at the top (the Mountain Shaper's abode); the mountain road lined with Amber Rock; a pagoda northeast of the waypoint.

Interacting with the barrier reads at first as a mystery: Jueyun Karst is where the adepti dwell, so perhaps this is an adeptus's home, but there appears to be no way in. After the first Archon Quest act it reads instead as the abode of Mountain Shaper, who is presently absent.

People: Mountain Shaper, an adeptus who first appears as a crane and has a human form of a bespectacled young man with a red streak in his dark hair (a human alias, Jiehu, appears in later event content). Two brothers, Li Ding and Li Dang, appear in the Archon Quest: poor men who came to hunt for treasure in the amber and were caught.

In the quest, Li Ding, praying at the top, mistakes the Traveler and Paimon for "adepti messengers" because they pass safely through Jueyun Karst. They go along with it. Li Dang is rescued from an amber and the two flee down the mountain promising to earn an honest living.

History: Mountain Shaper was one of the adepti summoned by Morax to fight in the Archon War. He explains that he planted the karst crawlers after settling here so that the mountain's tranquillity would not be disturbed; over the years they have prevented many disturbances but also trapped many curious things. He says that as the people of Liyue prospered, the adepti withdrew gradually into the mountains as a gesture of good will. According to the wiki's summary of Qiqi's character story, he once imprisoned the girl Qiqi in amber when she went on a rampage after the adepti revived her.

With Moon Carver and a third adeptus, he later helped Rex Lapis subdue the Geo dragon Azhdaha, as shown by the Nameless Treasure collection. After the Traveler tells him what happened at the Rite of Descension, he says he will convene with the other adepti once he has dealt with matters that need his attention on the mountain, since he fears the amber would trap innocents in his absence.

Atmosphere: An austere, defended mountain: ambers like golden boulders along the path, a talisman-sealed cave and few visitors. Local folk believe an adeptus lives here, but ordinary people never meet them.

Dangers: Amber Rock that traps travelers and may release enemies or treasure; Abyss mages; ordinary hilichurl camps.

Quests: Moulder of Mountains (Archon Quest, Chapter I, Act I: Of the Land Amidst Monoliths). Moon Carver sends the Traveler here to Mountain Shaper with a Sigil of Permission.

In the quest, Li Ding or the freed Li Dang can be met in either order; once Li Dang is freed, Mountain Shaper appears as a crane and demands to know who trespasses and frees a thief. He softens when shown the Sigil of Permission, which he says Rex Lapis cast by hand for mortals in small numbers, so few remain. He is startled that Moon Carver trusted a mortal as messenger, and his reaction to the news of Rex Lapis is anger, not grief: he asks what power in the world could aspire to such treason.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mt. Hulao is unchanged. Mountain Shaper left to convene with the other adepti in Chapter I, and he reappears in later seasonal event content.

209.comment: Mt. Hulao: Mountain Shaper at Mt. Hulao
209.content: Mountain Shaper is the adeptus of Mt. Hulao, formally known as the Perfected Lord who Guides the Waters and Shapes the Mountains (the wiki's translation of his Chinese title). His character page belongs in the NPC entry; here, note only that he protects the mountain by planting karst crawlers and speaks in the formal impersonal "one" of the older adepti.

210.content:
Mt. Laixin (also: Laixin, the sacred mountain, Láixīn-shān): Mt. Laixin ("the sacred mountain") is the peak where Chenyu Vale's spirit veins converge, so whoever controls it can control every acre of the vale. It was sealed until the 4.4 quest An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade opened it. On it stand Chiwang Terrace, an altar copied from the ancient city of Lang-Gan, and Carp's Rest, the abode of the carp adeptus Fujin, with the Votive Rainjade where offerings are made.

It is the only area on the world map without a Statue of the Seven.

Geography: A mountain in the vale's heart. Before it is unlocked, entering the area turns the view red and triggers an out-of-bounds reaction; the map shows it as colorless rather than red. Chiwang Terrace is on the summit; Carp's Rest is an adeptal abode on the mountain.

Its peak is called Chiwang Peak in the viewpoint text, and the viewpoint of Carp's Rest is called Clarion Echo.

Places: Chiwang Terrace: a jade-styled altar, unlocked by An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade. Carp's Rest: Fujin's abode, unlocked in The Cloud-Padded Path to the Chiwang Repose. Votive Rainjade: the offering site in Carp's Rest.

In the offering system, offering Spirit Carp raises Rainjade's Benediction and, at maximum, two yellow carps circle the jade and spirit smoke rises.

People: Fujin, the carp adeptus, rests at Carp's Rest. Lingyuan, the suanni who presides over the vale, can be spoken to at the summit in The Cloud-Padded Path. Little Mao, who was befriended by Lingyuan, appears in the quests.

Governance: None. A quest states that controlling Mt. Laixin means controlling all of Chenyu Vale; by disturbing the spirit veins, Lingyuan soured the soil and water and so the tea.

Culture: Chenyu Vale's ancestors offered jade by throwing it into the water, passing adeptal energy to the spirit veins, protecting their homeland and securing good weather and harvests. The rite is long forgotten; the game restores a version of it through offerings of Spirit Carp.

Chiwang Terrace is a copy of the jade altar once used in Lang-Gan to honor the White Horse Adeptus, Zibai. After she sacrificed herself to delay a Celestial Nail, the refugees rebuilt their society in Chenyu Vale, altar included (per the Chiwang Terrace wiki, citing the 6.3 story quest The Realm of Rocks).

History: Fujin hurled the Votive Rainjade from Mt. Lingmeng to quell the mistress's flood in the Archon War and then sank, losing power, into Carp's Rest, where for thousands of years she could only reminisce about the outside world through the scent of tea offerings. In 4.4 the Traveler found that Lingyuan, who longed for her old friend, was disturbing the spirit veins to restore the vale to nature; she yielded after defeat and Fujin performed the Rainjade Rite.

The rite restored soil and water but drained Fujin so she returned to carp form and to Carp's Rest. Some miasma still remained afterward. Lingyuan told the Traveler she would answer at their next meeting whether humans acted against their purpose.

Atmosphere: Spirit smoke curling from the jade, golden carp circling and the hush of an old rite.

Dangers: Miasma and the monsters it drives wild. Before the quest, the area is sealed and walking into it triggers an out-of-bounds reaction.

Travel: Locked until An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade; afterwards open. Carp's Rest requires finishing The Cloud-Padded Path to the Chiwang Repose, a quest available one in-game day after the earlier one.

Quests: Qiaoying of the Sacred Mountain begins at Carp's Rest, where the Traveler is first drawn into an adepti realm. The Cloud-Padded Path to the Chiwang Repose has them ascend the summit, speak to Lingyuan and meet Fujin at Carp's Rest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mt. Laixin is open to travelers; Fujin rests at Carp's Rest and Lingyuan presides over the vale.

Fujin can also be found outside Qiaoying with Lingyuan or Little Mao after completing Rainjade's Benediction.

211.comment: Mt. Laixin: Carp's Rest and Fujin
211.content: Carp's Rest is Fujin's abode on Mt. Laixin, the hidden refuge she retreated to after the war, "sinking into the sea" and losing much of her strength. Fujin, a giant golden carp who took human form, was worshiped as an adeptus and was close to humans. The Traveler first met her there in Qiaoying of the Sacred Mountain, when she lent them adeptal energy. After performing the Rainjade Rite she is back at Carp's Rest, in her carp form, to recover.

212.comment: Mt. Laixin: Chiwang Terrace and Lang-Gan's altar
212.content: Chiwang Terrace is a copy of an altar from the ancient civilisation of Lang-Gan, built to honor the White Horse Adeptus Zibai. After her sacrifice delayed a Celestial Nail, Lang-Gan's survivors fled to Chenyu Vale and rebuilt their society, including the altar. The terrace is unlocked by An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade.

213.content: The Votive Rainjade is a jade where Chenyu Vale's ancestors once offered jade by casting it into water, transferring adeptal energy to the spirit veins to guard their homeland and bring favorable weather and harvests. The old rite has long been forgotten, but if the lost adeptal energy is gathered into the jade again, the soil and water might be blessed anew. Offering Spirit Carp to the jade raises Rainjade's Benediction and unlocks rewards.

214.content:
Mt. Lingmeng (also: Past Glories of Wangshan): Mt. Lingmeng is a mountain in the Upper Vale of Chenyu Vale, Liyue, west of Qiaoying Village and southeast of Yilong Wharf. Its main landmark is Wangshan Hall, the weathered stronghold of the Guhua Clan, a martial school whose glory has faded. Local folklore also places an ancient cave and old spirits of the vale beneath its waterfalls.

The mountain, introduced in Version 4.4, is also the place from which, in the vale's history, the adeptus Fujin threw the Votive Rainjade into the water to save the people.

Geography: A subarea of Chenyu Vale's Upper Vale. Wangshan Hall (a main hall and a secret chamber) is the area's only listed point of interest. An Ancient Cave beneath the northwest waterfall holds a mural, once cleaned, showing the people of Chenyu Vale performing the Votive Rainjade ritual.

Chenyu Vale's climate is described as relatively humid. Wangshan Hall's main hall is unlocked during the quest A Wangshan Walk to Remember, and its secret chamber opens after Scrolls and Sword Manuals of Guhua.

Places: Wangshan Hall: the stronghold of the Guhua Clan, in disrepair because of the clan's decline. Huang the Third, a clan member, tries to raise money for its restoration by luring people at Yilong Wharf to tour it with exaggerated claims of its majesty.

The viewpoint "Past Glories of Wangshan" says that when Guhua was at its height, heroes from all walks of life gathered there to drink and sing, and the hall is still inscribed with the "chivalry" of years past. The clan teaches the three Guhua Greats (Light Piercer for polearms, Rain Cutter for swords, Life Ender for both), and its founder Guhua himself wielded a claymore, Rainslasher. According to the wiki the hall is where Guhua is said to have attained enlightenment.

People: Guhua Clan members live at and around the hall: Huang the Third, Wen the Fourth and others, a handful of practitioners trying to restore the clan's reputation.

The clan was founded not by Guhua himself, who never took a disciple, but after his death by Boxuan (Master Baixuan), who claimed to be his disciple to carry on his legacy. At its height the brotherhood was famed across Liyue for chivalry; over a few centuries it renamed itself several times and shrank to a few people.

The wiki's member list also names Wakamatsu among current members; Chen the Sharp and Zhiruo as former members; and, historically, Yingmin (Piercing Blade, the 11th master) and Zhangsun Jijing (Rainbearer). The area's music track is titled Guhua's Legacy.

History: At the end of the Archon War, in the story of An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade, the mistress of Chenyu Vale unleashed a flood down the Bishui River. Herblord fought her while Lingyuan led the people to shelter, and Fujin climbed Mt. Lingmeng and hurled the Votive Rainjade into the waters; the flood was stopped, though Fujin lost much of her strength. The cave murals on the mountain depict the rite.

The three-volume book Mt. Lingmeng Gossip, sold in Liyue Harbor, collects what its description calls far-fetched local folk legends. It says people of the mountain once worshipped many supernatural beings, that the old gods and spirits vanished in the Archon War, and that the leylines kept echoes of them, which sometimes appear as shadows in fog and rain and are taken as an ill omen. A second tale tells of a lost mariner who found a cavern of figures in ancient robes throwing jade into a dark pool, and of the physician Lan Jing, who entered the mountain in his youth and never spoke of it. A third speaks of a demon lord of the mountain beside a long-destroyed lunar chariot, ruler of the birds, beasts and adepti of wild nature, who is said to have been sealed beneath the vale.

Quests: World quests Scrolls and Sword Manuals of Guhua (Arcane Archive puzzle) and Shrouded Vale, Hidden Hero (a trial and an ancient sword), plus A Wangshan Walk to Remember. A hidden exploration objective, Wangshan Swordsman's Inscriptions, is also tied to the hall.

Shrouded Vale, Hidden Hero ends with a trial in four waves of enemies and an investigation of an ancient sword. After it, a Stonehide Lawachurl appears at the training place; its titles call it an uninitiated Guhua disciple.

Atmosphere: Fog, waterfalls and old hall timbers, with a sense that the mountain remembers more than its people do. The village stories make visitors cautious of mist and rain.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mt. Lingmeng is unchanged, and the Guhua Clan still maintains Wangshan Hall as a modest school. No later story content was found that alters it.

215.comment: Mt. Lingmeng: Wangshan Hall and the Guhua Clan
215.content: Wangshan Hall is the base and main training ground of the Guhua Clan. It has a main hall and a secret chamber, and is kept up by the few members who remain. The clan's motto, as quoted by its former member Chen the Sharp, is that the noblest martial virtue is to pursue what benefits other people. Xingqiu counts as a member with the title Guhua Guru of Feiyun Fame.

216.content:
Mt. Mingyuan (also: Mount Mingyuan): Mt. Mingyuan is a mountain in Chenyu Vale's Upper Vale in Liyue. It stands west of Yilong Wharf and east of Fontaine, directly under Celestia, whose floating island is visible straight overhead. The world quest The Dealing Sands begins here.

A Millelith camp lies on its southern slope, and a beach to its west was the setting for a sting against smugglers.

Geography: The wiki places it west of Yilong Wharf, east of Fontaine and under Celestia; a Treasure Hoarder camp sits west of the southern waypoint. The page lists Iron Dou'er as its NPC.

Standing on the mountain, the floating island of Celestia is visible directly above. A beach west of the mountain and a cliff above it were used in the quest, with the cliff's foot the meeting place for a deal.

People: Iron Dou'er, Iron Chuan'er and other "Iron" Treasure Hoarders loiter about the beach west of the mountain; Dou'er and Chuan'er turn out to be Millelith in disguise. At a Millelith camp on the southern slope the quest page lists Hongyu, Qingye (both in hoarder outfits) and Yijun.

Iron Dou'er has relatives in Liyue Harbor and recognised the Traveler at once but kept quiet so as not to spook the smugglers. The boss of the Iron and Salt Gang is Iron Ming; the buyer is Johnnie, called the Pinky Club's Pinky and from Fontaine, with a companion called Walker.

History: In The Dealing Sands the Millelith spent about a month infiltrating the Iron and Salt Gang, which was smuggling goods to buyers from Fontaine. When the Traveler stumbled onto a deal at the beach, the Millelith revealed themselves, fought Johnnie and Iron Ming, and arrested the smugglers. They paid the Traveler in Mora and said such helpers should be rewarded so that others would help too.

Iron Ming had planned to silence the Traveler under what he called an unspoken contract of outlaws, and boasted of the prices that rival buyers' families paid for his cargo, citing Liyue's love of contracts. Iron Dou'er answered that they would stop villains like him from befouling Liyue.

A ragged notebook at a hoarder camp west of the southern waypoint is thought by the wiki to belong to the same ring. It mentions Pinky Club buyers waiting on a beach, wariness of Fontainian underhandedness, and goods that must be covered by tea leaves and porcelain.

Quests: The Dealing Sands starts at Mt. Mingyuan with Iron Dou'er. The player goes to the beach beneath the cliff, joins talks between the two parties, defeats Johnnie and then Iron Ming, and speaks to the Millelith. It rewards the achievement Breaking Iron and Stone.

Dangers: Treasure Hoarders are present, though the "hoarders" at the camp and beach are mostly Millelith in costume; real hoarders and Fontainian smugglers appear in the quest.

Atmosphere: A windy mountain under the vast shadow of Celestia, with a beach, a camp and tension of a secret operation. This is a suggested scene mood drawn from the trivia and the quest.

Status as of 7.1: The smuggling ring is broken and its leaders arrested; nothing later changes it as of 7.1.

217.content: In The Dealing Sands, Millelith agents posing as the Iron and Salt Gang's Treasure Hoarders caught the real gang boss and a Fontainian buyer from the Pinky Club on a Mt. Mingyuan beach, with the Traveler's help.

218.content:
Mt. Tianheng (also: Mount Tianheng, Tianheng): Mt. Tianheng is the mountain range that shelters Liyue Harbor from the west and north, a natural shield for the city. Old tablets say Rex Lapis raised it when he first came down to Liyue, and that the first people there mined jade from its depths. Today it holds the Golden House, where Mora is minted, Blackcliff Forge, the Guizhong Ballista and the cliff-side district of Yujing Terrace.

In-game description calls it the pride of the range that shelters the harbor, a natural shield against anyone who comes from the west. Records speak of many wars where enemies were stopped by it, and the old walls, forts and defences are still visible.

Geography: The map labels the peaks west of Liyue Harbor as Mt. Tianheng. The wiki points out that the range north of the harbor, which the road to Guili Plains crosses, is also part of it. Yujing Terrace is built along its cliffside, and Chihu Rock connects to it on the west by bridge.

Tianheng Pass is the passage the Guizhong Ballista was built to defend. Ruined walls, forts and defensive structures survive in the hills.

Development note: a level artist says the entrance to Liyue Harbor through Mt. Tianheng was inspired by Tianmen Mountain in China, to give arrival a sense of ceremony and a strong contrast between the pass and the trade city that opens up beyond it.

Places: - The Golden House: the mint where all of Teyvat's Mora is made.
- Blackcliff Forge: the workshops that gave their name to the Blackcliff and Prototype weapon series.
- The Guizhong Ballista: an ancient automatic crossbow.
- The Jade Chamber: the Qixing's floating palace, here classed as part of Mt. Tianheng.
- Yujing Terrace, built into the cliffs.

Blackcliff Forge was built by excavating the mountains and joining workshops and furnaces with tunnels. White Tassels are also produced there. Manager Kuan is its shift supervisor; Jingda and Iron Shoulder are workers. The Golden House has a steward, Gongming, and Millelith guards. The Geo and Anemo monument puzzles and a ruin near the teleport waypoint south of Guili Plains also lie in the range.

History: According to Stone Tablet Compilations, Rex Lapis lowered the tides, raised Mt. Tianheng and calmed the waves when he first descended. People cut into the mountain, found jade and built a settlement they named Shanhui Fort ("Mountain Splendor Fort"); everyone prospered from the mines. The goddess Guizhong set up the Guizhong Ballista to guard it. Later Guizhong led her people north of the range to the Guili Plains. After she fell in the Archon War, Rex Lapis led his people south of Mt. Tianheng, where Liyue Harbor was founded.

The name Shanhui Fort was later shortened to "Shanhui Rock" and then "Mountain Rock". The mountain tribes are said to have sheltered in the tunnels of the forge in times of war, and long-forgotten passages are said to lead to an ancient underground realm. Liyue's earliest mining is believed to have started here. The Yun family's founder is credited with first tunnelling through the range.

The Guizhong Ballista was designed by Guizhong, under the name Obscuro Vulpes Mechanism, with help from adepti, among them Cloud Retainer. Rex Lapis judged it better than a mechanism Cloud Retainer had built. After Guizhong died, Cloud Retainer put finishing touches on it in her memory.

People: Blackcliff Forge workers and miners; Gongming and Millelith guards at the Golden House; Treasure Hoarders, Fatui skirmishers and other enemies in the ruins.

Millelith soldiers are posted around the Guizhong Ballista after its repair. Ningguang's Jade Chamber floats above Liyue Harbor.

Dangers: Fatui Skirmishers (Geochanter Bracers and Electrohammer Vanguards), hilichurl shooters, samachurls, slimes, Rock Shieldwall Mitachurls and Ruin Hunters wander the range. The Guizhong Ballista fires on perceived threats, including Treasure Hoarders approaching the ruins.

A Geo Monument puzzle awakens an Eye of the Storm, an elite enemy.

Travel: Liyue Harbor lies at the foot of the range. The main road from the north runs through Mt. Tianheng and arrives at Feiyun Slope. Another road leaves the city from Yujing Terrace past the Guizhong Ballista.

Quests: - Farewell, Archaic Lord (Archon Quest, 1.0): Zhongli and the Traveler repair the Guizhong Ballista with spare parts to hunt a "cocogoat" for Qiqi, and fight off Treasure Hoarders who had broken it. The Ballista is later mysteriously repaired overnight and the Millelith guard it.
- A New Star Approaches (1.1): the Traveler fights Childe at the Golden House, then Osial; the Jade Chamber is sacrificed.

In the Interlude Chapter (2.4), "Where the Heart Finds Rest" starts in Mt. Tianheng, where the rebuilt Jade Chamber is used to lure the sea monster Beisht, while Ballistae fire from Guyun Stone Forest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mt. Tianheng still shelters Liyue Harbor, with the Golden House no longer minting. No content from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes it.

The Golden House no longer mints Mora since the Geo Gnosis was handed to the Tsaritsa. The Jade Chamber has been rebuilt (2.4).

219.content: The Golden House is where all of Teyvat's Mora is minted. After the Rite of Descension the Qixing moved the dead god's body, the Exuvia, here. The Traveler faced Childe there before Osial's attack. After Rex Lapis handed his Gnosis to the Tsaritsa, it stopped minting new Mora.

220.content: Blackcliff Forge is known as the birthplace of the Blackcliff and Prototype series weapons and also makes White Tassels. Its workshops and furnaces were carved into the mountains and joined by tunnels. Mountain tribes are said to have sheltered in the tunnels in wartime and unexplored passages lead to an ancient underground realm. The Yun family's founder is credited with first tunnelling through these mountains.

221.content: A giant automatic crossbow built by Guizhong, the late Goddess of Dust, and the adepti to protect Liyue. It fires at any perceived threat nearby, even Treasure Hoarders. After Guizhong's death Cloud Retainer finished it in her memory. A notice at the supply post says its spare parts should only be collected by a worthy craftsman if "that ancient evil" returns. Replica ballistae were used against Osial at the Jade Chamber, and enhanced ones against Beisht at Guyun Stone Forest.

222.comment: Mt. Tianheng: Skybracer and the Propped-Up Mountain
222.content: In a tale told by Madame Ping at Lantern Rite, an enemy god's blow during the Archon War nearly toppled Mt. Tianheng onto a village at its foot. The adeptus Skybracer had a friend cut off his antlers, a gift made of Morax's divine power and the hardest substance in Liyue, and wedged them under the mountain, which rose higher than before. He kept fighting until he died of his wounds, and his blood is said to have become the Bishui River. The legend is told during the Lantern Rite event and is not confirmed elsewhere.

223.comment: Mt. Tianheng: The Archon War and the Move South
223.content: The goddess Guizhong lived with her people on the Guili Plains north of Mt. Tianheng, tending the soil and allied with Rex Lapis. Warfare among the gods later devastated the plains and killed her. Rex Lapis led his people south of Mt. Tianheng, and they never returned. The plains became wilderness. Liyue Harbor grew from that settlement.

224.content:
Mt. Xuanlian (also: Mount Xuanlian): Mt. Xuanlian is a peak in Chenyu Vale's Southern Mountain in Liyue, south of Chizhang Wall and Yaodie Valley. It is admired for strange rock and sunset views, and a nearby cave holds the blessed water sought in a world quest.

A viewpoint here is called Clear Skies Over Xuanlian. The Hezhe Post photography contest names the mountain as one of its four subjects.

Geography: South of Chizhang Wall and south of Yaodie Valley; reached by a shortcut from Yaodie Valley through a cave. Pressure plates in a cave near the mountain hide a Sacred Simulacrum.

A small path leads from Yaodie Valley to the mountain, and a cave and the "blessed waters" of Mt. Xuanlian lie at its end.

People: Akai, a contest competitor in Our Chenyu Vale Trek, is menaced by monsters on the mountain and shares his best photo spot with the Traveler.

History: The viewpoint text quotes a short line of verse: the weighty winds blow, the day is dark, but the cascading falls run clear. A competitor's scenery guide in Our Chenyu Vale Trek says you rarely see such strange mountains elsewhere and that the sunset there is "truly moving".

In The Roaming Abode, a Qiaoying herb gatherer left to draw blessed water near the mountain for a divine plant at his house. He was injured by monsters on the way; Uncle Luo says villagers found him near Mt. Xuanlian clutching a bottle, buried him and poured the water in his yard. The Traveler fetches the Xuanlian Sacred Water too.

Luo scoffs that the water is only river water. A text in the herb gatherer's yard, Pharmacy's Amelioration, describes a strange grass named Xiangjun on an earthen raft that floats without water, a few leagues east of the mountain.

Quests: Our Chenyu Vale Trek (photograph the mountain between 17:00 and 18:00 for Picture: Mt. Xuanlian) and The Roaming Abode (draw blessed water at the cave). The viewpoint is Clear Skies Over Xuanlian.

Dangers: Hilichurls near the quest photo spot; monsters in the shortcut cave that wounded a villager in The Roaming Abode.

Atmosphere: Weathered rock, falls running clear and sunset light on a lonely mountain. This is a suggested scene mood drawn from the viewpoint and the scenery guide.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1.

225.content:
Nameless Ruins (also: Wúmíng Yíjì, Nameless Ruins of the Chasm): The Nameless Ruins are an area of ancient, unnamed ruins in the Underground Mines under the Chasm in Liyue. Mounds of dark mud cover the floor, and the roof of the cavern bears an upside-down ruin with a water pool: the Inverted City, an old Lang-Gan site. The mines' travellers meet Abyss mages, Ruin Guards and hilichurls here.

The Nameless Ruins are where the Archon Quest of Chapter II brings the Traveler and Dainsleif deep below the Chasm.

Geography: A set of halls, stairs and sealed sections in the Underground Mines. The floor holds solid dark-mud mounds, luminous Seelie wander the dark, and Oozing Concretions and Noctilucous Jade grow here. A purple barrier closed off the Inverted City until "The Grave of the Guarded".

The architecture is geometric with triangular forms, gold strips and vertical sliding doors. The wiki observes a resemblance to Enkanomiya, which is not stated in canon.

People: No settled inhabitants. In 2.6 hilichurls drifted here to die, protected by cursed Black Serpent Knights loyal to Dainsleif's old command; Abyss Order cells appear in the same area.

Dangers: Elite Abyss mages (Electro, Hydro, Pyro), Ruin Guards and Ruin Graders, Black Serpent Knights and Shadowy Husks, plus Hilichurls, Floating Hydro Fungus, Cryo Whopperflowers and Geo Slimes.

Quests: "Requiem of the Echoing Depths" (Chapter II Act IV, 2.6), especially "The Grave of the Guarded"; it also lies on the way for "Perilous Trail" in the Chasm.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 a dark, mostly empty set of ruins under a partly reopened mine.

226.comment: Nameless Ruins: Nameless Ruins and the Black Serpent Knights
226.content: The knights fought here with no honour left, because the curse had corroded them, yet one silently ordered the others to stand down. The place let Dainsleif confirm that the hilichurls came to the Chasm to die near the pool that eases the curse. Halfdan died here holding back the amplifier.

227.content:
Nantianmen (also: Southern Heavenly Gate): Nantianmen is the northwestern corner of Minlin, where an enormous tree with glowing blue veins, the Dragon-Queller, rises from the rocks. Beneath it lies the Geo dragon Azhdaha, an ancient friend of Rex Lapis that the adepti sealed after erosion drove him mad. A stone tablet by the tree asks passers-by not to disturb the evil dragon beneath.

The tablet reads that life endures in Heaven and Earth thanks to the merciful Adeptus, and that an evil dragon lies here. The Dragon-Queller is described as a tree that the dragon is slowly merging with. The name means "Southern Heavenly Gate", a term in Chinese myth for the gate between mortal and heavenly realms.

Geography: Nantianmen lies in the northwest of Minlin, near Mt. Hulao. The Dragon-Queller is a massive tree whose branches flow with cold moonlight; at its tip a large blue branch points straight toward Liyue Harbor and cannot be climbed. Bright yellow flowers grow around its base.

Its roots reach deep into the earth. Hilichurls, Treasure Hoarders and Eremites are found around it.

The wiki says the clash of elemental energies in the battle created Dragonfall, a rare ore; Zhongli explains in No Mere Stone that it forms through elemental reactions rather than heat and was mined to obscurity a few centuries ago.

Places: - The Dragon-Queller, the tree that seals Azhdaha, with the Moonlit Tree viewpoint.
- The stone tablet at the tree's foot, erected by Mountain Shaper as a warning.
- Beneath the Dragon-Queller: the domain in the earth under the tree where Azhdaha is fought.

Jiu, a girl who worshipped Azhdaha, once stood by the tree in the open world before 1.5. The roots draw on ley lines.

People: Jiu, a young-looking girl who was Azhdaha's vessel, was seen here before the events of Zhongli's story quest. The miners of the Chasm were lured here. Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver sealed the dragon long ago.

Kun Jun, a man possessed by the benevolent remnant of Azhdaha's mind, searched for Dragonfall in Liyue. The Millelith of Liyue Harbor, such as Jiayi, send people to check on the region.

History: Azhdaha, a Geo dragon ruling much of what is now Liyue, was woken from a long sleep and gained sight from Morax, whom he befriended and swore never to harm Liyue. Erosion made him forget, and mining in the Chasm hurt the ley lines and drove him into a rage. Morax, Mountain Shaper, Moon Carver and another adeptus fought him from the Chasm north to Nantianmen. With a shred of sanity he accepted his fate, and was sealed in the Dragon-Queller. Mountain Shaper set up the tablet.

Over centuries the seal weakened. Azhdaha manifested a vessel, Jiu, to announce his return, found that nobody remembered him, and had Jiu lead missing miners from the Chasm to unearth the seal. In Zhongli's story quest (1.5) the Traveler and Zhongli fought him below the tree, assisted by his benevolent remnant in Kun Jun's body, and resealed him.

He is said to believe that Morax betrayed him, because erosion erased his memory of consenting to the seal. A flashback at the Moonlight Merriment event (2.1) shows him gazing at the night sky with the goddess Marchosius riding on his shoulder.

Atmosphere: A strange, moonlit stillness around a vast living tree whose branches glow cold blue, with a feeling that something huge is waiting beneath. The viewpoint text says its roots reach into the heart of the earth, perhaps joined to something that awaits an opportunity to emerge and bask in moonlight.

Dangers: Hilichurls, Cryo and Geo slimes, Treasure Hoarders, Eremites, Stonehide Lawachurls, Rock Shieldwall Mitachurls and Ruin Hunters wander the area. The deeper danger is the sealed dragon, whose seal weakened over time.

After the 1.5 events Azhdaha was resealed, but the Dragon-Queller stays dangerous to disturb.

Travel: The tree stands between Mt. Hulao and Nantianmen proper. The Trounce Domain beneath it is entered through the tree.

Quests: - The Secret of Nantianmen (world quest, 1.1): Jiayi asks the Traveler to check on reports of earthquakes; they find nothing unusual.
- No Mere Stone (Zhongli's story quest, 1.5): the missing miners, Jiu, Kun Jun and the fight with Azhdaha.

Moonlight Merriment (2.1): Azhdaha appears in a cinematic with Marchosius.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Azhdaha remains sealed under the Dragon-Queller after being resealed in 1.5. No content from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the site.

Jiu faded away, and the benevolent remnant said goodbye to Morax.

228.content:
Azhdaha is an ancient earth dragon, once Morax's friend and ally in the Archon War. Erosion made him forget Morax and mortals; when miners damaged the ley lines in the Chasm he attacked humans, and Morax and the adepti sealed him in the Dragon-Queller. Centuries later his vessel Jiu tried to free him. He was beaten by the Traveler, Zhongli and his own benevolent remnant, and resealed. The tablet by the tree was set up by Mountain Shaper to warn the world.

Azhdaha was born of elemental crystallisation and slept underground for thousands of years until his stirring caused earthquakes. Morax gave him eyes, they made a contract that he would never harm Liyue, and Morax warned that he would be sealed if he did.

229.comment: Nantianmen: Jiu, Kun Jun and the Missing Miners
229.content: Jiu, a small girl in a green dress, worshipped Azhdaha and despised Morax. In the story quest No Mere Stone, she led a group of miners from the Chasm to dig below the Dragon-Queller to free him. Kun Jun, a man possessed by Azhdaha's benevolent remnant and looking for Dragonfall, tracked her with the Traveler and Zhongli. Jiu was a vessel of Azhdaha's wrath; as her energy ran out she faded with Morax's name on her lips.

230.content:
Nine Pillars of Peace: The Nine Pillars of Peace are nine ancient stone pillars standing on Cuijue Slope in Minlin, Liyue, around a ruin and a temple at the centre of the area. In-game viewpoint text says nine shackles of stone were said to be laid deep in the valleys there to drive off evil and cleanse the world.

Approaching them darkens the sky: when a player nears the pillars, the area turns grey and the land outside Cuijue Slope looks unnaturally dim until they leave the vicinity.

Quests: The world quest Nine Pillars of Peace is started at the stone tablet in the middle of Cuijue Slope. The Traveler gathers nine Stones of Remembrance by making offerings to Statues of the Seven in Liyue, then climbs each pillar and sets a stone into its face-like tile. Doing so opens the central ruin, where the Traveler must defeat Ruin Guard and other guardians to reach its treasure room.

The quest ends with a Dull Ring from the ruin, which the Traveler may sell to Bolai in Liyue Harbor or to Linlang. Bolai pays less Mora but adds Adeptus' Temptation, while Linlang pays more Mora. The quest's tablets say the pillars were raised to suppress conflict and warn that breaking them would let war consume the world again; Linlang relays only a legend that Liyue's forebears built them, and no builder is named.

Surroundings: Cuijue Slope, which holds the pillars, is home to a Pyro Regisvine boss and a Ruins Torch puzzle (three torches lit with Pyro open a chest), and its local specialties include Cor Lapis, Qingxin and Violetgrass.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing further has been revealed about the pillars; they remain a relic of old Liyue, raised to suppress conflict per the quest tablets, with no builder named.

231.content:
Northland Bank (Liyue) (also: Liyue Northland Bank, Northland Bank Liyue branch): The Northland Bank (Liyue) is the Liyue Harbor branch of the Northland Bank, the Snezhnayan bank with branches around Teyvat. It stands on Feiyun Slope and is the only non-local bank in Liyue. The Fatui use Northland Bank funds abroad and sometimes its branches as bases, and in the Liyue Archon Quest this branch is where the Traveler meets Childe's contact Ekaterina and where Childe arranges to meet them.

The branch is staffed by a manager, a receptionist, guards and the occasional customer. It is also the stop from which Childe sends the Traveler on to Liuli Pavilion, where he has arranged a dinner with Zhongli.

Places: The bank has a public hall inside, where the receptionist works at her desk and the manager is found by day, and a back room behind it. Guards stand outside. It sits on Feiyun Slope in upper Liyue Harbor, just above the Heyu Tea House.

The reception desk handles Mora exchanges: a player who still holds a Mora pouch left by Childe (from Downtown or Teucer's Terrific Tour) can swap it for ordinary Mora there. That is a gameplay convenience. A Precious Chest in the back room is also a gameplay detail.

People: Andrei is the manager and is inside only by day. Ekaterina is the receptionist and is present day and night; she greets the Traveler as a friend of Childe and passes on his messages. Vlad guards the door by day and Nadia (the Liyue guard) by night. A customer, Mister Qi, is inside by day.

Ekaterina speaks with the polished confidence of a Fatui functionary. In the Wangsheng quest she jokes that the Traveler's first day of an illustrious career with the Fatui has begun, says ideas are fluid like water and only the Tsaritsa's will is as solid as permafrost, and stresses that Harbingers do not lightly break promises. Vlad, asked, says it is the only non-local bank in Liyue.

Governance: The Northland Bank belongs to Snezhnaya. Later canon (7.0) says Pantalone is in charge of its operations as a whole, though other Harbingers may handle the opening of new branches. The Liyue branch operates openly in Liyue Harbor as a bank, even though Fatui business passes through it.

History: After the Rite of Descension Childe uses the bank as the place where the Traveler can find him once he is free of the Millelith. Back from visiting the adepti, the Traveler and Paimon find that the Qixing have hidden the Geo Archon's vessel. Childe has promised to find someone to break the stalemate, so they visit the bank again. Ekaterina says Childe has kept his side of the agreement and that he is at Liuli Pavilion; there he introduces Zhongli. The final visit is in The Fond Farewell, in search of Zhongli.

The leftover funds Childe provides in Downtown and Teucer's Terrific Tour (a story quest) are exchanged for Mora at this branch. This is a gameplay mechanic, and canon does not explain how his funds reach the branch.

Atmosphere: Quiet and businesslike compared with the loud restaurants and teahouses on Feiyun Slope. The staff speak politely and give nothing away; a promise made to a Harbinger is treated as a debt.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the branch remains open in Liyue Harbor as one of the Northland Bank's overseas branches.

No later canon changes it. In 7.0 the Snezhnograd headquarters and the bank's founding by Pantalone were shown; that history belongs to the main bank, not this branch.

232.content: Staff seen in the Liyue branch: Andrei, the manager (daytime, inside); Ekaterina, the receptionist (inside, day and night); Mister Qi, a customer (daytime); Vlad, a guard outside by day; Nadia, a guard outside at night. Ekaterina is the one who deals with the Traveler on Childe's behalf.

233.comment: Northland Bank (Liyue): Northland Bank as the Fatui's Foreign Base
233.content: Loading-screen text says the Northland Bank has branches in many places; when the Fatui operate outside Snezhnaya they use funds provided by the bank and even use it as a base. Pantalone founded the bank shortly after becoming a Harbinger and is in charge of its operations. Loans are generous but must be repaid in full and on time, and the Fatui have a debt-collection division for those who default.

234.content:
Pearl Galley (also: The Pearl Galley): The Pearl Galley is a luxurious ship anchored near Liyue Harbor in the Sea of Clouds, meant for the exclusive enjoyment of specially invited guests. Its receptionist is Luoxia and its proprietor is Rouran.

Guests are expected to come by invitation; the Traveler's first boarding without one is handled gently by Luoxia. Once The Ocean Pearl is done, the ferryman Pinghai can take the Traveler to and from the ship.

People: Aboard are the receptionist Luoxia, the poet Li the Ninth, Cui'er, Guan Hong, Luo Feng, Maksim and Qiu'ge, with Uncle Zhao as daytime security. Pinghai ferries visitors from Liyue Harbor.

The Ocean Pearl quest has the Traveler gather an invitation letter from guests, deliver letters between Cui'er and Chaoxi, and bring Qiu'ge three Qingxin flowers, before Luoxia and Pinghai return them to the harbor.

Culture: A scroll on one table, the Connoisseur Catalog, offers the ship's "wares of beauty" in poetic language and lists the names of the "flowers" of the painted boat. The wiki reads these as the names of hostesses who can be hired to keep guests company. The catalogue's line about the beauty of water lying in the pearls it holds echoes a classical Chinese essay on literature.

Naming: The ship's Chinese name, Zhudian-fang, is rendered on the wiki as "Pearl-Inlaid Boat".

Quests: Boarding for the first time triggers the world quest The Ocean Pearl. The ship is also the starting point of Zhongli's story quest Shadow of Yore, the first part of Sal Flore, where Zhongli is discussing Rex Lapis and the first Mora with guests at a table and the Traveler meets Wanyan at the stern. If The Ocean Pearl is not yet complete, it starts first and both quests can proceed together.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Pearl Galley remains moored near Liyue Harbor.

235.content:
Pervases' Temple (also: Temple of Pervases): Pervases' Temple is a small temple in Lisha dedicated to Pervases, a Yaksha who died in the Archon War, and holds a statue of him. It began as a run-down house, then was restored through the Hereafter quests. Wang Ping'an, once the false adeptus Starsnatcher, now keeps it and gives out incense for visitors to offer to the statue.

Pervases was a junior Yaksha who served Rex Lapis and perished during the Archon War. The temple is where his spirit lingered in a crane statue, and where Xiao is moved by the loss of his fellow Yakshas.

Places: Before restoration the temple looks like a dilapidated house in poor repair, with Treasure Hoarders nearby. After the quests it is repaired and tidy, with a censer and a statue of Pervases. The statue shows an illuminated beast form, a crane wearing a large-bead necklace like the one Xiao wears.

After the restoration Wang Ping'an stands by the temple and gives out Fine Incense to anyone who asks. Offering it to the statue is an interaction in the game. During the limited-time event Waterborne Poetry (4.1), Xiao composed a poem about the Yaksha and left it on the table inside.

The Ministry of Civil Affairs posted Millelith to guard the temple while it was being rebuilt, since Wang Ping'an feared that Treasure Hoarders might raid the material deliveries.

People: Wang Ping'an looks after the temple, hands out incense and says few people come, that the temple is off the beaten track and he wonders how to let people know it is there. He is writing a book about Xiao, the Vigilant Yaksha, and collects evidence for the stories.

Xiao is connected to the temple through his fellow Yaksha. Pervases is described as close to Bosacius, the Prime Yaksha, and Xiao regrets that Pervases was one of many Yakshas who paid the ultimate price.

History: In Xiao's story quest Butterfly's Dream, Pervases performs the Mortal Lingering ritual with a censer and seven-star lamps to see modern Liyue, then permits the Traveler to take them, knowing that dispels his ritual. He senses the karmic burden Xiao bears, tells them the truth about himself and leaves a message for Xiao before going dormant. Starsnatcher, now Wang Ping'an, repents, repays his followers and later sets out to restore the temple. In Hereafter the Traveler buys grilled tiger fish near Wanmin Restaurant and brings a serving for Pervases. They find Wang Ping'an attacked by hilichurls and Treasure Hoarders and help him; across the three quests of the series the temple is rebuilt, and he stays on as its keeper. After Rex Lapis saves Xiao in The Chasm, Xiao returns to the temple to think about the fate of the Yakshas.

Atmosphere: A small, quiet shrine off the beaten track with incense burning before a crane statue; a place for remembering those who died in the war without recognition.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the temple stands restored in Lisha under Wang Ping'an's care.

No later canon changes it.

236.content: Pervases was a junior Yaksha under Rex Lapis, who gave him the name. He died during the Archon War and a thousand years later, on the anniversary, performed the Mortal Lingering ritual to see modern Liyue. His favourite food was grilled fish, and he is shown as a man with short slicked-back black hair or, in statue form, a crane. His spirit lies dormant in the statue at the temple.

237.comment: Pervases' Temple: Wang Ping'an and Starsnatcher
237.content: Wang Ping'an posed as the adeptus Starsnatcher, using a Sigil of Permission and an ornate mask, until Xiao's story quest exposed him as a fake. He repented, repaid his followers and, in Hereafter, rebuilt Pervases' temple. He remains there as its keeper and is writing a book on Xiao.

238.content:
Qiaoying Village (also: Qiaoying): Qiaoying Village is a mountain village in Chenyu Vale, north-western Liyue, close to the Fontaine border. It is known throughout Teyvat for high-quality tea, sold in Liyue Harbor and exported to other nations, and is home to the Chunming Teaworks. Its architecture is inspired by real-world Hui-style buildings.

Locals credit the blessing of the adepti on Chenyu Vale's land and water for the ideal tea-growing conditions. A special cauldron, said to be an adeptal mechanism, roasts the leaves and gives them their aroma.

Geography: Qiaoying sits in the Upper Vale of Chenyu Vale, the Liyue subregion around Mt. Yaojun, with significant numbers of tea trees planted around the village. It has docks. The vale is humid compared with the Hills of Barsom.

The village borders Fontaine. Fontaine imports tea via Lumidouce Harbor, so the village feeds a trade line that crosses the sea. Yilong Wharf, the vale's trading port, lies in the same Upper Vale.

Places: The Chunming Teaworks is the best-known workshop: it combines methods passed down for thousands of years with the newest tea-drying and roasting machines, and its reputation extends well beyond the village. The Yanshang Teahouse employs an evaluator and hired muscle, and the docks have a handful of workers.

After the quest The Roaming Abode and a one-day wait, a blue flower appears behind a house in the north-east; interacting with it yields a Soulscent Bloom artifact.

People: Ding Sr. and Ding Jr. work inside the Chunming Teaworks and Jin stands outside it. Hanquan (hired muscle) and Qianyun (evaluator) work at the Yanshang Teahouse. Other residents include Grandpa Lu, Uncle Luo, Leong, Moyan and Muli; the researcher Djarkutan is also in the village. Fujin, one of the vale's adepti, and Lingyuan appear here at times.

Zhiqiong was once commissioned to map the village's terrain for a construction project that was later shelved. She remarks that the village smells strongly of tea and mentions one particularly skilled tea maker, whom she calls "the old man".

Culture: Tea is life here. Cultivars named in canon include Dipped Dew, Tianheng Bohea, Qiaoying floral tea, Sunglo Tea and Single-Origin Yauwan Tea. The village performs an annual tea-serving ceremony, using the wilted petals of Spiritscent Flowers to prepare floral tea.

Chenyu Vale lore holds that Fujin planted the first tea tree in the vale. The tree is said to thrive there because it remembers a promise between two friends, which is why this type of tea grows well only in Chenyu Vale.

History: Chenyu Vale's first human settlements were founded some 6,000 years ago by tribes fleeing the Chasm, guided by Fujin. Its tea later became famous in Liyue Harbor and elsewhere. Qiaoying itself is described mainly through its tea trade.

In 4.4, the adeptus Lingyuan, yearning for the vale's old state, tampered with its spirit lines. The soil and water were tainted, Qiaoying's tea fell in quality and miasma erupted in places. The Traveler calmed Lingyuan, and Fujin spent most of her remaining power restoring the tea; she was left stuck in carp form, and some miasma remained.

Qiaoying features in Lantern Rite events (limited-time). In The Exquisite Night Chimes, at Hu Tao's request, Zhongli collected tea seed oil and sesame oil here because they could not be found around Liyue Harbor. In Vibrant Harriers Aloft in Spring Breeze (4.4), the Traveler and Paimon came to Qiaoying and met Navia and Clorinde on a nearby mountain top, where hikers like to shout after the climb, and locals tolerate it. Zhongli's 2023 birthday mail has him returning to the village to relax and reflect with friends.

Atmosphere: Tea fragrance carried on mountain breezes, terraces of tea trees, Hui-style roofs and the sound of leaf-roasting. The 4.4 showcase described spring sun, wind and the Spiritscent Flower drifting together through peaceful streets.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Qiaoying is peaceful, with its tea quality restored.

Fujin remains in carp form after the repair, and some miasma lingers elsewhere in the vale.

239.content: A tea-processing workshop famous well beyond Qiaoying Village. It uses millennia-old methods alongside modern machines for drying and roasting, which may explain the village's renown. Ding Sr. and Ding Jr. work inside.

240.comment: Qiaoying Village: The Chenyu Vale Taint
240.content: Lingyuan, a suanni who preferred the wilds and longed for how the vale used to be, tampered with the spirit lines. The tainted soil and water degraded Qiaoying's leaves and set miasma loose. The Traveler stopped her after a fight, and Fujin spent her power to restore the tea but could not clear all the miasma.

241.content:
Qingce Village (also: Qingce, Mt. Qingce, Mount Qingce): Qingce Village is a tranquil village at the foot of Mt. Qingce in Bishui Plain, at Liyue's northern edge, with clear water and terraced fields of flowers. Many younger residents have left for livelier places such as Liyue Harbor, so it has become something of a retirement spot. It is led, in all but title, by Granny Ruoxin.

According to legend, the serpent god Chi once nested here before Morax slew it and sealed its power. "Qingce" is said to be an ancient name of the Chi itself.

Geography: Houses are simply built, mostly of wood with blue roofs, on terraces cut into the mountain. The mountain is described as cradling the village and its croplands. Crescent-shaped water paddies sit between hills and bamboo forests, with cloud banks in the valleys, and the wind makes the paddy water ripple in many colours.

Local specialties include Cor Lapis, Glaze Lily, Jueyun Chili, Qingxin and Violetgrass. The area is home to slimes, Treasure Hoarders and, near the ruins, Ruin Machines.

Places: The community centre is where Granny Ruoxin is found. Ms. Bai owns the mill, Pops Kai a tea shop and Master Lu the Fanmu Carpenter shop, and there is a market. The Qingce Village Bulletin Board carries local posts. The Vault of Qingce lies hidden to the north-west.

Geo statues stand scattered around the village, especially to the west, which Granny Ruoxin names as the spot where the Geo Lord crushed the Chi. Some glow. They are said to bear Morax's likeness and, together with orange adeptus amber, help suppress the Chi's power.

People: Granny Ruoxin is the community leader and not an official village chief; the name stuck. Others include Little Liu, Little Xing, Little You, Little Zuo and Little Yi, Pops Kai, Master Lu, Ms. Bai, the herb gatherer Zhi, Hanfeng, Jiangcheng, Dongdong, Chang the Ninth and Uncle Ghast.

Granny Ruoxin grew up in Liyue Harbor and acted at the Heyu Tea House. She moved toward a life at Mt. Qingce with an adventurer who left on an expedition and never returned. She no longer hopes so much for his return as for his happiness. She asked the villagers, on the bulletin board, to help the ailing Jiangcheng with his fieldwork.

Governance: There is no formal village head. Ruoxin says she has done a village chief's work for so long that people call her that, and the old tend the fields and look after grandchildren so younger family members can work elsewhere.

Culture: Village life is gentle and slow, with food and water in plenty. The elderly raise their grandchildren while the young work in Liyue Harbor and beyond.

Ruoxin plays Genius Invokation for relaxation, not to win. At the Lantern Rite event Fleeting Colors in Flight (limited-time), she invited Yun Jin to perform opera in the village.

History: Thousands of years ago the Chi made its nest on Mt. Qingce and seized the region. Morax fought it at a great height and killed it, but its power seeped into the land, so he subdued each aspect of it in turn: spirit, bones, flesh, soul and form, bound in different directions. He taught the villagers to erect Geo statues to crush what remained. The magic formula of the Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula is said to have bound it.

An inscription in the village says the Chi did not entirely perish and that three statues were used against it. In the quest The Chi of Yore (1.0), a self-styled researcher named Yan'er pursues the Chi's rumoured corpse; the Traveler gathers three fragments (pictographic carvings from before writing), enters the Vault of Qingce and finds treasure but no trace of the Chi.

Local belief says the Blood-Fed Trees grew from the Chi's blood and mark its eyes, while the terraces are its scales. Zhongli denies the mountain's origin in the Chi's body: Mt. Qingce stood long before the Chi ravaged it. During the Unreconciled Stars event (limited), Ruoxin says some villagers had fallen asleep and could not wake after the meteorites came down.

Atmosphere: Gentle, sleepy and nostalgic: cloud-filled valleys, terraced paddies, elders chatting, and young people absent. Inside the village life is slow but warm.

Dangers: Slimes, Treasure Hoarders and the Ruin Machines of the ruins near the village; the Ruin Hunter guarding them blocked even Yan'er.

Quests: The Chi of Yore (World Quest, Bishui Plain) is the main story; Granny Ruoxin also features in the Lantern Rite events Fleeting Colors in Flight and Unreconciled Stars (both limited).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Qingce Village is quiet, mostly elderly, and unchanged by recent main-story events.

Granny Ruoxin still lives in the village. The Chi remains a legend that few still remember.

242.content: Ruoxin leads Qingce Village's community centre. She grew up in Liyue Harbor, was an actress at the Heyu Tea House alongside Fan Er'ye, and came to the countryside seeking a simpler life. She wonders whether her lost lover would like the village and has stopped waiting, although she says she does not regret their love. She is kind, wry, and enjoys gossip and Genius Invokation. She is a gentle storyteller who remembers things most people have forgotten, like the old tale of the Geo Lord suppressing the Chi.

243.comment: Qingce Village: The Chi of Qingce
243.content: The Chi was a serpent god or dragon-like monster of Mt. Qingce, defeated by Morax. Its power seeped into the land afterward. Morax subdued it facet by facet, spirit in the north, bones south-east, flesh north-west, soul north-east, form south-west, and taught villagers to raise Geo statues. The Vault of Qingce, with a glowing orb and treasure rooms, contains no sign of the beast.

244.content:
Qingxu Pool (also: Qingxu's Forsaken Tower): Qingxu Pool is a ruined site in Lisha, Liyue: stone towers and pavilions standing around a rocky outcrop in a shallow pool. Legend says an evil god once ruled a city here, that the city was drowned under water until the Archon War ended, and that the ruins were exposed as the tides withdrew. Five hidden Geo seals guard a Nameless Treasure, and an underground ruin below plays a part in a Yelan story quest.

A nearby settlement is the home of Tieshan. The ruins have attracted treasure hunters, the Liyue Qixing and the Fatui.

Geography: A subarea of Lisha whose ruin entrance stands in the middle of a giant rocky outcrop rising from a shallow pool, surrounded by steep cliffs and several stone towers set among the natural scenery. Local specialties: Cor Lapis, Noctilucous Jade and Qingxin. The viewpoint, Qingxu's Forsaken Tower, describes a ruined tower amid a verdant field that still guards a bygone age.

Roald's diary (volume 8), written on the westward road from Mt. Tianheng, calls it a ruin known locally as Qingxu Pool and says legends hold it predates the Geo Archon's rule over Liyue. The area is home to hilichurls, Treasure Hoarders and Abyss mages.

Places: The ruin entrance on the outcrop; five pavilions with Geo seals; a stone tablet; the underground ruins reached only during a story quest.

The tablet reads that Rex Lapis walks among us and Liyue is secure, and that to mark the work of the forebears he left five seals within pavilions; later visitors must retrace the ancients' path and acknowledge it to win their treasure. Using Geo on all five seals opens a Luxurious Chest at the tablet with a Nameless Treasure inside.

History: Legend, as Roald records it, says the ruins were left by an evil god whose name has been wiped from the record and by that god's people. The self-serving god was defeated and the city submerged until the end of the Archon War, then exposed as the tides withdrew. Roald heard this from Soraya, a scholar from Sumeru he met at Wangshu Inn.

Whether the evil god is the Geo dragon Azhdaha, who rampaged across Lisha before Rex Lapis and three adepti sealed him in The Chasm, is unclear. The Nameless Treasure here is one of three whose carvings tell of that sealing, along with those at Lingju Pass and Dunyu Ruins.

The Liyue Qixing once approved an excavation of the ruins for rumoured buried treasure, but the ruins were completely sealed and the technology to blast through solid rock did not yet exist, so the project was dropped. Rumours persisted, and the Fatui agents in Liyue chased the treasure, to the diplomat Yusupov's annoyance.

People: No one lives in the ruins, but Tieshan comes from a settlement around the area; he says his home is Qingxu Pool, not the city.

Quests: Hidden in Nameless Treasures (the five-seal puzzle) and, in Yelan's story quest Calculated Gambit, the Qingxu Pool Underground Ruins quest domain.

Calculated Gambit (Umbrabilis Orchis Chapter, Act I, Version 2.7): Uncle Tian, the Tianshu, is choosing a successor, and Yelan assesses the candidates. The candidate Zhiyi's manifesto includes a Qingxu Pool Redevelopment Plan. Yelan realises it is a front for Fatui infiltrators in the Blackcliff Forge, who want to use the Forge's secret explosives to break into the sealed ruins and take whatever treasure is there. In Foregone Conclusion, the final part, she and the Traveler follow the Fatui diplomat Yusupov and Zhiyi into the underground ruins and capture them, though Zhiyi betrays Yusupov first.

Dangers: Hilichurl berserkers and shooters, Treasure Hoarders, large Dendro slimes, Abyss mages and Blazing Axe Mitachurls.

The underground ruins in Foregone Conclusion are a story-only instance with hilichurls, Pyro Abyss mages, Blazing Axe Mitachurls, Geovishap Hatchlings, sliding walls, fire orbs, lamps and elevators; Yelan joins as a trial character.

Atmosphere: Mist clears from cliffs in the morning; stone towers blend into the scenery. Roald found it calm and unperturbed by the development of Liyue Harbor, and thought the ruins perhaps left as a reminder of an earlier age for the adepti and other gods.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the pool is unchanged. The Fatui's excavation plot ended with Yusupov and Zhiyi's capture in Version 2.7, and no later story content was found that alters the ruins.

245.comment: Qingxu Pool: Qingxu Pool Redevelopment Plan
245.content: In Yelan's story quest the proposal to redevelop Qingxu Pool was Zhiyi's manifesto item, pushed with Fatui backing, to use the Blackcliff Forge's secret explosive recipes to break into the sealed underground ruins. Yelan saw through it, and Zhiyi was exposed.

246.content:
Qingxu Pool Underground Ruins (also: Underground Ruins of Qingxu Pool, Qingxu Pool treasure vault, Qīngxū-pǔ Dìxià Yíjì): The Qingxu Pool Underground Ruins are old chambers beneath Qingxu Pool in Lisha, Liyue, reached through a workers' entrance left over from an abandoned excavation. Rumour says treasure lies below. In the 2.7 Story quest "Foregone Conclusion" the Liyue investigator Yelan and the Traveler follow the conspirators Zhiyi and the Fatui ambassador Yusupov down here and expose them.

The site is the dramatic climax of Yelan's quest chain, not a place anyone visits in ordinary life. Qingxu Pool itself is a monster-infested ruin field that most people avoid, which is exactly why the conspirators chose it.

Geography: A stone labyrinth under Qingxu Pool: lifts and gates, flooded passages, sliding walls, rooms with grooves for water, and statues that can be pushed onto light spots. Part of it is a construction workers' emergency access route, built when the earlier excavation was attempted. The deepest chamber is a hidden room used as a meeting place.

The way down is blocked by water and a sealed gate rather than a single door. Lamps fed by fire orbs lower the water, and once water runs into the grooves the statues light up and can be moved to open the final door. The quest domain uses this as a puzzle, but within the story it is simply how Yelan's party gets past the workers' sealed route. Yelan warns that the ruins are a labyrinth and she cannot promise safety underground.

History: Legend, as relayed by the Qingxu Pool wiki, says the ruins predate the Archon War: an evil god ruled the city, was defeated, and the city lay underwater until the war ended. The Liyue Qixing once approved a dig for the rumoured treasure, but the ruins were sealed and the technology to blast through the rock did not exist, so the project stopped. Many groups, including the Fatui, never gave up on the rumour.

Later, the Qingxu Pool Redevelopment Plan, proposed by the Tianshu candidate Zhiyi, was a cover. In Yelan's investigation (Calculated Gambit), Fatui agents had infiltrated the Blackcliff Forge to learn its ruin-grade blasting recipes, so that they could blow through the floor at night and take whatever lay beneath.

Quests: In Foregone Conclusion (2.7), Yelan announces Zhiyi as her pick for Tianshu to lull him, has him followed, and learns that Yusupov has left the Fatui embassy alone for Qingxu Pool. Yelan leads the Traveler to a workers' entrance. Below, they overhear Zhiyi drinking with Yusupov and admitting he poisoned his teacher, Uncle Tian, using a slow-acting poison delivered in fish soup. Zhiyi then poisons Yusupov's wine, intending to burn the evidence and collapse the ruins with explosives, with Yusupov's undercover agents shut in the next room. Yelan and her Millelith appear before he can light it. Zhiyi tries to talk his way out, then is taken away. The next morning the physician Baizhu confirms Uncle Tian's poison is gone, with recovery expected to take time.

Zhiyi planned to pin the loss of the Fatui agents and Yusupov on a rogue Fatui operation to steal the Forge's explosives, then cancel the redevelopment plan himself and stand as a clean Tianshu. He also arranged with Yusupov's second-in-command Theofan, who supplied the poison, to tie up loose ends. Yelan photographed the whole scene with a Kamera as evidence. She says she will make Zhiyi an offer rather than let him face the worst outcome, warning that the Fatui will not treat a traitor kindly if they learn what he did.

Zhiyi had been given Snezhnayan poison by the Fatui and adapted it into a slow-acting one, hidden in fish soup, to dose Uncle Tian. Yusupov had told him that a commoner could only reach the Tianshu post by shining in its darkest moment. Yelan's rebuke is that Uncle Tian trusted Zhiyi most and would have given him the chance anyway.

Dangers: Fire-throwing Pyro Abyss Mages, hilichurl fighters and shooters, a Blazing Axe Mitachurl, young Geovishaps and a Stonehide Lawachurl guard the route, according to the domain page. Water and collapse are further dangers; Zhiyi's explosive charge would have buried everything.

Atmosphere: Dim stone halls, dripping water and the glow of fire orbs; behind the sealed gate, the clink of cups and a quiet, self-satisfied conversation that the party overhears.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins have not been revisited in story content found for this entry. The explosives were removed by Yelan's people, and the treasure, if any, is still not proven to exist.

247.comment: Qingxu Pool Underground Ruins: Qingxu Pool Redevelopment Plan and the Blackcliff Forge Plot
247.content: The Qingxu Pool Redevelopment Plan was Zhiyi's proposal while competing for the Tianshu post. Yelan judged it a guise: Fatui infiltrators placed inside the Blackcliff Forge could use its explosives to open the sealed ruins and take the rumoured treasure. Yusupov, the Fatui diplomat in Liyue, was irritated that the treasure hunt took attention from his diplomatic work. Zhiyi planned to cancel the plan after eliminating Yusupov, to look innocent.

248.content:
Qingyun Peak (also: Moon Carver's Abode): Qingyun Peak is the home of the adeptus Moon Carver, one of the great peaks of Jueyun Karst in Minlin. He appears as a stag, a disciple of Rex Lapis and, according to a tablet at the foot of the steps, the kindest of all the adepti. His abode is sealed from the world, and high above the peak a small island of Plaustrite called the Dwelling in the Clouds floats, reached only by solving a puzzle.

Moon Carver is the first adeptus the Traveler meets in Jueyun Karst in the Archon Quest.

Geography: Qingyun Peak is a tall, cloud-ringed mountain in the adeptal highlands of Jueyun Karst. A stone staircase leads from the teleport waypoint up to a monument at the top. At the foot of the steps are tablets and a censer; the winding path east of the peak leads to another tablet.

Above the peak, floating in the sky, is the Dwelling in the Clouds. The peak is one of the three summits of the three-cranes puzzle; the other crane statues are at the top of Mt. Aocang and on the sharp peak of Mt. Hulao. The adventurer Roald, climbing the precipice, found a sea of clouds, a few oddly shaped trees and Lapis Gledes crying overhead, and a bitter wind at night.

A tablet on the main road to Qingyun Peak, in Jueyun Karst, speaks of walking to the changing tide and the misty shroud before ascending to sit and gaze at the unfurling clouds.

Places: - The foot of the steps: tablets, one reading "Black clouds too shall pass, just as silver linings end", and a censer where the Traveler meets Moon Carver.
- Moon Carver's abode: a sealed cave past the censer behind a barrier.
- The stairs and the Three Cranes puzzle, ending at the Dwelling in the Clouds.

A second tablet near the Plaustrite steps reads: "Moon Carver, disciple of Rex Lapis. The kindest adeptus amongst all, in the manifestation of a stag." A third on the winding road east speaks of a southern shortcut and urges those seeking mysteries to watch the tides of the seas above and below.

The Dwelling in the Clouds carries a message from Cloud Retainer saying she built it as a private sanctuary, that the adepti used it to seek ultimate truth in seclusion, and that now Taishan Mansion is sealed they have returned it to her. She intends to travel again, starting with Guili Plains.

People: Moon Carver, a stag adeptus; in human form he appears as Houzhang, a middle-aged man with a streak of olive green in brown hair. Qilang, an herb gatherer, can be found on the peak. The Millelith pursued the Traveler here in the Archon Quest.

Mountain Shaper of Mt. Hulao is a frequent companion; the two travel together in several Lantern Rite events. Cloud Retainer, whose creation floats above the peak, lent Moon Carver a Multi-Purpose Abode Cleaning Talisman that he has still not returned.

Culture: Jueyun Karst is considered sacred and mortals rarely climb here. The Qingyun tablets praise Moon Carver and carry short verses about the view above the changing weather.

A tablet reads that "Come sun or rain, all seems the same from the heights of Jueyun Karst." The Three Cranes tablet speaks of "the one who may ascend" as the one who kowtows atop three mountains, with the sun, moon and stars each shining and three divine birds sending auspicious signs.

History: Moon Carver was among the adepti Morax gathered to fight in the Archon War. He and Mountain Shaper are two of the three adepti who helped seal the dragon Azhdaha.

When Rex Lapis was apparently killed, Moon Carver was the first adeptus to hear the Traveler's account, and was furious that the Qixing had accused outsiders without proof. He later helped the Millelith fight Osial and agreed to let mortals govern Liyue.

The Dwelling in the Clouds was created by Cloud Retainer for reflection, and Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper later persuaded her to lend it to the adepti for the trial of "heaven", with Rex Lapis' approval.

Atmosphere: Remote and windy, above a sea of clouds, with stone steps and tablets leading toward a sealed cave. At night the wind above the clouds is cold and relentless, in Roald's account.

Dangers: Slimes, Treasure Hoarders and whopperflowers roam the peak's paths. The adepti dislike intruders; the Millelith that followed the Traveler here were driven off.

Travel: From Qingyun Peak's waypoint, a staircase climbs to the monument. The puzzle that opens the way to the Dwelling in the Clouds is solved by finding three shining crane statues and turning them to face the monument.

Quests: - An Impromptu Change of Plan (Archon Quest, 1.0): the Traveler shows a Sigil of Permission to Moon Carver, who drives off the pursuing Millelith and sends them on to Mountain Shaper, Cloud Retainer and Xiao.
- The Three Cranes puzzle and "No Honor Among Thieves" (Qingyun Peak version) are world content here.

Lantern Rite events (2.4, 3.4, 4.4, 5.3, 6.3) feature Moon Carver with Mountain Shaper; in 4.4 and 6.3 they appear in the city, using the aliases Houzhang and Jiehu in the first of these.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Qingyun Peak is still Moon Carver's mountain. No content from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes it.

Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper still keep their peaks. Xianyun, the Cloud Retainer, lives in Liyue Harbor but retains care of the Dwelling in the Clouds.

249.content: Moon Carver is an adeptus with a stag form; his tablets call him Rex Lapis' disciple and the kindest of the adepti. The Traveler met him when fleeing the Millelith with a Sigil of Permission; he was enraged by Rex Lapis' apparent death and the Qixing's treatment of foreigners. In later Lantern Rites he is often seen with Mountain Shaper and wears a human form as Houzhang, a man with olive-green hair streak.

250.comment: Qingyun Peak: The Dwelling in the Clouds
250.content: A small floating island of Plaustrite above Qingyun Peak. Cloud Retainer made it as a place for meditation and later agreed, at Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper's urging and with Rex Lapis' approval, to let it serve as the heavenly trial for those who sought the adeptal path, building a small pavilion on it. The word "Jadevoid" for an adeptus' dwelling comes from it. As few can follow the path now, it is back in her care. It is reached by turning three crane statues to face the monument at the top of the stairs, which opens wind currents and platforms.

251.comment: Qingyun Peak: Moon Carver at Lantern Rite
251.content: At the 4.4 Lantern Rite, Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper took human forms as Houzhang and Jiehu and came to Liyue Harbor, hoping to find Cloud Retainer who had moved there as Xianyun. They overheard her and the Traveler discuss kite-making and were recognised by Paimon after they recounted shared memories. Later they flew a Fontainian-motor kite near Mt. Aocang and lost it, then played Treasure Hoarders at Xianyun's request in a staged attack meant to help Gaming and his father Yip Tak resolve their differences; Gaming saw through it, and the plan still worked.

252.content:
Qiongji Estuary (also: Qiongji, Qióngjī-yě): Qiongji Estuary is the quiet eastern coastal area of Liyue where the Bishui River reaches the sea. Its heart is the Guili Plains, once the center of the Guili Assembly, the ancient civilisation that the gods Guizhong and Morax ruled together before the Archon War destroyed it. Around them lie Mingyun Village, an emptied mining hamlet, Luhua Pool with its bright terraced ponds and two watching statues, and the Yaoguang Shoal's gentle shallows.

The land is open and still. Most of what happened here is now only ruins, tablets and legend.

Geography: Flat plains, ponds and shoreline in eastern Liyue. The Bishui River's second arm (the one that does not end near Dawn Winery) flows through Qiongji Estuary into the Sea of Clouds. Yaoguang Shoal lies south of Mingyun Village and east of Guili Plains. Guili Plains lies near Liyue Harbor, reached by the road that runs through the Mt. Tianheng range north of the city.

At its height the Guili Assembly was said to spread a thousand miles with Stone Gate as its northern boundary; by in-game measurement the Plains lay at its heart, with the edge of Jueyun Karst to the west and the end of Mingyun Village to the east.

Places: Guili Plains: ruins of the old Assembly, with Jade Plates and stone tablets. Mingyun Village: a ghost of a mining village with three small mines. Luhua Pool: a "unique landscape" of brightly colored pools watched by two giant statues. Yaoguang Shoal: a shallow, sandy shoal.

Three mining tunnels near Mingyun Village yield Iron Chunk, Noctilucous Jade and Cor Lapis. Yaoguang Shoal was named, in the local tongue, after the bioluminescent creatures that once swam ashore after dusk like fallen stars; lovers took them all and the sight is gone.

People: Almost no residents. Mingyun Village's inhabitants moved west toward Liyue Harbor and the Chasm when the ore ran out. The adventurer Zhiqiong was born in Mingyun Village and recalls its mines fondly.

Governance: None specific. Under the Guili Assembly the gods Guizhong and Morax, supported by other gods and adepti, ruled the region.

Culture: The Assembly's people took up agriculture; farming towns appeared throughout the area. Guizhong and the adepti built the Guizhong Ballista on Mt. Tianheng, and her four commandments were to teach with wisdom, be bound by virtue, fortify the bones and unite in ambition.

The name Guili comes from the first character of Guizhong's name and the "li" in Morax's name at the time, and the plain is also called the Plains of Returning and Departing. Luhua Pool's viewpoint text calls its site the Weeping Garden, a place where, legend has it, a deep, pure affection filled an ancient garden and made the pool.

History: When Morax first came down, much of western Liyue was under the sea; he lowered the tides and raised Mt. Tianheng. Guizhong later joined his settlement north of the mountain with her people, and together they built the Guili Assembly. About 3,700 years ago, in the Archon War, Guizhong was slain in a battle that laid waste to Guili Plains and Dihua Marsh; a great flood followed, and Morax moved his people south of Mt. Tianheng to found Liyue Harbor.

The Assembly was a prosperous civilisation with highly advanced engineering, supported by gods such as Marchosius and by the adepti. Its capital area is described as a once-thriving city where a certain flower bloomed abundantly, an earthly paradise consumed by war. The Assembly is gone, but the Liyue Harbor that replaced it endures.

Mingyun Village's mines dried up several years ago, and its people left. Hilichurls moved into the abandoned facilities.
