Atmosphere: Wide plains with silent ruin tablets, the bright colors of Luhua's ponds, a quiet shoal where the glow once was, and, at Mingyun, the empty houses of a village whose ore ran out.

Dangers: Hilichurls have moved into Mingyun Village. In the quest Luhua Landscape, Abyss Mages guard the ruin entrance at Luhua Pool and spiders lurk inside.

Travel: The Plains lie near Liyue Harbor; Mingyun Village sits at the Assembly's old eastern edge, with Yaoguang Shoal south of it. The Bishui River's mouth is here.

Quests: World quests include Luhua Landscape (an artist's paintbrushes and a pair of statues), The Tree who Stands Alone (Mingyun Village), Guili Plains Treasure Hunt and Troubles Traveling Through Tributaries, among others.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Qiongji Estuary is a quiet, nearly empty coastal region, with the Assembly's ruins untouched.

No Qiongji-specific events appear in 6.x-7.1 content.

253.comment: Qiongji Estuary: The Guili Assembly and Guili Plains
253.content:
The Guili Assembly was an ancient civilisation in Liyue founded and ruled by Guizhong, God of Dust, and Morax, God of Geo, with Marchosius the God of the Stove and the adepti in support. Its center was the Guili Plains, which Liyue Harbor's founders tried to expand into before Guizhong died. The Plains' viewpoint text, "Ruins of Guili," calls it a thriving city where a flower bloomed in abundance, consumed by war so that its people scattered again.

Guizhong was kind-hearted and wise though not especially powerful, and she loved mechanisms: she and the adepti, Cloud Retainer among them, built the Guizhong Ballista on Mt. Tianheng. Texts say she died in a destructive battle that also wrecked Dihua Marsh, and a flood followed.

254.content: Mingyun Village is home to several scattered mining deposits, but most have dried up and the few remaining ores cannot sustain the village, so its people have left for Liyue Harbor and the Chasm. Hilichurls now use the leftover facilities. The adventurer Zhiqiong was born here and remembers its mines with fondness.

255.comment: Qiongji Estuary: Luhua Pool and Yaoguang Shoal
255.content: Luhua Pool is a unique landscape of brightly colored pools overlooked by two statues, with ruins hidden beneath. A legend says a deep, pure affection filled the ancient garden here and made the pool. Yaoguang Shoal, south of Mingyun Village and east of Guili Plains, is named for the bioluminescent sea creatures that once appeared after dusk like fallen stars swimming to shore; they are now gone, taken by lovers, though the shore may still have things to give.

256.content:
Ridge Watch: Ridge Watch is an ancient ruined site at Stone Gate, in the mountains where Mondstadt and Liyue meet. The domain description likens it to a boundary marker looking north and south, over mountain and river. Those who endure its trial can win artifacts.

It is a domain of blessing, so its place in the world is as a ritual and proving ground, not a settlement.

Geography: Ridge Watch stands at the start of the ridge in the Stone Gate area of Bishui Plain, on the mountainous route linking Mondstadt and Liyue. The in-game blurb describes ancient city ruins that overlook both north and south.

Legend, according to the domain text, holds that its gates and blessings open only to those whose hearts are lit with an eternal blaze, a theme echoed by its Pyro-heavy defenders.

Atmosphere: A stern, wind-swept stronghold of old stone. The text speaks of toughness of spirit and body and of not fearing pain: whoever conquers the trial gains the protection of the ritual site and the power to pursue far-off dreams.

Dangers: The domain is guarded by Pyro slimes, hilichurl berserkers, fire-wielding Mitachurls and Geovishap. Its Ley Line Disorder (a gameplay effect) sends backlash shockwaves at attackers who strike a shielded character, which is why the levels are all titled "Unyielding".

The artifact sets offered are Tenacity of the Millelith, Pale Flame, Brave Heart and Martial Artist (gameplay detail). The game gives no formal tie between the Millelith and these ruins.

History: No named historical event is attached to the ruins. Their apparent role as a boundary watchpost is an impression from the domain text, not a stated fact.

Status as of 7.1: Added in 1.5 and unchanged as of 7.1.

All four levels carry the same Ley Line Disorder, and the later levels advise shield or Crystallize support; this is gameplay guidance, not story. The domain's recommended levels scale from 59 to 90.

key: Roots of the Valley of Life
257.comment: Roots of the Valley of Life
257.content:
Roots of the Valley of Life: The Roots of the Valley of Life (an unofficial name) is a point of interest in The Chasm's Main Mining Area, in Liyue. The hidden exploration objective Seed from the Valley of Life takes place here.

Climbing the branches on the tree's southern side lets the player enter a Mine Passageway to Sumeru, near a mushroom growing on the tree.

Travel: The passageway is a shortcut between the underground mines of Liyue and Avidya Forest in Sumeru. The pages consulted give no in-world explanation of how it came to exist.

Its far end opens beside the waterfall under the Statue of The Seven near Gandharva Ville in Avidya Forest. The tree lies in the Main Mining Area of The Chasm: Underground Mines.

The wiki lists this crossing as one of several Mine Passageways (it appears as location 4 in its gallery of passageway contexts).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is simply an explorable site and travel link; no lore beyond the hidden objective is given.

258.content:
Sal Terrae (also: Salt of the Earth, Salt Temple, Havria's domain, Of Mysteries and Salt): Sal Terrae is a salt-crusted ruin on the Bishui Plain in Liyue, the last sanctuary of Havria, the gentle God of Salt, who refused to fight in the Archon War and gave her people shelter. Her own king killed her with a sword and the city turned to salt. Today a sealed domain holds her remains, a single salt flower, and the broken sword. It is the setting of the first act of Zhongli's story quest.

Since 5.7 the surface ruins also host Stygian Onslaught, a recurring ley line disturbance that the Millelith sealed off and the Traveler helps quell.

Geography: A low plateau of ruined walls and sunken foundations beside the Bishui River. Roald's diary says most of the ancient city sank into the riverbed, leaving the temple's foundation. A sealed ruin lies beneath, guarded by a stele reading that salt seals the ruin within and none uninvited may enter, and opened by Geo, Electro and pressure-plate mechanisms. Local specialties include Cor Lapis, Noctilucous Jade and Violetgrass; the nearby area holds Hilichurl camps and a Stonehide Lawachurl.

Windmill mechanisms and pressure plates mark puzzle spots. Inside the sealed ruin, statues made of salt line the corridors, and the last chamber ends in an open hall.

People: No residents now. Wanyan, of Yinyuan Hall, who in fact reveres Havria, and Kliment, a Fatuus archaeologist, entered the ruin with Zhongli; Treasure Hoarders had already looted much of the surface.

Culture: Havria's people honoured a goddess of kindness who handed out flowers as a blessing or comfort; Liyue's Flower Ball custom is said to have come from this. Her relics were a chalice that never ran out of salt and a ruler that turned land to salt for harvest, plus the broken sword of her death.

Yinyuan Hall, the trade hall for salt, descends from survivors who fled to Morax's Liyue Harbor.

History: Havria was a weak, gentle god who refused to fight in the Archon War and instead conceded land after land to other gods, finally settling in a tiny holding at Sal Terrae. The city stood for centuries until its first and last king killed her with a sword. Her body dissipated into a salt flower (the "sal flore") and her released power turned everyone nearby into salt. A few outside the blast fled to Liyue Harbor.

Descendants, afraid of a curse, returned to break the sword and lay it, with two of her relics, on a pedestal in the sealed chamber before resealing the ruin. Over millennia Yinyuan Hall's story drifted until it said Morax murdered Havria out of jealousy; Wanyan's "expedition" with Zhongli was an attempt to prove this. Zhongli, who is Morax, told the truth, took the ruler and later cast Havria's relics into the sea at Guyun Stone Forest, saying he must find a better way to keep the truth of history.

Atmosphere: White crust on stone, the smell of salt, dry wind off the river and a silence broken by gears and the occasional echo in empty halls. Inside, salted statues of people caught in their last gestures make a sad, unsettling gallery.

Dangers: Hilichurls with Pyro and Electro bows; the Stonehide Lawachurl; a Fatui Pyro Agent (Kliment) in the sealed ruin; Pyro Abyss Mages in the sealed ruin; and, during Stygian Onslaught, powerful bosses spawned by the disturbance.

Quests: "Sal Flore" (Zhongli's Historia Antiqua Chapter, Act I): "Shadow of Yore", "Vortex's Wake", "A Ruin Under Lock and Key", "Farewell, Sweet Salt" and "A Record of All Things". The domain is "Of Mysteries and Salt". "Tumult Subduer" (5.7) opens Stygian Onslaught.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the sealed ruin is open, the relics are gone, and the surface hosts the recurring Stygian Onslaught disturbance. No new Sal Terrae canon appears in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

259.comment: Sal Terrae: Havria, God of Salt
259.content: Havria was a gentle god of the Archon War era, weak in power, who fled the fighting and made countless concessions to protect her followers. Her relics were a self-refilling salt chalice and a ruler that turned land into salt. Her kindness is the reason she could not defend herself against her own king. See her entry for her story.

260.comment: Sal Terrae: Zhongli and the Sal Terrae expedition
260.content:
Zhongli accompanies the archaeologists Wanyan and Kliment in return for a contract that each may claim one item in turn. Kliment breaks it out of greed over the chalice and Zhongli subdues him; Wanyan, exposed as a devotee of Havria hoping to blame Morax, learns that the sword before her was the murder weapon. Kliment is a Fatuus who claims to be registered with Liyue's Ministry of Civil Affairs.

Zhongli believes Havria could not have cursed those she loved, and perhaps accepted her people's plan to end her life as a mercy. He tells the Traveler afterwards that as Rex Lapis he had always written history himself, and that this incident made him want a better way to preserve it.

261.comment: Sal Terrae: The salted ruin and Roald's diary
261.content: Roald's diary records the folk version: the God of Salt gave shelter to those displaced by the war; the king, who had once loved her too, killed the lone god to show that gentleness did not suit the times; the temple fell and the city crumbled to salt; the king's end is unknown. Rumours say her body, turned to salt, still holds the posture from the moment she was struck.

262.comment: Sal Terrae: Stygian Onslaught at Sal Terrae
262.content: Since 5.7, a strange ley line disturbance appeared at Sal Terrae. The Adventurers' Guild reported many monsters and the Millelith sealed the area; the world quest "Tumult Subduer" (needs Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue finished) sends the Traveler in, with Keqing and Yelan involved, and unlocks Stygian Onslaught.

key: Realm of Resounding in Sea and Living in Rosy Clouds
263.content:
Sea Gazer's Abode (also: Abode of Sea Gazer, Realm of Resounding in Sea and Living in Rosy Clouds): Sea Gazer's Abode is the hidden treasure house of Sea Gazer, an adeptus of Liyue who died long ago, located in the Lisha area. Abandoned and forgotten, it still runs on adeptal energy, which keeps its guardian mechanisms and the monsters inside active. It appears only in the Interlude quest Seagaze Sunset (Version 2.4), when the Traveler, Paimon and Shenhe enter it to fetch a huge piece of Sunset Vermillionite for the rebuilding of the Jade Chamber.

The abode is a quest domain, a pocket space reached through a waterfall once Shenhe lifts the adepti art that conceals it. Inside, false clouds hide the lower levels and the party must break the mechanisms keeping the illusion up in order to descend.

Geography: The entrance is hidden around Lisha and is revealed when Shenhe performs an adepti art that turns the weather rainy and removes the concealment; a Seelie then leads the party to a waterfall, which is the way in. Inside, the abode is three levels: floating islands above a sea of clouds, a lower cloud-wrapped level, and a deepest level with a pool of water, a maze of movable stone walls and Seelie courts.

The clouds are not real: Shenhe explains they are an adepti art used for spatial partitioning, held in place by mechanisms called Ancient Array Cores. Once a core's guardians are beaten it can be destroyed and the party drops to the next level, the last fall ending in a pool of water. The rocks and trees look incomplete from above, which is what first makes Paimon suspect something lies beneath the clouds.

Places: The first level has east and west Geo Lamps, each tied to a Geogranum, and a central island; activating them opens a wind current to glide on and raises Plaustrite platforms. The second level is another core arena. The third holds the water pool, a deactivated Ruin Guard, a maze of four stone walls that must be pushed in the right order, a final core, and the Seelie courts, beyond which a bridge leads to the Sunset Vermillionite.

The wiki lists Shenhe as the domain's trial character and recommends Cryo, Geo and Pyro elements; these are game-mechanic notes, not lore.

People: Nobody lives in the abode and its builder, Sea Gazer, is long dead. The party inside consists of Paimon and Shenhe, who knows adepti arts and whose master is Cloud Retainer.

Sea Gazer was an adeptus, a skilled explorer and collector who kept his rarest finds here. He had been very close to Mountain Shaper. Cloud Retainer later recalls that he was usually mild-mannered but quite a braggart when showing off a new discovery at Guizhong's gatherings at the Guili Assembly.

History: According to Xingqiu, citing the book "Records of Drifting Clouds", Sea Gazer built the abode to store his rarest and most exquisite treasures, among them Sunset Vermillionite. After he died the abode was abandoned and its location was lost to time. Xingqiu worked out that it lay in Lisha by cross-referencing a stack of folk-history books that make oblique references to it.

The Jade Chamber is being rebuilt, and Ningguang has opened a contest to gather the materials, of which Sunset Vermillionite (the Plaustrite that lifts the structure) is the hardest to find. The Feiyun Commerce Guild holds one piece for auction, which Xingqiu expected to sell for over 500 million Mora, so he pointed the party to the abode instead. Paimon worries that taking a dead adeptus' treasure is disrespectful; Shenhe says Sea Gazer would not have minded, on the strength of a rumour only.

Dangers: Because the abode is abandoned, its adepti defences treat visitors as intruders. Ancient Array Cores release pulses that deal Physical damage, and each is protected by waves of monsters (slimes of several elements, hilichurls, Mitachurls, a Lawachurl, a Geovishap and Ruin Guards, per the domain's enemy lists). An inactive Ruin Guard on the lower levels awakens and smashes the ground during the descent.

The falls between levels are part of the way down; the party survives the last drop only because a pool of water breaks it.

Travel: Entry requires removing the concealing adepti art at the marked spot in Lisha and then following the Seelie to the waterfall. Within the abode movement is by gliding on wind currents, using Plaustrite platforms and pushing stone walls.

Quests: Seagaze Sunset, part 2 of Act I (The Crane Returns on the Wind) in the Interlude Chapter, is the only quest set here. After Xingqiu's briefing at the Feiyun Commerce Guild, the party reaches the abode, descends through its levels and finds the huge Sunset Vermillionite. Shenhe lifts it alone and carries it to the Jade Chamber worksite, where Ningguang's secretary Baiwen rates it the finest Plaustrite received so far and says it will go into the Jade Chamber's foundation.

Afterwards Shenhe admits she is fatigued from the abode, accepts a rest at a makeshift hotel run by Ju'an, and Cloud Retainer arrives the next day.

Atmosphere: A cloud-bound pocket world: floating weathered stone, ancient mechanisms humming with leftover adeptal power, the sound of water, and a small Seelie drifting ahead as a guide. It feels grand and lonely, the private treasure room of a collector left to rust and monsters.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the abode is a finished quest location. Its treasure, the Sunset Vermillionite, was removed in 2.4 and is meant for the Jade Chamber's foundation.

The wiki lists no later appearance, and nothing in canon through 7.1 says what became of the remaining defences or the second Seelie in the court. Its builder remains dead and only sparsely described.

264.comment: Sea Gazer's Abode: Sea Gazer's Abode (Seagaze Sunset)
264.content:
The abode is where the Traveler and Shenhe find the Sunset Vermillionite for the Jade Chamber: a hidden treasure house of the dead adeptus Sea Gazer in Lisha, with cloud-veiled levels, Ancient Array Cores, movable stone walls and a guiding Seelie.

Sea Gazer was a close friend of Mountain Shaper, and Cloud Retainer and Guizhong would answer his boasts about new finds with mechanical creations of their own. A Mingxiao Lantern in the Lantern Rite event The Exquisite Night Chimes was modelled after him, which is limited-event material.

265.content:
Sea of Clouds (also: Cloud-Coming Sea, Yunlai Sea): The Sea of Clouds ("Cloud-Coming Sea") is the southern coastal area of Liyue and the nation's gateway to the world. It holds Liyue Harbor, the great trading city where "a thousand ships" drop anchor and goods from all seven nations change hands under contract; the mountain barrier of Mt. Tianheng that shelters the city from the west; and the island spires of Guyun Stone Forest, where Rex Lapis is said to have pinned a sea god. Its Geo boss is the Geo Hypostasis.

The area is Liyue at its most public: crowded wharves, banks and guilds, and a cliff-backed city under the watch of the Qixing and Millelith. Beyond the quay, the sea is old and quiet around the stone islands.

Geography: Coastline, harbor and mountains in one view. Liyue Harbor sits on the sea with Mt. Tianheng rising to its west and north, making a natural shield; the road north leads out to Guili Plains and the Bishui River's mouth. Out on the water lies Guyun Stone Forest, an archipelago of seven large islands.

The Bishui River flows through Qiongji Estuary into the sea nearby. The northernmost island at Guyun houses the Geo Hypostasis, and the southwestern island holds the Domain of Guyun. Mt. Tianheng reaches north of the city too: the range along the road to Guili Plains belongs to it.

Places: Liyue Harbor has three districts: Feiyun Slope, the prosperous merchant district at the northern entrance; Chihu Rock, the lower-class district on an island to the southeast; and Yujing Terrace, the wealthy cliffside residential quarter in the west. Above the city floated the Qixing's Jade Chamber. Guyun Stone Forest lies offshore.

The Jade Chamber was lost in the battle with Osial (Archon Quest Chapter I) and later rebuilt; it is the airborne seat of the Liyue Qixing and the home of Ningguang. Feiyun Slope includes a Snezhnayan merchant area with Northland Bank.

People: Merchants, ship owners, sailors, miners, guild clerks, Millelith soldiers, scholars and shopkeepers fill the harbor. The ruling Liyue Qixing and Ningguang oversee trade. Foreign merchants, including Snezhnayans and Fontainians, are regular sights.

Governance: The Liyue Qixing, a council of seven, run the harbor with the Millelith as their army, under what the nation calls a rule of contracts. Rex Lapis, the Geo Archon, founded it but handed rule to the mortals; Zhongli, who is Rex Lapis in a mortal life, now lives among its people.

Culture: Liyue Harbor is a city of contracts, ceremony and festivals; the best known is Lantern Rite, when thousands of lanterns rise into the night. Guyun is considered more a vista than a destination, and its reputation as a "forest of tombstones for the old gods" keeps most locals away.

Liyue folk tell the battle differently, but all agree Rex Lapis used the sacred lance Vortex Vanquisher to pierce Osial's rainbow and pin him in the deep sea; Beidou's character story calls the tale of the sea-monster victory a beloved one.

History: Before the Archon War, Rex Lapis led his people south of Mt. Tianheng and founded what is now Liyue Harbor. They tried to extend the city to Guili Plains, but after Guizhong died in the war they came back to the harbor. In the same war Rex Lapis defeated the sea god Osial at Guyun and pinned him to the sea floor with stone spears, whose broken remnants are the jagged cliffs there.

Mt. Tianheng's lore says a clash between Morax and another god nearly toppled it, until the adeptus Skybracer had his antlers, a gift of Morax's power, cut off and wedged under the peak, then fought on until he died. Liyue's earliest mines are believed to have begun in these hills. In the Archon Quest Chapter I the Fatui Harbinger Childe unleashed Osial, who shattered the Guizhong Ballistae and was defeated only when Ningguang dropped the Jade Chamber on him.

Zhongli later threw Havria's relics into the waters at Guyun in the story quest A Record of All Things, calling it a homecoming, and told Osial that their ancient grudge was a bygone memory. The Mt. Tianheng legend is also tied to the Bishui River's origin.

Atmosphere: Quays, ships and crowded markets in the city, with the road in through Mt. Tianheng arriving suddenly in a trade capital; offshore, the lonely silence of the stone islands, where the sensitive are said to hear a strange stirring rhythm deep in the ocean.

Dangers: The Geo Hypostasis holds the northernmost Guyun island. Fatui agents have operated in the city. Anyone who sleeps at Guyun may relive Osial's defeat.

Travel: Roads lead north to Guili Plains and the Bishui country and east toward Qiongji Estuary. Ships dock at the harbor from every nation.

Quests: The area hosts a large share of Liyue's world and story quests, notably the Archon Quest Chapter I Act III (Heart of Glaze), Zhongli's story quest, and Lantern Rite events.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Liyue Harbor is thriving and the Qixing still govern; the Jade Chamber has been rebuilt.

Rex Lapis lives on as Zhongli. The 7.1 anomaly of the Celestial Nails is centered on the Chasm, not the harbor.

266.comment: Sea of Clouds: Osial and Guyun Stone Forest
266.content: Osial, the Overlord of the Vortex, was an ancient sea god who clashed with Morax in the Archon War. At Guyun Stone Forest Rex Lapis pinned him to the sea floor with stone spears, and the jagged cliffs there are the remnants of those lances. Osial could raise tsunamis as tall as Liyue's mountains. In Archon Quest Chapter I the Fatui unleashed him to lure out Rex Lapis and steal his Gnosis; Ningguang crushed him with the Jade Chamber. Locals call Guyun a forest of tombstones for the old gods.

267.comment: Sea of Clouds: Skybracer and Mt. Tianheng
267.content: Mt. Tianheng shields Liyue Harbor from the west. In a Lantern Rite telling, during the Archon War an enemy god's blow nearly toppled the peak onto a village at its foot, so the adeptus Skybracer had his antlers chopped off and wedged under the mountain, raising it higher. He fought on until his lifeblood ran out, and that blood became the Bishui River.

268.comment: Sea of Clouds: The founding of Liyue Harbor
268.content: Before the Archon War, Rex Lapis brought his people south of Mt. Tianheng to found Liyue Harbor. They later tried to move the city out to the Guili Plains, the central area of the Guili Assembly ruled by Guizhong, God of Dust, and Morax, but after Guizhong died in the war they returned to the harbor. The harbor launched Liyue's seafaring trade and is called Teyvat's largest market harbor.

269.content:
Second Life (also: Second Life shop, Rongfa Shangpu, 荣发商铺): Second Life is a small general goods shop in the main plaza of Chihu Rock, Liyue Harbor. Its owner, Dongsheng, is a former adventurer who left the road after a serious accident in Dihua Marsh, where a masked adeptus rescued him. He named the shop to remember that day.

It sells ordinary cooking ingredients such as salt, pepper, onion, milk, rice and tofu, and its stock is refreshed daily. The wiki says that high Liyue reputation earns a discount.

Places: One shop on the plaza of Chihu Rock, open day and night.

People: Dongsheng runs the shop. He used to be an adventurer who travelled everywhere, and has stayed put since being rescued. He calls his current life a simple one, and says the life he has was given to him by the adeptus.

He is also seen in a Yun Jin hangout memory image set at the shop, according to the wiki.

Culture: The shop's name plays on a Liyue adage, 'a withered tree lives again', which Dongsheng uses for the idea of a life given back. The Chinese name takes the last part of the saying, meaning something like '(re-)flourishment'.

Asked about the shop, Dongsheng is happy to tell the story, but does not press it on anyone and says it is best not to raise old matters when a visitor declines.

Atmosphere: A modest corner shop where the owner is polite and unhurried and the slogan is plain: satisfaction guaranteed.

Travel: In the central plaza of Chihu Rock in Liyue Harbor.

The shop's Chinese name, Rongfa Shangpu, is explained on the wiki as commemorating the rescue, drawing on the idiom 'kumu farong'; Japanese and Korean names use the same idiom.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

270.content: Dongsheng is the owner of Second Life. A former adventurer injured in Dihua Marsh, he was rescued by a masked adeptus, after which he stopped travelling and opened a shop. He tells the story only to customers who ask.

271.content:
Spiritstone (also: the Chasm Nail, Wishstone): The Spiritstone is the Celestial Nail at the bottom of the Chasm in Liyue, a vast sky-blue crystal pillar. It was sent from the heavens to purify Abyssal corruption in the ancient civilisation of Lang-Gan. Zibai held it back long enough for many of Lang-Gan's people to flee, and its impact is said to have made the Chasm.

Geography: The nail hangs high in the Court of Pillars, the deepest point of the Chasm: Underground Mines, a vast cavern of old stone and glowing crystal. A viewpoint note attributed to Zhiqiong calls it a huge sky-blue crystal pillar that could only have come from the heavens, whose shade it shares. A crater surrounds the point of impact. A fragment, called the Wishstone, was found in the Stony Halls.

A luxurious chest sits on top of the nail. After the events of the Chasm Delvers the nail floats lower than before, and the platform beneath it was struck by its fall.

Places: Wishstone site (Stony Halls): where miners touched a fragment and began seeing their desires granted.

Court of Pillars: the cavern where the main body hangs, with five crystal mechanisms that feed into the nail.

Space beneath the nail: during the limited-time Perilous Trail event (2.7), the Chasm's Bed lay under it. See the Chasm's Bed entry.

History: Celestia sent the nail to purify the Abyssal taint in Lang-Gan. In the Realm of Rocks cinematic (Lantern Rite event, Luna IV) Istaroth tells Zibai that all places tainted by the Abyss must be purified and that this includes Lang-Gan. Zibai, who was a god of Lang-Gan, replies that she will die among its people. She raises a canopy of jade light under the falling nail, buying time for people to escape. Istaroth catches her as she falls and splits her soul into three. The survivors went on to Chenyu Vale, where their descendants live today, according to the wiki.

Quests and item texts say the nail's impact formed the Chasm. The Zibai quests (The Realm of Clouds, The Realm of Rocks) are part of the limited-time Lantern Rite event A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon.

Wishstone: in modern times, a fragment found in the Stony Halls gave miners hallucinations in which their desires were granted. Lumenstone and Lumenspar began appearing in large numbers, the Chasm's mines seemed to shift as if alive, and the Dark Mud of the Abyss emerged. Lumenstone repels Dark Mud. The Liyue Qixing therefore closed off the Chasm and sent investigators.

Atmosphere: A cathedral-like cavern, cold and silent, where a pale blue pillar hangs overhead. The nail seems to belong to another place entirely.

Dangers: Abyssal power once bound the nail, and the beings guarding it are Abyss Mages, an Abyss Herald and Khaenri'ahn rifthounds. The Khaenri'ahn Ruin Serpent Haftvad the Worm emerged when the Traveler released the nail.

Travel: Reached only by descending through the Chasm: Underground Mines, beyond the gate Zhiqiong identified near the camp. The Qixing had closed the Chasm after the Wishstone's effects on the miners.

Quests: Wherefore Did the Spiritstone Descend? (2.6), part six of the Chasm Delvers world quest series. The Traveler purifies five crystal mechanisms with a charged Lumenstone Adjuvant, drawing out Haftvad the Worm. Yelan shoots the nail with a Hydro-infused arrow, dropping it onto the serpent and subduing it, after which it floats back up lower than before.

Perilous Trail (2.7), a limited-time event with its own Archon Quest Interlude, sent Traveler, Paimon, Itto, Shinobu, Yanfei and Yelan into the space under the nail. Yelan said she had shot the nail because it is highly effective against remnants of Khaenri'ahn civilisation.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the nail still hangs in the Chasm. The sources read do not record any Spiritstone-specific change from 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

272.content:
The Spiritstone is the Celestial Nail in the Chasm, sent to purify Abyssal corruption in Lang-Gan. Zibai held it back so more of Lang-Gan's people could flee. Miners found a fragment, the Wishstone, which showed them their desires; Lumenstone repels the Abyss's Dark Mud that came with it.

In the Chasm Delvers the Traveler purified the nail's crystal mechanisms, drew out Haftvad the Worm and, with Yelan, crushed it under the nail.

273.comment: Spiritstone: The Realm of Rocks (Zibai and Lang-Gan)
273.content: Cinematic in the Lantern Rite event A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon. Istaroth tells Zibai that Celestia will purify Lang-Gan and that her guilt is unnecessary. Zibai chooses to shield her people; the nail's fall is delayed, and Istaroth splits Zibai's soul to preserve it. This is limited-time event content.

274.content:
Stone Gate (also: Shimen): Stone Gate is the roadside crossroads in Liyue's Bishui Plain where the roads from Liyue Harbor, Qingce Village, Dawn Winery and Dihua Marsh meet. Its bulletin board greets travellers as arriving at "the door of Liyue": south to the bustling port, north to the rustic wine country of Mondstadt. It is a place for tea, gossip and a few stay-behinds rather than a settlement with its own government.

The Ridge Watch domain, ancient city ruins that overlook the ridge between Mondstadt and Liyue like a boundary marker, lies in the area.

Geography: The junction joins the road to Dawn Winery in the northeast, to Wuwang Hill and Qingce Village in the northwest, and to Dihua Marsh and Liyue Harbor in the south. Ruins, a windmill mechanism and hilichurl camps stand among the hills around it.

Local specialties are Cor Lapis, Dandelion Seed and Jueyun Chili. Ridge Watch's own text describes it as standing over the start of the ridge, looking both north and south, mountain and river.

Places: The Stone Gate Bulletin Board carries travellers' notices: a welcome as the door of Liyue, a note about a purple-clad young woman from Yujing Terrace asking locals about their daily needs (evidently Keqing), a swordsman's admittedly bad poem, a hypermarket advert for Dihua Marsh, and praise for Pops Zhou's tea. Ridge Watch, a domain of ruined walls, is nearby.

People: Pops Zhou sells cheap tea at the gate; a friend of forty years says it has never declined or improved. Aunt Qiao knows the stall holders and is asked to mind their stalls. Huachu and Jianqiu sit drinking his tea. Zhuyu, an herb gatherer, and his wife Qinglian are found south of the gate towards Dihua Marsh.

Huachu is the second daughter of Gentry De'an of the Minghua Company; her father disapproved of Jianqiu, an arithmetic teacher, so the two faked her death in Liyue Harbor and settled quietly at Stone Gate. Jianqiu claims to be the Minghua Bank's assistant shopkeeper, unaware the bank has been sold. During a Lantern Rite festival (limited-time event) they visited the Harbor's outskirts and ate at the Emerald Maple Inn. Zhuyu was once a sailor and became an herb gatherer to care for Qinglian when she fell ill; he does not know she is only pretending to be ill so that he will stay with her.

Atmosphere: Quiet and breezy: travellers resting at the tea stall, the occasional merchant passing, hills with windmills and old ruins.

Dangers: Hilichurls and samachurls, slimes, Whopperflowers and Fatui skirmishers roam the surrounding ground, with Abyss Mages, Geovishap Hatchlings and Mitachurl shield-bearers as tougher threats. The road itself is generally safe.

Travel: Two Teleport Waypoints lie nearby. It is the natural stop for anyone walking between Mondstadt and Liyue Harbor.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Stone Gate is an ordinary roadside stop; no later canon changes it.

275.content: Lovers who eloped and now stay at Stone Gate. Huachu, daughter of the Minghua Company's Gentry De'an, and Jianqiu, an arithmetic teacher from Chihu Rock, are said to have left a corpse dressed as her in the Feiyun Slope well to fake her death, which led De'an to sell off the Minghua Bank to pay for the funeral. Huachu's bulletin note speaks of a hoped-for new home far away under the Geo Archon's protection.

276.content:
Stony Halls: The Stony Halls are rugged rock chambers in the Chasm's Underground Mines in Liyue. Dark mud and oozing concretions coat the stone, lumenlamps give light, and Abyss Mages hold the halls.

Its Chinese name reads as "Rugged Stony Hall", which suits the uneven chambers.

Geography: Features here are Dark Mud, Lumenlamps, Oozing Concretions and Ruin Braziers. It is a subarea of the Underground Mines beneath the Chasm.

Neighbouring subareas of the mines include the Ad-Hoc Main Tunnel and the Main Mining Area. The wiki page gives no description or history for the halls themselves.

Dangers: Common foes are Geo Slimes; the elite foes are an Electro Abyss Mage and a Pyro Abyss Mage, both Abyss Order casters.

The mage encounters make the halls a place where the Abyss presence in the Chasm is most obvious; see the Chasm and Chasm Delvers entries for the wider context.

Atmosphere: Uneven halls of stone lit by lamp glow, with dark mud on the walls and the flicker of Abyss magic. This is a suggested scene mood drawn from the feature list, not a quoted description.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1.

277.content: The Underground Mines open after the world quest Surreptitious Seven-Star Seal Sundering in the Chasm Delvers series. Their subareas include the Stony Halls and the Ad-Hoc Main Tunnel.

278.content:
Taishan Mansion: Taishan Mansion is a Domain of Mastery near Jueyun Karst in Liyue that grants Character Talent materials. Its description says people who sought the way of the adepti once had to pass the trials of heaven and earth, and Taishan Mansion was the trial of earth; now the adepti have left this realm, it is a common treasure trove.

A tablet above the mansion says it was established by royal decree, but the Geo Lord wanted his home to remain among the people of Liyue, so every trace of the path to that divine place was lost in the mortal world. Its hidden treasure is now engulfed in water, and the tablet adds that people should leave at the sight of the adeptus.

The tablet is canon text on the environment, not a full history. It does not say who the decree came from, when the mansion was built, or whether any adeptus still visits.

Gameplay detail: the domain uses Adventure Rank 25 to 45 and recommended levels 38, 54, 71 and 88 across four levels. Level IV pairs two Blazing Axe Mitachurls with Fatui Pyro Agents, with a limit of 480 seconds. Smoldering Flames at level IV is far stronger than at I to III.

Geography: The domain sits in Jueyun Karst, the cloud-ringed peaks in northwest Liyue that are said to be where the adepti live. Waypoints stand to the southwest of the mansion and west toward Guili Plains. The mansion's entrance is under water until a puzzle is solved.

Solving the puzzle: defeat the three waves guarding a glowing monument by the steps, start it to partly drain the water, then guide Geograna to light three stone lanterns around a second monument; this drains more water and exposes the entrance.

Dangers: Gameplay rules, labelled as such: the ley line disorder periodically inflicts Smoldering Flames on your character, causing Pyro damage until the Pyro is removed. Enemies are Pyro slimes, Blazing Axe Mitachurls and Fatui Pyro Agents. Recommended elements are Hydro, Cryo and Electro.

Rewards depend on the weekday: Prosperity, Diligence and Gold teaching series, from the Altar of Flames, Heart of the Flames and Circle of Embers levels.

Atmosphere: Scorching heat, mist burning off the walls, and the weight of a place built for people who came looking for immortals.

Status as of 7.1: Permanent and unchanged as of Version 7.1.

279.comment: Taishan Mansion: Jueyun Karst and the adepti
279.content: Jueyun Karst is considered the realm of the adepti and is usually out of reach of mortals. Herb gatherers make a living collecting valuable resources there, and the official exploration text calls the area unsuited to outsiders and best viewed from Wangshu Inn.

280.content:
Teatree Slope (also: Old Tea Tree Slope): Teatree Slope lies in the southern mountain of Chenyu Vale, south of Qiaoying Village and north of Yaodie Valley. It was once part of the Herblord's land and is where the adeptus Fujin planted the vale's first tea tree, which still grows there.

The tree is the ancestor of the tea that made Chenyu Vale known in Liyue Harbor and elsewhere.

History: Long ago the vale belonged to its unnamed mistress, who was served by the snake-spirit adeptus the Herblord and the golden-carp adeptus Fujin. Fujin, who was fond of humans, planted the first tea tree in the Herblord's territory. Later its branches were grafted across the river by mountain dwellers and its tea grew famous. The tea is said to thrive only in Chenyu Vale because the tree remembers a promise between two friends.

During the Archon War the mistress sent the Bishui River in flood against Morax. Fujin and the Herblord turned against her: the Herblord fought their former master and went missing, while Fujin threw the Votive Rainjade into the water and was later trapped at Carp's Rest. In the present Fujin asked the Traveler to restore the vale's spirit lines when its tea was tainted.

Places: The slope's viewpoint is titled "Ancient Pact". The old tea tree is the focal point.

Atmosphere: A quiet mountain slope above tea country; humid, green and calm.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tree still stands; nothing after 4.4 changes it.

281.comment: Teatree Slope: The first tea tree
281.content: Accounts of the first tea tree come from item texts and Baizhu's Character Story: it was planted by Fujin on the Herblord's land, someone later tied a jade ornament to the sapling, and the pact between two friends is said to be why its tea thrives only here. The tea banquet promised for all the adepti was never held, and the Herblord's own fate is unknown.

282.content:
The Chasm (also: Yu Valley): The Chasm is a vast mining region on Liyue's western coast. A huge pit of layered, whorled cliffs sits above a maze of underground mines rich in ore and jade. In the cataclysm 500 years ago monsters poured out of it, and the Millelith and the Yaksha Bosacius died sealing them in. A few years ago the Liyue Qixing closed the mine after strange accidents. Since the Traveler's expedition (2.6) it has been reopening. A blue-glowing Celestial Nail, the Spiritstone, hangs in its depths.

Revealed in 6.3: the Chasm was once Lang-Gan, an ancient civilisation governed by the angel Zibai. A Celestial Nail sent to purge Abyssal taint buried it, and survivors fled to Chenyu Vale. In 7.1 the Spiritstone began emitting a strange light along with every other Nail in Teyvat, and Liyue now watches the Chasm closely.

Geography: Two levels. On the surface is a giant bowl of stratified rock with spiral terraces, odd-coloured soil and plants, scaffolding and old mine works. Its areas include The Chasm's Maw (the mine entrance, with abandoned miners' quarters), Glaze Peak, Tiangong Gorge and Cinnabar Cliff. Below lie the Underground Mines, an unlit labyrinth of tunnels and caverns reached through the Maw and other shafts, under the Qixing's "Seven-Star Array" seal. Ancient texts sometimes call this underground the "Yu Valley".

Underground subareas include Stony Halls, The Glowing Narrows, the Nameless Ruins (inverted ancient buildings around an upside-down pool) and the Court of Pillars, where the Spiritstone hangs. The ecologist Khedive believes perfectly preserved marine fossils deep in the mines show that the whole area was once seabed and was transformed in an instant. Fluorescent plants thrive below, and a withered tree like those at other Nail sites grows near Stony Halls.

Places: - **The Chasm's Maw**: the main entrance to the mines, with abandoned miners' quarters and an emergency notice ordering the miners to disperse.
- **Cinnabar Cliff**: the surface area with the Statue of the Seven. In 7.1 Xiao keeps watch here.
- **The Spiritstone** (the "Chasm Nail"): a huge sky-blue crystal pillar floating in the Court of Pillars, a Celestial Nail.
- **The Chasm's Bed**: a predatory sealed space beneath the Nail.

- **Stony Halls**: where miners found the "Wishstone", a fragment of the Spiritstone.
- **Nameless Ruins**: an underground "palace" exposed when the surface was damaged in the cataclysm, probably a remnant of the civilisation the Nail destroyed.
- **Exploration camp**: the Chasm Exploration Team's base underground.
- A relic of Rex Lapis's ancient battles stands on the surface, with a notice warning visitors not to disturb it.

People: Muning, a Ministry of Civil Affairs specialist, runs the site from the camp at the mine entrance. He handles miners' return to work, Millelith rotations, contracts and endless weekly reports. Millelith guards such as Tie Hong hold the approach. The Chasm Exploration Team includes Zhiqiong (adventurer and cartographer), Khedive (ecologist), Jinwu (safety technician), Taliesin (bard) and Clitopho (a former Treasure Hoarder turned demolitions expert). After the expedition it became an official part of Huishan Hall.

Muning's family is prominent in Shenglu Hall and the porcelain trade. Zhiqiong grew up in Mingyun Village, whose mines ran dry. Driven to be remembered, she vanished into the depths after leaving a farewell letter. Yelan descends from the cataclysm-era thaumaturges Boyang and Rongzhao. In 7.1 Xiao watches the Chasm on Rex Lapis's orders.

Governance: The mine belongs to Liyue and is administered by the Liyue Qixing through the Ministry of Civil Affairs, with the Millelith on guard. After a notice put the question to the Yuehai Pavilion, the Qixing halted all mining. They sealed the depths with the Seven-Star Array and let in only those with permission from Yujing Terrace or a special commission. The Qixing first agreed to let the Fatui investigate, but cancelled the deal after the events of Chapter I and ran their own investigation.

Economy: The Chasm is Liyue's most famous mine. Its specialities are Cor Lapis, Noctilucous Jade, Qingxin and Violetgrass, and its glazed sand crystals go into porcelain. The closure put many miners out of work. Reopening is slow, with work resumed in stages, recruitment notices posted, and the Feiyun Commerce Guild involved.

Lumenstone, a catalytic stone that blazes with light in the mines but loses its power once taken out, appeared along with the Nail fragment. Refined into the Lumenstone Adjuvant, it drives back the Abyssal Dark Mud. Dragonfall, a rare ore said to have formed when Morax and Azhdaha fought here, was "mined into obscurity" centuries ago.

History: In the age of the unified civilisation the land was Lang-Gan, a civilisation of mountain settlements built around mines. Its people worshipped Zibai as the God of Soil and Grain and offered to the Three Moons at a jade altar. After the war of funerary flame tainted Lang-Gan with the Abyss, the Heavenly Principles sent a Celestial Nail to purify it. Against Istaroth's advice, Zibai held the Nail back long enough for her people to escape, and it killed her. The impact buried Lang-Gan and carved out the Chasm. Survivors went east to Chenyu Vale and are suggested to have reached the Guili Assembly too. Liyue's people later mined the Chasm. During the cataclysm 500 years ago an "iron meteorite" struck, and Khaenri'ah's monsters poured out. Morax sent the Millelith to defend the region and evacuate the miners. They, the maddened Yaksha Bosacius and the thaumaturge Boyang drove the monsters into a space beneath the Nail and sealed it with the Fantastic Compass, sealing themselves in as well.

About two years before the Traveler's expedition (according to the Millelith guard Tie Hong), an incident deep in the caverns led to the closure. Miners at Stony Halls had found the Wishstone, a Spiritstone fragment that showed people visions of their desires. Lumenstone appeared, the mines shifted as if alive, earthquakes struck and black ooze spread, so the Qixing closed the Chasm. A Fatui device sent in to deal with the ooze exploded. In 2.6 the Traveler broke the Bedrock Keys of the Seven-Star seal with the exploration team, cleared the Dark Mud and purified the Spiritstone, which had been bound by Abyssal power. This roused Haftvad the Worm, a Khaenri'ahn Ruin Serpent. Yelan shot the Nail down onto it, and the Nail rose again, though lower than before. The earthquakes stopped and the ooze began to recede. In 2.7 (*Perilous Trail*) the Traveler, Yelan, Yanfei, Itto and Shinobu fell into the Chasm's Bed, met Xiao there searching for Bosacius, learned the fate of the sealed vanguard, and escaped with Zhongli's help.

Legend also claims a "Solar Chariot" fell here in the war of funerary flame. A broken-off piece formed the Dunyu Ruins, and the main body leapt back into the sky in the Archon War. Some say Morax and Azhdaha fought here. In the wiki's account, mining that disturbed the ley lines tormented Azhdaha, and Morax, Mountain Shaper, Moon Carver and another adeptus fought him down into the depths. Shortly before the 6.3 Lantern Rite, a civilian dig funded by Huishan Hall turned up Lang-Gan relics. Zhongli later explained that strange phenomena in Lang-Gan's former domain had brought back Zibai's "Earthly Soul", which led to her restoration at the 6.3 Lantern Rite.

Atmosphere: On the surface: ochre cliffs, wind, abandoned scaffolding, cranes and minecarts, Millelith patrols and Treasure Hoarders keeping out of sight. Below: total darkness broken only by Lumenstone, glowing plants and Abyssal ooze, groaning rock, old Khaenri'ahn machines, and the sense that the place is watching you. Viewpoint notes left by Zhiqiong capture the awe of first seeing the Nail.

Dangers: Cave-ins and sheer drops, poisonous gas, Dark Mud that spreads Abyssal corruption, Abyss Mages and Heralds, rifthounds and riftwolves, Ruin Machines and the Ruin Serpent, Geovishaps, Fatui skirmishers, and Treasure Hoarders who sneak in for loot. The Chasm's Bed is the worst of all. It distorts space and time, reads minds and turns fears into illusions that can attack, and it slowly "devours" whoever stays too long.

Travel: On foot from central Liyue, past the Millelith checkpoint where outsiders are turned away. Access to the depths was via the Maw once the Seven-Star seal was broken. Miners are now kept away from the most dangerous sections.

Quests: - *The Chasm Delvers* (2.6): the expedition, the Wishstone and the Spiritstone.
- *Valor's Afterglow*: Zhiqiong's disappearance.
- *Perilous Trail* (Interlude Chapter Act II, 2.7): the Chasm's Bed, Bosacius and Boyang.
- *A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon* (6.3): Lang-Gan relics and Zibai.
- *Anomaly: Liyue* (7.1): Xiao at Cinnabar Cliff.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Chasm is a partly reopened mine guarded by the Millelith. After Ronova destroyed a Celestial Nail, every other Nail across Teyvat began emitting a strange light, the Spiritstone among them.

Rex Lapis has ordered Xiao to watch the Chasm so he can report any change at once. More Millelith have been sent to patrol, and Cloud Retainer and other adepti are investigating. Zhiqiong is still missing in the depths.

283.content:
The Spiritstone is the Celestial Nail that buried Lang-Gan: a huge sky-blue crystal pillar floating in the Court of Pillars at the bottom of the Chasm. Celestial Nails purify powers that should not exist in Teyvat, and Lumenstone and Lumenspar near it repel the Abyss's Dark Mud. A fragment, the Wishstone, was found in Stony Halls, gave miners visions of their desires and led to the mine's closure. In 2.6 the Traveler freed the Nail from Abyssal bindings. Yelan then shot it down onto the Ruin Serpent Haftvad, and it rose again, but lower.

Yelan says the Nail works well against remnants of Khaenri'ah's civilisation. The Traveler and Yelan suspect that the force of its fall weakened the old seal over the Chasm's Bed. In 7.1, after Ronova crumbled Hyperborea's Nail with Eitr, the Spiritstone, like the other Nails, began emitting a mark into the sky.

284.comment: The Chasm: The Chasm's Bed and the sealed vanguard
284.content:
Beneath the Spiritstone lies a space older than the cataclysm. It traps whatever enters, wears away the Abyss's power, and in time devours humans as well. In the cataclysm the Millelith vanguard, the thaumaturge Boyang and the Yaksha Bosacius lured the monsters inside and sealed it with the Fantastic Compass, a catalyst powered by a mortal and an adeptus together. The monsters were destroyed, and the defenders were lost with them. Xiao later confirmed there that the "Nameless Yaksha" who had returned to fight in the Chasm was Bosacius.

Inside, the space twists paths into loops, freezes hunger and fatigue and then lets them hit all at once, reads minds and builds illusions from fears and memories. The Traveler saw the Abyss and their sibling there, and an echo of Bosacius still fought on. The Traveler's group escaped in 2.7 using an illusory Fantastic Compass that the space itself produced, which responded to the combined energy of Yelan (a mortal) and Xiao (an adeptus). Xiao poured out his strength to lift them to the surface, and Zhongli caught him as he fell back. The entrance has since closed.

285.comment: The Chasm: Lang-Gan beneath the Chasm
285.content: Lang-Gan was a civilisation of the unified era on Liyue's western coast, guided by Zibai, a heavenly envoy and later Moon Envoy. She gave its first emperor-priest the longbow Yayu and taught the people silk painting, farming, spinning and weaving. Lang-Gan had no books and kept its history in ballads. Its settlements ran from peak to peak, and life centred on the mines. When the Nail fell, Zibai's sacrifice bought the people time to flee east. Lang-Gan lies buried beneath the Chasm's hills, and the vale's Chiwang Terrace copies its jade altar. In 6.3 Lang-Gan relics dug up in the Chasm went on show in Liyue Harbor, and moon poems from Lang-Gan were recited at Lantern Rite.

286.comment: The Chasm: The Qimen gate at the Chasm (5.3)
286.content: During a Lantern Rite event (5.3), Ningguang assigned Yelan to the Gate of Injury at the Chasm. Lan Yan said her grandfather remembers the Chasm's gate as the Gate of Life, back when their ancestors lived near the Chasm before moving to Chenyu Vale. Yelan told the Traveler that the Chasm was once home to the people of present-day Chenyu Vale, and that her own ancestors died fighting beside the Yakshas there.

287.content:
The Chasm: Main Mining Area (also: Main Mining Area): The Main Mining Area is the central zone of the Chasm's Underground Mines in Liyue, a dark network of shafts lit by lumenstone lamps. After a series of mysterious accidents the whole mine was closed and its miners put out of work; the Liyue Qixing are gradually reopening it.

It is entered by way of Glaze Peak and is the core ground of the exploration the Traveler joins in the Chasm Delvers series, where black "dark mud" spreading Abyssal corruption has to be cleared with lumenstone light.

Geography: A subarea of the Underground Mines, which have their own map tab separate from the main continent. Features include dark mud, oozing concretions, lumenlamps, luminous Seelie and elemental monuments. Noctilucous Jade is the local specialty.

The mines can be entered from the Chasm's Maw, Tiangong Gorge, Glaze Peak or Avidya Forest. In play they unlock at Adventure Rank 28 after Chapter I Act III and the quest Surreptitious Seven-Star Seal Sundering.

Dangers: Treasure Hoarders, Fatui skirmishers, slimes and Whopperflowers roam the shafts; elites include Pyro Abyss Mages, Geovishaps, Mirror Maidens and Rifthound Whelps.

The ground itself is hazardous: dark mud spreads corruption, and dangerous gas and cave-ins hamper delvers.

History: The Chasm began when a celestial nail fell on the ancient civilisation of Lang-Gan and buried it under the hills. In the recent past accidents closed the mine and the Qixing sealed its entrance with a Seven-Star Seal. In the Chasm Delvers series the Traveler and the Ministry of Civil Affairs' representative Muning's team break the seal's keys, open the mines, set up a camp, and finally purify a corrupted Skyfrost Nail that was the source of the dark mud.

A Millelith-and-Yaksha defence of the ore veins five hundred years ago, told by a miner at the Chasm's Maw, is the mining folk's own memory of the cataclysm.

Lang-Gan, per the wiki's reading of weapon and artifact texts, was part of Teyvat's unified civilisation, governed by the angel Zibai, whose people lived around the mines and worshipped the Three Moons. When the moons shattered in the War of Funerary Flame the land was tainted by the Abyss, and a celestial nail sent to heal it fell and turned the region into the Chasm; the nail is known as the Spiritstone. Zibai's people evacuated eastward first. These details are tied to the ancient history and are not spoken by the Chasm miners.

Atmosphere: Dim passages, glowing lumenstone and an eerie quiet, with the weight of rock overhead.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the main mining area is open to supervised exploration.

288.content:
The Chasm: Underground Mines (also: Underground Mines, Chasm Underground Mines, Yu Valley): The Chasm: Underground Mines is the dark labyrinth of mine tunnels and ruins beneath Liyue's great pit, the Chasm. Sealed by the Qixing after a string of accidents and strange tremors, it was reopened in 2.6 to an exploration team led by the Ministry of Civil Affairs. Below the working mines lie older things: Dark Mud and Abyssal corruption, a sky-blue Celestial Nail called the Spiritstone, the buried ruins of the ancient city of Lang-Gan, and hilichurls and cursed Khaenri'ahn survivors who came to the depths to shelter.

Light is the main resource down there. Explorers rely on the glowing Lumenstone and a tool called the Lumenstone Adjuvant to see and to hold back the mud.

Geography: A network of tunnels, caverns and ruins stretching down beneath the Chasm's Seven-Star Array. It has its own map tab and exploration progress, separate from the main map. Entrances include the Chasm's Maw (the main mine entrance), Tiangong Gorge, Glaze Peak and Avidya Forest.

The sub-areas include the Main Mining Area with the exploration camp, the Stony Halls, the Glowing Narrows, the Nameless Ruins (with the Inverted City hanging from the cavern roof), the Court of Pillars around the Spiritstone, and the Chasm's Bed deep below. Marine fossils preserved in the depths suggest the whole area was once under the sea and that whatever made the Chasm happened in an instant.

Places: Main Mining Area: where the exploration team set camp. Stony Halls: where a fragment of the Nail, the Wishstone, was found. Nameless Ruins and Inverted City: ruins of Lang-Gan, with an upside-down city and pool. Spiritstone: the Celestial Nail. The Chasm's Bed: a sealed, older space below.

The Chasm's Maw has an elevator down from the surface. The map text for the mines calls the place "Yu Valley" in ancient texts and warns that one should always expect the unexpected in the shafts.

People: The Chasm Exploration Team, made official as part of Huishan Hall after the incident, includes the cartographer Zhiqiong, Jinwu and Khedive, with the Ministry of Civil Affairs representative Muning on the surface. Treasure Hoarders sneak in; in the deeper ruins are hilichurls living out their last years and the Black Serpent Knights guarding them.

Governance: The Liyue Qixing seal and reopen the mine through the Ministry of Civil Affairs. Access depended on destroying the Seven-Star Seal's Bedrock Keys on the surface.

Culture: Miners' lives once centered here; the Qixing's closure scattered a workforce. A notice in Lisha says the old surface mines had run low and miners moved to the Chasm.

History: The area was the home of Lang-Gan, a unified-era civilisation guided by the angel Zibai. Abyssal taint after the War of Funerary Flame led the Heavenly Principles to drop a Celestial Nail on it; Zibai delayed the strike so many could flee east, and the Nail's impact made the Chasm. Sometime during or after the Archon War, miners disturbed the ley lines and the dragon Azhdaha, who was fought by Morax and the adepti. During the Cataclysm Abyssal monsters poured out and the Millelith and the Yaksha Bosacius fought them here.

Before the Traveler, the Qixing closed the mine two years earlier after an unknown incident, and the Fatui had tried and failed to deal with the black ooze. In 2.6 the Traveler helped the exploration team break the Seven-Star Seal, light the tunnels, blast open a rockfall and purify the Abyssal-infected Nail, calming the tremors. In the Requiem of the Echoing Depths the Traveler and Dainsleif found Halfdan and the Black Serpent Knights guarding hilichurls in the Inverted City. In 2.7 the Traveler, Yelan, Yanfei, Itto and Shinobu fell into the Chasm's Bed, where Xiao was searching for Bosacius, and escaped together.

The Perilous Trail party were saved when Xiao poured out his strength to lift them out and Zhongli caught him as he fell; Xiao confirmed the "Nameless Yaksha" at the Chasm was Bosacius, and afterwards invited the Traveler to Pervases' temple.

Atmosphere: Total darkness pierced by pale blue glow; dripping caves, hanging ruins, pools of black mud that sap strength. Deep in the Chasm's Bed the space feels outside the usual rules.

Dangers: Dark Mud, which drains energy and strengthens enemies; Dangerous Gas that explodes with Electro or Pyro; Abyss Mages and Lectors; Treasure Hoarders; the Ruin Serpent Haftvad; shadowy Black Serpent Knights lost to the Khaenri'ahn curse; and the Chasm's Bed, a looping space where hunger, thirst and fatigue vanish and then strike back, and where domains turn fears into illusions.

Travel: Enter through the Chasm's Maw from the surface, or by the other entrances after unlocking. The Qixing's seal must be broken first, and the Lumenstone Adjuvant is needed to light and navigate.

Quests: The Chasm Delvers series (2.6), including Chasm Spelunkers and Wherefore Did the Spiritstone Descend?; Archon Quest Requiem of the Echoing Depths (Chapter II Act IV, 2.6); Interlude Chapter Perilous Trail (2.7); Valor's Afterglow (Zhiqiong); Paleontological Investigation in The Chasm and other investigations.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the mines are partly reopened and watched: Millelith patrol, Xiao keeps watch for the Nail anomaly, and Zhiqiong's whereabouts remain unknown.

In 7.1 the Nail of Retribution at the Chasm, like others across Teyvat, began to glow; additional Millelith patrol and Cloud Retainer and other adepti are investigating, and Rex Lapis (Zhongli) had Xiao monitor the site.

289.comment: The Chasm: Underground Mines: The Chasm Delvers expedition
289.content: The Traveler took a commission from the Adventurers' Guild and met Muning, the Ministry of Civil Affairs representative, who wanted to find out why the Chasm had been sealed. With the cartographer Zhiqiong and the team, they destroyed five Bedrock Keys to open the Qixing's Seven-Star Seal, set up camp, found missing miners, fended off Treasure Hoarders and used the Lumenstone Adjuvant to clear Dark Mud. After blasting a rockfall with a cannon, they found the Abyssal-infected Nail, purified it and ended the tremors. Muning made the team part of Huishan Hall.

290.comment: The Chasm: Underground Mines: Dark Mud, Lumenstone and the Adjuvant
290.content:
The Lumenstone Adjuvant is a tool the Traveler receives in the early mine quests; it lights the surroundings and lets the wearer open blue-sealed chests, lamps and braziers, and it recharges at waypoints, Luminous Seelie and certain lamps. Dark Mud is black ooze that drains the Adjuvant, hampers movement and makes enemies stronger; it gathers around Oozing Concretions and spreads Abyssal corruption.

Chunks of ore that seem related to the Nail were found in the mines. A sufficiently upgraded Adjuvant can destroy an Oozing Concretion, dispersing the mud around it.

291.comment: The Chasm: Underground Mines: The Inverted City and the Black Serpent Knights
291.content: In Requiem of the Echoing Depths the Traveler and Dainsleif entered the Inverted City, a ruin of an older civilisation (Lang-Gan). An upside-down pool there weakens the Khaenri'ahn curse of immortality, so hilichurls had come to live out their final years in it, protected by Black Serpent Knights, Dainsleif's former subordinates, now mindless but still obeying their last order to protect Khaenri'ah's people. One Knight, whom Dainsleif takes to be Halfdan, led them to a hilichurl camp where a Khaenri'ahn flower, the Inteyvat, showed the Traveler a vision of their sibling and an Abyss Herald planning to amplify the pool to lift the curse and restore "the homeland". Dainsleif thought it futile and the Traveler agreed to stop it. An Abyss Lector activated the device; Halfdan sacrificed himself to stall it while the Traveler destroyed the machinery, and his soul spoke briefly with Dainsleif before passing on.

292.comment: The Chasm: Underground Mines: The Chasm's Bed and Perilous Trail
292.content: In Interlude Chapter Act II, Yelan, Yanfei, Arataki Itto, Kuki Shinobu and the Traveler fell into a space under the Spiritstone where hunger and time warp, and domains turn fear into illusions. Xiao was inside searching for his missing brother-in-arms Bosacius. An illusory Fantastic Compass, a charm of mortal and adeptal power, lifted them to the surface; Xiao spent his last energy to hurl them out and Zhongli rescued him. Xiao learned the Nameless Yaksha at the Chasm was Bosacius.

293.content:
The Chasm Withered Tree (also: Chasm Withered Tree): The Chasm Withered Tree (an unofficial name) is a withered tree in The Chasm's Underground Mines in Liyue, north of the Main Mining Area. It cannot be interacted with.

Approaching it makes Paimon remark that it looks just like the strange ancient white tree on Dragonspine.

The wiki takes her comparison to refer to the white tree where the Princess' Box is found in the Dragonspine quest Dragonspine's Last Trio. The game does not say whether the trees are connected.

Further details: Identical withered trees stand on Dragonspine, on Tsurumi Island near the shore where the "Boatman" is found, and beside the central island in The Orchard of Pairidaeza, but the Chasm's tree is the only one that triggers dialogue when approached.

key: the space beneath the Chasm Nail
294.content:
The Chasm's Bed (also: Chasm's Bed, the space beneath the Chasm Nail): The Chasm's Bed is a mysterious, ancient pocket of space deep beneath the Chasm's Spiritstone. It bends space and time, reads the minds of those inside, and devours the people it traps. During the Cataclysm, Bosacius and Liyue's Millelith used it to seal away the monsters of Khaenri'ah. The Traveler and others entered it in the Version 2.7 Perilous Trail event.

Geography: A map description calls it a mysterious space beneath the Chasm that would have been exceedingly hard to reach without an accidental fall, with a way out just as unclear. It is a maze of stone caverns with spatial rifts, doors and passages that shift and close behind travellers. Its rock is extremely old Liyue Mountain Rock. In Perilous Trail it was entered through an entrance beneath the Chasm Nail, and became unreachable after the quest ended.

Breaches in the caverns close on their own, and rifts regenerate after being cut open, so no matter how many were attacked there was no way out.

Places: The labyrinth of caverns and spatial rifts; the doors that show each person what they fear; and the deeper area where Bosacius and Boyang completed the seal with the Fantastic Compass.

During the event, the entrance to the event mode Realms of Guile and War was inside the space until Perilous Trail ended, after which it moved to a spot near the Chasm Nail. This is game-structure information.

History: When the Cataclysm began, an iron meteorite hit the Chasm and the monsters of Khaenri'ah poured out. Morax sent the Millelith to defend Liyue and evacuate miners. Brothers Boyang and Rongzhao were among those ordered by the Qixing to take the Fantastic Compass, a catalyst that manipulates space, and aid the Millelith. Bosacius, already mad, was drawn by the bloodshed and fought for Liyue, mistaking the Millelith for his Yaksha comrades. The fighting exposed an underground palace, and the defenders found that monsters weakened as they went deeper. The plan was to use the compass to trap the monsters and seal them away, at the cost of a mortal and an adeptus powering it and being sealed in too. Bosacius and Boyang volunteered.

As the Millelith advanced they became limited too: breaches closed behind them, rifts regenerated, they lost track of time and tired. They used an Orichalceous Time-Dial to mark time between battles. In the end the monsters lost all mobility and were devoured, as were most of the Millelith, leaving only Boyang and Bosacius. Boyang saw illusions of his family and feared he was mad; Bosacius saw his Yaksha comrades, remembered his name and purpose, and together they used the compass to complete the seal. Bosacius died, and Boyang eventually perished too.

Centuries later (the wiki says five hundred years), Yelan shot down the Spiritstone, which she says is especially effective against Khaenri'ahn remnants. The impact may have damaged the seal. When Yelan and Itto were about to fight, their power gave the final push to open the seal, and the group fell in. Xiao entered by himself to learn if the nameless yaksha of the records was Bosacius, and later joined them.

Atmosphere: Silent, shifting stone, and a sense of being watched. The space seems to know your thoughts and will turn them into doors, voices and faces. Time loses its grip: hunger and tiredness pause, then arrive all at once. Its purpose seems to be to entrap and devour those who enter.

Characters describe it as a living thing. It targets those inside with changing illusions.

Dangers: Spatial distortion that returns walkers to the same place (Itto compares it to an Inazuman bake-danuki legend); time distortion (Paimon felt twenty days pass, Itto three to five, though one day had passed); selective fatigue; mind-reading illusions that can become real and attack, including a recreation of Bosacius as he fought; and devouring, in which prolonged stay turns a person into a shadow wandering like a lost soul. The space can also fake voices, such as the Conqueror of Demons, to lure people deeper.

The party escaped by turning the space's mind-reading against itself. They imagined the Fantastic Compass so that the space produced an illusory copy of it, which they used to open a way out. Shadowy figures pursued them during the escape. Xiao proposed to break out with all his power, but the party refused to leave him behind.

Travel: Not reachable under normal play. The entrance beneath the Chasm Nail disappeared after Perilous Trail. Whoever enters needs a way to leave, which only the illusory compass provided.

Quests: Archon Quest Interlude Act II, Perilous Trail (Version 2.7): The Unexpected Guest, Chasmic Maze, Danger All Around, End of the Line, and At Tunnel's End, Light. Realms of Guile and War was the event mode.

Perilous Trail is a limited-time event, so knowledge of the space is not universal in Liyue. The party was the Traveler, Paimon, Arataki Itto, Kuki Shinobu, Yanfei and Yelan, with Xiao joining.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the space is sealed again and inaccessible. The sources read record no later content about it.

295.comment: The Chasm's Bed: The Chasm's Bed
295.content:
The Chasm's Bed is an ancient space beneath the Spiritstone that reads minds, bends time and space and devours those who stay. Bosacius and the Millelith sealed monsters inside it during the Cataclysm with the Fantastic Compass; the space was entered again in the 2.7 Perilous Trail event.

It shows each person illusions drawn from their fears and memories, pulls them deeper through rifts, and can make the illusions real. Escape required imagining the compass so the space would create it.

296.comment: The Chasm's Bed: Boyang and the Millelith in the Chasm
296.content: Brothers Boyang and Rongzhao were sent by the Qixing with the Fantastic Compass to help the Millelith against Khaenri'ah's monsters. Boyang and Bosacius sealed the space and died inside. Yelan is said by the wiki to descend from the brothers.

297.comment: The Chasm's Bed: Escaping the Chasm's Bed
297.content: The Fantastic Compass is a catalyst that manipulates space and was used to seal the monsters. In Perilous Trail the party escaped by imagining it until the space created a copy, then used it to leave; the copy disappeared afterwards.

298.content:
The Chasm's Maw (also: Mouth of the Great Mine): The Chasm's Maw is the surface entrance to the Chasm's underground mines in Liyue. A miners' hut stands there, empty since the mine was shut, and a large memorial of rough stones honours the Millelith and Yaksha who died protecting the Chasm five hundred years ago.

The viewpoint is named "Mouth of the Great Mine". A miner called Wang prays at the memorial.

Places: The Miner's Quarters, an abandoned wooden hut, holds an emergency notice: because of sudden changes in the Chasm, all miners were to be dispersed in three days and told to send letters and parcels through the Ministry of Civil Affairs. A battered miner's helmet, the Helm of Warding, lies inside. Nearby is the Millelith memorial.

A Statue of the Seven and climbable rocks lie behind the memorial. Local specialties are Qingxin and Violetgrass; Geovishaps and Mirror Maidens are the elite threats.

People: Wang, a miner who used to work the Chasm, prays at the memorial before anyone descends. He tells the Traveler of the dark calamity five hundred years ago, when the Millelith under a Yaksha held the ore veins and some led the foe into the depths.

Wang also relays a legend: a Millelith soldier crippled in the fight became a self-taught doctor and set up the memorial after gaining a Vision, and his story became tangled with tales of a Millelith treasure. Wang does not credit the tales but says they keep history alive. In the quest The Millennial Mountains the Traveler gathers six lost offerings (Helm of Warding, Cup of Commons, Skyfeather, Warrior's Spear, Flower of Farsight and Sundial of Ages) to open the treasure.

History: Five hundred years ago a dark calamity swallowed the mines and Rex Lapis ordered the Millelith to guard the ore veins; those who died are remembered here. Much older, the Chasm itself was born when a celestial nail ended the civilisation of Lang-Gan.

The Chasm's Maw keeps the practical memory of the disaster: Wang says the fallen Millelith turned into elements and became one with the mine, so praying to them is also reverence to the Chasm itself. The Ministry's notice about dispersal and parcels shows the miners were sent off in an orderly way before the closure.

Atmosphere: Rocky, windy, with wooden huts and old stone cairns; reverent and a little bleak.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area is open and quiet.

299.content:
The Glowing Narrows (also: Glowing Narrows, The Great Mushroom's Place): The Glowing Narrows is a subarea of the Chasm's Underground Mines in Liyue, a lightless cavern passage lit by fluorescent growths and dominated by a giant talking mushroom, Xamaran. It lies deep in the mines, beyond the main tunnel, in country where black "foul energy" still seeps from cracks and the Traveler's Lumenstone Adjuvant is the main tool for clearing it.

The viewpoint text, written as if by the miner-engineer Zhiqiong, calls it the Great Mushroom's Place and records the strange calling voice she heard there. It is a quiet, eerie stretch of the mines where the only resident with anything to say is a mushroom.

Geography: A cavern passage in the Underground Mines, a separate map layer beneath the Chasm's surface. The giant mushroom sits in the southern part of the narrows, and a stream runs through the area; the source of the black foul energy lies upstream along the water, by a fissure. Luminous Seelie and fluorescent growths light the dark.

The Underground Mines are entered from the Chasm's Maw on the surface and are unlocked at Adventure Rank 28 after Chapter I, Act III of the Archon Quest and the world quest "Surreptitious Seven-Star Seal Sundering". The Glowing Narrows becomes reachable only after "Perils in the Dark", the fifth part of "The Chasm Delvers". The area's listed features are Luminous Seelie, Cryo Whopperflowers, Floating Hydro Fungus and Large Hydro Slimes, with Geovishap and Shadowy Husk (Defender and Line Breaker) as elite enemies.

People: Xamaran is the only named inhabitant: a giant glowing mushroom that speaks by releasing spores into the air, so that Paimon and the Traveler hear a voice with no mouth. It addresses people as "Two-Legs" and calls itself one of the "legless", ranking creatures by their number of legs, and it has small mushroom kin around the cave that it can no longer shelter. Paimon nicknamed it "Sheeshroom".

Xamaran says it has dwelt here many years and found the cavern a cosy home, but that foul energy has been rising lately and has drained its strength. It smells the heat of golden sand and the damp of a rainforest in the Traveler and calls that its hometown, and Paimon links this to Sumeru; the Sumeru scholar Khedive is at the exploration camp. The wiki records that Tighnari remarked it took Xamaran a long time to reach its present form.

Xamaran is more guarded about its ancestry. In the Natlan quest series Mushroom Realm Mystery (Tribal Chronicles, Act III "Field Fungal Traces", 5.5) the Traveler learns that Xamaran is an offshoot of Bifrons, the Sage-Lord of Fungi. Xamaran calls Bifrons "my foolish father", says they have had no business with each other for many years, and that it has nearly forgotten the name.

History: The cavern belongs to the Chasm's mines, which Liyue worked until a run of accidents and then a black ooze led the Qixing to seal them. Nothing in canon dates Xamaran's arrival or says who first named the narrows.

The foul energy Xamaran fights is the same Abyss-tainted dark mud (Oozing Concretions) found throughout the mines. The Chasm Delvers summary traces its source deeper still to a corrupted Skyfrost Nail-type meteorite that the Traveler purifies, after which the ooze recedes; the narrows are part of that wider story but Xamaran's quest happens alongside it rather than as part of the Archon-level plot.

Atmosphere: Dark and humid, lit by drifting spores and glowing caps. Sound carries oddly: the mushroom's voice seems to arrive from the air. Mood is more strange than threatening, until the black mud appears.

Dangers: Geovishap, Shadowy Husks, Cryo Whopperflowers, Hydro slimes and floating Hydro fungi. The dark mud and Oozing Concretions are Abyssal corruption and are cleared with the Lumenstone Adjuvant. The viewpoint text itself jokes that the strange voice could be a hallucination from poisonous gas.

Quests: "Dimming Mushroom's Call for Help" (world quest, 2.6), begun by approaching the giant mushroom after "Perils in the Dark". The Traveler lends the Adjuvant's power to Xamaran, clears three Oozing Concretions, revives five of its kin, and uses Xamaran's gift, the Blessings of Wisdom, on a fissure upstream; a mushroom grows from the fissure and blocks it. Xamaran then falls asleep. The quest also counts toward a hidden exploration objective.

Xamaran's closing words wish that no regret lingers in the night bygone and all shadows fade before dawn; afterwards it only murmurs a loop of three sayings about ignorance, knowledge and wandering.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the narrows are open and quiet; Xamaran sleeps and answers only with fragments of its aphorisms.

Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes the area. The only later canon tied to it is Xamaran's lineage, revealed in 5.5.

300.content:
Xamaran is the giant glowing mushroom of the Glowing Narrows. It speaks in an archaic, formal, third-person style ("Xamaran calls", "Xamaran begs of you") and divides living things by how many legs they use. It thanks the Traveler and Paimon as the wisest of the two-legged, lectures about hard work making up for lack of nature, and tells a joke about Paimon being eaten by mushrooms that it admits nobody found funny. Only the Traveler's help with the Lumenstone Adjuvant restores its light.

Xamaran refuses to deal with the source of the foul energy itself, calling itself legless and unwilling to meddle in the matters of the Two-Legs, and says it has a greater duty to shelter its kin. After the quest it sleeps and repeats three sayings: ignorance may be a blessing and knowledge a calamity; only the graced with knowledge flourish; only the tested by wandering brave the wilderness.

In the 5.5 Natlan content, once the Traveler has done the Natlan quest series and asks about the Sage-Lord of Fungi, Xamaran calls it its progenitor, "abounding in might, yet more bereft of wisdom" than the four-legged, and "my foolish father". It adds that it can tell no more stories about it.

301.content:
The Lost Valley: The Lost Valley is a hidden domain in Fuao Vale, within the Chasm of Liyue. It was an ancient ritual ground, and ruin machines from outside have overrun it. Defeating them yields artifacts.

Its past is told in layers: buried by cataclysm, lifted up by an alien object, then exposed by a battle born of betrayal.
