Geography: It lies in Fuao Vale, part of the Chasm. A huge golden raw-mineral rock and nearby rock pillars guard the way; the domain is revealed when a strong blow on a nearby pillar sets off a resonance quake between Geo constructs.

The entry is a Geo-resonance puzzle: Geo constructs are placed at equal distances between the mineral and the nearest pillar. Paimon marvels at the minerals' size.

Atmosphere: Desolate and hushed, a former sanctuary of grey stone. The pillars around the battlefield are blank, unlike those of other blessing domains.

History: The domain description gives the site's past: buried beneath the earth during a cataclysm that tore heaven and earth asunder (linked to the War of Funerary Flame), raised by the descent of an alien object (the Spiritstone), and unveiled by a destructive battle that followed a betrayal (linked to Azhdaha). It closes by noting that those who once frequented the place are no more.

The links to the War of Funerary Flame, the Spiritstone and Azhdaha come from the domain description's own wording; it does not retell those events in full.

Dangers: Ruin machines such as Ruin Guards, Scouts, Cruisers, Destroyers and Graders hold the ground. The in-game explanation is that these mechanical invaders came from outside the ancient site. Its Ley Line Disorder (game mechanic) deals true damage when characters use Elemental Skills.

Status as of 7.1: Added in 2.6 and unchanged as of 7.1; it plays no part in later regional stories.

The domain's four levels range from two heavy ruin machines up to a Ruin Grader with escorts, and all share the Machine Nest challenge theme. Unlike other blessing domains, its pillars are blank rather than inscribed, so the site carries no readable ruin writing.

302.comment: The Lost Valley: The Lost Valley artifacts
302.content: Clearing the domain can yield the sets Vermillion Hereafter, Echoes of an Offering, Martial Artist and Gambler. This is a gameplay detail.

303.content:
The Serpent's Cave (also: Serpent's Cave): The Serpent's Cave is a cavern in the Chasm's Underground Mines in Liyue and the arena of the Ruin Serpent, a hulking excavator-style Ruin Machine. Like the rest of the mines it is lit by Lumenstone glow and streaked with black Abyssal "dark mud".

It has a teleport waypoint, Cor Lapis deposits and wall-grown Lumenlamps, and the Chasm's mix of ancient automatons and Shadowy Husks. Nothing in canon explains its name beyond the serpentine machine that haunts it.

Geography: An underground chamber complex on the Underground Mines map, a separate layer under the Chasm's surface, reached beyond the Ad-Hoc Main Tunnel and next to the Underground Waterway. Spoutrock vents, Dark Mud, Lumenlamps and Oozing Concretions fill it, with Luminous Seelie as the only gentle presence. Cor Lapis is the local specialty.

The cave opens up after the Traveler has found all three clues to the missing miner Uncle He in the world quest "Chasm Spelunkers". The serpent's own arena is reached through part of that quest, and its tunnelling attacks, vacuum fields and teleport suit a machine built to dig.

People: No named residents. The exploration team's miners and Zhiqiong work out of the camp elsewhere in the mines. Treasure Hoarders also sneak through the Underground Mines, but the wiki does not list them in this cave.

History: Nothing is recorded about the cave's past in itself. The mines were worked by Liyue after the Archon War and shut during the Qixing's closure, after a mysterious run of accidents and the ooze. Canon places the 500-year-old cataclysm fighting of the Millelith and the yaksha Bosacius in the Chasm generally, not in this cave specifically.

The Ruin Serpent's wiki title is "Excavator: SI/Glp" (a mechanical designation), in the family Automatons, group Ruin Machines. Its drop, the Runic Fang, is a boss material. Which era built it is not stated.

Atmosphere: Echoing, wet-stone caves, a soft glow from Lumenstone growths and the grind of old machinery. The ground can shudder when the serpent burrows, and the dark mud gives the place a sullen, wrong feeling.

Dangers: The Ruin Serpent, a normal boss, is the main threat. It burrows and charges, makes a Sand Tomb vacuum field, raises Oozing Concretions at the corners of the arena and draws power from them for barrages and shockwaves; at the start of the fight it also drains a carried Lumenstone Adjuvant to a low charge. Elite enemies include Ruin Cruisers, Defenders, Destroyers and Scouts, and Shadowy Husk Standard Bearers.

The Adjuvant's blooming light can destroy the Concretions, and a yellow rock created alongside them recharges it.

Gameplay detail: the Ruin Serpent gains very high resistance to damage while it charges its Bomb Barrage or Shockwave, which is why those are the moments to hit its exposed weak points; its Oozing Concretion attack is disabled in the Spiral Abyss version of the fight. A boss drop is the Runic Fang.

Naming: The Chinese name means roughly 'huge snake rock cave' and the Japanese 'huge snake rock hole'; the wiki gives no in-world explanation, and the Serpent's Cave should not be linked to the Black Serpents or the Serpent of All Evils without canon support.

Travel: Entered on foot through the mines after the exploration team's camp is reached; a teleport waypoint in the cave is unlocked by exploring it.

Quests: The cave is open as soon as the three clues about Uncle He are found in "Chasm Spelunkers", part of "The Chasm Delvers" series (2.6). The Ruin Serpent fight requires progressing further in that same quest.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1; no 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content revisits the Serpent's Cave.

304.content: The Ruin Serpent is the Chasm's mechanical boss, a drilling automaton shaped like a giant snake. It buries itself, rolls and drills, and powers its heavier attacks by absorbing the dark-mud Concretions it makes. Its weak points are exposed only while it charges its Bomb Barrage or Shockwave, and a hit disables them until it repairs itself.

305.content:
The Surface (also: Chasm surface): The Surface is the overground mining district of the Chasm in Liyue: terraces, winch platforms and cliff paths atop the great pit, with the entrance to the Underground Mines in the Chasm's Maw. The Liyue Qixing closed the whole mine after unexplained accidents; it is now being reopened bit by bit, and the surface is where the guards, an exploration team and trespassing Treasure Hoarders overlap.

Hilichurl camps and Geovishap share the cliffs with Treasure Hoarders, and Cor Lapis is the local specialty. Millelith soldiers hold the access road.

Geography: Broken, layered rock country of cliffs and platforms around the pit's rim, with Spoutrock vents, Unique Rock Pillars, Pressure Plates, Bloatty Floatty and Geograna. Seelie live here too.

The Chasm's surface and its Underground Mines are separate map layers. The main way down is the Chasm's Maw; a crane platform hangs over the hole and the Mine Passageway lets travellers fall or ride into the mines. The Qixing's Seven-Star seal blocked it until broken during "Surreptitious Seven-Star Seal Sundering", by destroying five large Bedrock Keys on the surface.

People: Millelith guard the road, among them a soldier named Tie Hong who greets the Traveler warmly, remembering the fight at the Jade Chamber. Muning, the Ministry of Civil Affairs representative who is worried about the sealed mine, waits at the campsite by the mine entrance. Hilichurls and Treasure Hoarders squat in the ruins and workings.

Official notices on the surface show the Qixing's position. One records that Yuehai Pavilion voted to halt mining after an unnatural red glow left the gems; another says the old storehouse renovation was stopped for anomalies and that it will be kept as it is for Millelith and Ministry staff. A third marks a relic of old battles bequeathed by Rex Lapis, to be left alone.

History: Before the War of Funerary Flame the Chasm was the land of the ancient human civilisation of Lang-Gan, which worshipped the angel Zibai. The wiki records that when the war's Abyssal contamination reached it, the Heavenly Principles had a Celestial Nail cast down and the people fled to neighbouring Chenyu Vale. Later legends place the fall of the Solar Chariot, and the clash of Morax and Azhdaha, here.

During the cataclysm 500 years ago the Chasm was the epicentre of the Abyssal invasion of Liyue, and the Millelith and the yaksha Bosacius fought at the front. In recent years accidents led the Qixing to close the mine. Before the great expulsion of the Fatui, they discovered black ooze and offered to deal with it, but their device exploded; the Qixing then reopened the surface first, which let Treasure Hoarders slip in.

The Chasm Delvers series resolves the underlying crisis: the Traveler purifies a corrupted nail, and the earthquakes and ooze subside. This allowed the Qixing to reopen the mines while keeping miners away from the more dangerous parts.

Atmosphere: Dusty, wind-scoured stone under a wide sky, with the deep dark of the pit beside you. Guards are cautious; the tone of the notices is one of reluctant, formal warning.

Dangers: Hilichurls of several kinds (Rock Shield guards, Grenadiers, Electro and Pyro shooters, Geo Samachurls), Treasure Hoarders of all types including Potioneers, and Geovishap.

Treasure Hoarders keep sneaking into the closed areas for wealth, and the Millelith ask visitors not to break the law.

Travel: The Underground Mines below require Adventure Rank 28, Archon Quest Chapter I Act III and the world quest "Surreptitious Seven-Star Seal Sundering"; the surface itself can be visited earlier, past the Millelith guard.

Quests: "The Chasm Delvers" (world quest series, 2.6) begins on the surface with the Chasm Charters and the breaking of the Seven-Star seal; the five Bedrock Keys are on this level.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the surface is open, the seal is gone and the Underground Mines are accessible. No later content changes it.

306.content: Notice posters on the Chasm surface record Liyue's official response. One declares the gems' crimson glow hidden by sinister forces and records the Yuehai Pavilion's verdict that mining should stop at once, telling readers to put away greed and look to a better tomorrow. Another halts renovation of an old storehouse near the Lumenstone, to be kept for the Millelith and the Ministry.

key: After Three Bowls, Do Not Cross the Harbor
307.content:
Third-Round Knockout (also: Sanwan Buguogang, 三碗不过港, After Three Bowls, Do Not Cross the Harbor): Third-Round Knockout is a tavern on Chihu Rock in Liyue Harbor, owned by Degui. Zhiruo waits tables there and Iron Tongue Tian tells stories. The wiki notes it seems a favourite of Zhongli's.

Its name is said to come from a sailor who got drunk on three bowls of the house's wine-fermented sweet rice balls; before that the tavern had no name.

Places: One tavern in the harbor, staffed by its owner, a waitress and a storyteller.

People: Degui is the boss and owner and is found outside in the daytime. Zhiruo is the waitress. Iron Tongue Tian is the storyteller.

After dark the regulars include Jiangzhou, Uncle Gao and Uncle Sun.

Overheard in dialogue, Degui scolds Zhiruo for serving full portions and putting real wine into the boozy desserts, preferring to halve portions and use wine sparingly to make more money. Zhiruo says customers complain, but Degui tells her to listen to him and not to them.

Culture: Xu Liushi, a sailor of the Alcor, names wine-fermented sweet rice balls as the tavern's specialty and says he got drunk after three bowls, which gave the tavern its name.

The Chinese name echoes the Water Margin story of Wu Song, who drank many bowls of strong wine at a tavern named 'After Three Bowls, Do Not Cross the Ridge'. The wiki offers this as a likely reference.

Atmosphere: A harbor tavern of wine, stories and sweet rice balls, run by an owner who watches the takings closely.

Travel: On Chihu Rock, the plaza area of Liyue Harbor.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

308.content: Degui owns Third-Round Knockout and is a penny-pinching boss who pushes staff to cut portions and use less wine. He is seen only in the daytime.

309.content: Iron Tongue Tian is the tavern's storyteller. Little else about him is given in this location's sources.

310.content:
Tiangong Gorge (also: Tiangong Canyon): Tiangong Gorge is a gorge on the surface of the Chasm in Liyue. It is one of the entrances to the Underground Mines, and during the Chasm's closure it became a hideout of smuggling Treasure Hoarders, which the Millelith quietly infiltrated.

Ruin Guards and Ruin Graders stand among the cliffs alongside hilichurls and a Mitachurl. Qingxin and Violetgrass grow here.

Geography: A narrow stone ravine in the Chasm's overground area, part of the same cliff country as The Surface. Cliffs, Spoutrock vents, Pressure Plates, Unique Rock Pillars and Geograna give puzzles; Seelie live here. Local specialties are Cor Lapis, Qingxin and Violetgrass.

A hidden two-way passage, the second of the Chasm's mine passageways, joins the gorge to a small pond southwest of the Chasm Withered Tree in the Main Mining Area, where a small group of Treasure Hoarders sits. It is blocked at the gorge end by a gate that opens only from the inside, and a Luxurious Chest is at the gorge entrance. Finding it gives an achievement.

People: Treasure Hoarders had a smuggling camp here. In the world quest "Undetected Infiltration", Millelith Squad Leader Yanbo of the Chasm District and his men turn out to have been disguised as hoarders.

Yanbo waits next to the waypoint of Lumberpick Valley, then splits the clearing of the camps (cooking quarters, alchemy camp, weapons stash) between himself and the Traveler. A larger camp holds a smuggling crew, whose last bosses are named in the quest as Brass Bull Zhao and Chen the Flower.

History: After the miners were dismissed, Treasure Hoarders occupied the closed Chasm. In "Undetected Infiltration" Yanbo confirms the area was indeed one of the hoarders' lairs, and says his Millelith squad, in disguise, first took the Traveler for saboteurs.

The first wave at the main camp includes a Fatui Pyro Agent and a Fatui Cryo Cicin Mage alongside the hoarders; the quest text summarised here does not explain their role.

Atmosphere: A cramped, echoing gorge of pale stone with the rattle of camp life, hidden in the cliffs.

Dangers: Ruin Guards and Ruin Graders, a Rock Shieldwall Mitachurl, Cryo and Pyro Hilichurl Shooters, Geo Samachurls, Large Anemo Slimes, and the Treasure Hoarders.

Travel: Entry from the overground Chasm; it is also an official entrance to the Underground Mines map, alongside the Chasm's Maw and others.

Quests: "Undetected Infiltration" (world quest, 2.6): defeat the "Treasure Hoarders" at their lair, learn they are Millelith, clear two camps and then the main smuggling camp, and report to Yanbo. The quest grants an achievement.

The quest becomes available once the Traveler has finished first talking to Zhiqiong in "Surreptitious Seven-Star Seal Sundering". A Treasure Map Fragment (The Chasm) lies in a tent at the large camp, but the wiki calls it unrelated to the quest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, no change; no 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content revisits the gorge.

311.content:
Tianqiu Valley (also: Tiānqiú-gǔ): Tianqiu Valley is a valley of ruined towers and stone in Minlin, Liyue, once a prosperous settlement. A legend says it was ruined by the rampage of an ancient dragon king, whom Rex Lapis and his adepti imprisoned in an adepti realm, while the dragon's servants fled underground to sleep. A cavern under the ruins holds a Primo Geovishap.

Tianqiu Valley has two waypoints (east and south) and three ruined towers on the west side. The Adventurers' Guild's concern about earthquakes in the valley is what sends the Traveler to the cavern.

Geography: A broad valley in Minlin with ruins, a Geo elemental monument and Seelie. Three ruined towers stand on the western side, each hiding a puzzle: a torch puzzle in the north, a time-limited climb in the west and fights against infused monsters in the south. A large cavern revealed by earthquakes holds the Primo Geovishap.

The towers carry a "Light Actuator" for the main ruins' mechanism. The valley's common enemies include slimes, hilichurls, Fatui skirmishers and Treasure Hoarders; elite foes include Geovishaps, a Geovishap Hatchling, Pyro Abyss Mages and Electro Cicin Mages.

People: Treasure Hoarders work the area; their notes complain of too many monsters, of men who came out "acting strange", and of a warning about a dragon-lord. They answer to a "Boss".

History: A tablet in the ruins laments the cold trail of the adepti and mourns that, though mighty Azhdaha was defeated long ago, this land of beauty cannot be restored. Zhiping of the Adventurers' Guild says, citing texts, that the valley was once a prosperous settlement, and passes on the legend of an ancient dragon king's rampage ended by Rex Lapis and his adepti, with the dragon's servants hiding underground. She treats it as unverifiable folklore.

The Primo Geovishap's own description says folktales hold that after the "draconic calamity" that ruined Tianqiu Valley, the Geovishaps and Primo Geovishaps burrowed deep underground to await their overlord, Azhdaha. Hence the legend is the setting's explanation for the creatures' presence.

In the world quest the Primo Geovishap lairs in a cavern uncovered by strong earthquakes; the Primo Geovishap boss itself came with the 1.3 promotional event "Even Mountains Tremble".

Atmosphere: Broken towers against a wide sky, dry stone and a lingering sense of an old calamity; tremors underfoot suggest something large sleeping below.

Dangers: A Primo Geovishap in the cavern (randomly infused with Cryo, Pyro, Electro or Hydro in the quest), Geovishaps, Treasure Hoarders and infused monsters in the towers.

Quests: "Trails in Tianqiu" (the tablet and the three towers) and "No Restoring This Past Land of Beauty" (Zhiping's request to investigate the earthquakes and cavern).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 an exploration site with the Primo Geovishap still in its cavern and no developing story.

312.comment: Tianqiu Valley: The dragon king legend of Tianqiu
312.content: The legend, as told by Zhiping and echoed in the Primo Geovishap's description, is the only link in canon between this valley and the dragon Azhdaha, who is otherwise sealed under the Dragon-Queller in Nantianmen and in the Chasm. The tablet's poem names Azhdaha as defeated; the quest title takes its words from it.

313.content:
Toy Shop (also: Granny Shan's toy shop, Toy Stall, 玩具摊): The Toy Shop is a small unnamed stall in Liyue Harbor kept by Granny Shan. Its map description says people always want to enjoy themselves whatever the time or situation, and that sentiment seems to be why she has kept running it year after year. It sells spinning tops, wooden swords, kites and other knick-knacks, with rarer toys sometimes on offer.

Only Mora is accepted. The stock includes a zither, lanterns, firework-style toys and a launching tube.

Places: A single stall on Chihu Rock, Liyue Harbor, marked as a special souvenir shop on the map.

People: Granny Shan is the owner. The wiki says she has been a toymaker for over forty years and especially likes making kites. She is the aunt of Zhenyuan, according to her wiki infobox.

Culture: Her toys are simple, traditional playthings: tops, wooden swords and kites.

The shop's list also includes a floral zither, Xiao Lanterns and a Launch Tube, along with toys named for fireworks and festival scenes. The wiki gives no further description of them.

Atmosphere: A cheerful corner stand run by a patient old maker, with a sense of long continuity.

Travel: In the Chihu Rock plaza of Liyue Harbor.

The wiki dates the shop's map entry to Version 2.7. Its stock consists of Mora-priced items only; the Chinese name literally means 'toy stall'.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

314.content: Granny Shan is a toymaker of over forty years who runs the Toy Shop in Liyue Harbor and especially likes making kites. Her niece is Zhenyuan.

315.content:
Underground Waterway: The Underground Waterway is a stretch of clear, cold water running through the Chasm's Underground Mines in Liyue. Zhiqiong found it while exploring alone and thought it the perfect place to rest and wash off the ill fortune of the mines.

It is one of the calmer corners of the mines, though Abyss Mages, Shadowy Husks and a Black Serpent Knight patrol it. It has a Geo and Hydro Elemental Monument and the gentle Hydro Mimic Boar.

Geography: Water-filled caverns on the Underground Mines map, between the Ad-Hoc Main Tunnel, the Serpent's Cave and the Main Mining Area. Features: an Elemental Monument (Geo and Hydro), Ruin Braziers, Rock Piles, Spoutrock and Luminous Seelie. Local specialties are Cor Lapis and Noctilucous Jade.

It becomes accessible after the three Uncle He clues are found in "Chasm Spelunkers", like the Serpent's Cave. The wiki also lists a fishing point here.

People: No named residents. Zhiqiong is the area's discoverer in-world: her viewpoint note says she found it alone, drew it on the map, and hopes the Traveler will follow. The "gentle elemental creatures" she mentions move very slowly and have no quarrel with the world; the wiki identifies them as Hydro Mimic creatures.

History: No history is recorded. The mines were worked by Liyue and abandoned when the Qixing sealed the Chasm.

Atmosphere: Cool, damp, quiet; Luminous Seelie drift above still water. After the black mud and machinery of the other caverns it reads as a refuge, which is how Zhiqiong describes it.

Dangers: Cryo Abyss Mages, a Black Serpent Knight: Windcutter, Shadowy Husks (Standard Bearer and Line Breaker), Hilichurls with Rock Shields or Cryo bows, and Geo and Hydro Slimes. Floating Hydro Fungus drifts through the caves. The Hydro Mimic Boar is listed as a special enemy.

The Abyss Mages show that the mines' wider Abyssal corruption reaches even this cleaner cavern; the wiki does not explain the Black Serpent Knight's presence.

The viewpoint note, in Zhiqiong's voice, says the waters are clean and cool and good for washing off the ill fortune gathered on the way, and that she drew the waterway on the map.

Naming: The Chinese name means roughly 'underground water swamp' and the Japanese 'underground wetlands'; both suggest a marshy cavern rather than a canal, though the English name and viewpoint speak of a waterway.

Quests: No quest of its own. The area is reached during "Chasm Spelunkers" in "The Chasm Delvers" (2.6).

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1.

316.content:
Vault of Qingce: The Vault of Qingce is a cavern behind a waterfall north of Qingce Village in Bishui Plain, Liyue. Rumour says it holds the remains of the Chi, and a floating orb-like mechanism glows golden inside. A secret room at the back, with buildings in the style of Qingce Village, is opened during the world quest The Chi of Yore.

The secret room holds treasure. After the quest, the Qingce Cache challenge can be started inside the vault.

Lore: Local legend, told by Yan'er, says the Chi was a dragon-like monster that held the area until Rex Lapis (Morax) defeated it; its body turned to rock, its blood to water and its scales to the terraced fields. Yan'er adds that in older speech the word "Chi" also meant "Qingce". Locals call the unusually large trees nearby Blood-Fed Trees and say they grew on the Chi's blood.

A piece of incomplete writing says that after the serpent was driven from Qingce, the formula that subdued it ceased to work; its blood congealed into stone and poisoned the world, so three statues were used to hold it down. The Traveler solves puzzles to collect three fragments; Granny Ruoxin explains they are a drawing rather than writing, which leads to the vault. The vault's large amber crystals are said to be the Chi's congealed blood.

Quests: In The Chi of Yore, the Traveler defends the Qingce Cache against falling rocks and waves of Ruin Guard and Ruin Hunter before reaching the chests, a Geoculus and a Seelie at the room's end.

Rewards: The quest rewards the Liyue Shrine of Depths Key. Inside the back room are six chests (one Luxurious, one Precious, two Exquisite, two Common), a Geoculus and a Seelie.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the vault stands open after the quest; whether the Chi's remains truly lie below is still not stated.

317.content:
Votive Rainjade (also: Rainjade's Benediction): The Votive Rainjade is a ritual jade at Carp's Rest on Mt. Laixin in Chenyu Vale, Liyue. Offering Spirit Carp to it raises the offering system Rainjade's Benediction and brings the blessings of soil and water.

Its in-game description says the ancestors of Chenyu Vale's people once threw jade into the waters, passing adeptal energy into the spirit veins; this protected their homeland and secured fair weather and good harvests. The rite has long been forgotten, and if the lost energy were gathered into the jade again the blessings might return.

Practice: Spirit Carp are offered in groups of five. Fifty carp bring the benediction to its maximum level. The offering system's description says it ensures favourable weather in Chenyu Vale for the next year. When maxed, two yellow spirit carp spiral around the jade and its core gives off spirit smoke.

Access opens by completing the quest The Cloud-Padded Path to the Chiwang Repose, which becomes available after An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade. From forty carp onward a Reveal button marks one uncollected carp. Each level pays rewards; the top level grants the achievement One Ring for the Rite of All.

Rewards: Every level pays Adventure EXP, Mystic Enhancement Ore and Mora; the ten levels together pay out among other things Intertwined and Acquaint Fate, Crown of Insight, a Rainjade Statuette and the character-themed item Chenyu: Rainjade Rite (gameplay rewards).

History: Cleaned murals in two caves, the Ancient Cave beneath Mt. Lingmeng's north-west waterfall and Huangcong Grounds near Chizhang Wall, show Chenyu Vale's people performing the Votive Rainjade ritual.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is a working offering site; no later change is recorded.

318.content:
Wangshan Hall (also: Wangshan Hall Main Hall, Wangshan Hall Secret Chamber): Wangshan Hall is the stronghold and training ground of the Guhua Clan on Mt. Lingmeng, in the Upper Vale of Chenyu Vale. The clan has declined, so the hall has fallen into disrepair. To raise Mora for its repair, the Guhua disciple Huang the Third entices visitors in Yilong Wharf to tour it with exaggerated claims about how grand it is.

The tour is in the quest A Wangshan Walk to Remember. The Traveler finds a modest hall, then, using a backup key, discovers a flooded secret chamber holding the real treasure of the clan: books and trials left by the hero Guhua.

Places: Wangshan Hall has a Main Hall and, below, a Secret Chamber that opens after the Scrolls and Sword Manuals of Guhua quest. The Main Hall holds the clan's manuscripts of martial ways, with annotations in a free-spirited hand and a crooked one: the Way of the Rain Cutter (swordwork) is in the Main Hall, and the Way of the Light Piercer (polearms) in the Secret Chamber, waterlogged and mostly illegible.

A key and a series of trials open the gates; the Hall includes an archive in which books must be matched to coloured frames by elemental sight, and mechanisms that drain the water level when a trial is completed. Guhua's own handwritten notes on a failed training day and his dug fish pond are kept there. Later, a Stonehide Lawachurl appears near the waypoint outside, for players to fight (a gameplay detail).

In Shrouded Vale, Hidden Hero an engraved stone and a sword carry an ancient swordsman's inscriptions of slaying tigers beneath Mt. Tianheng and skewering a scaled beast in the Sea of Clouds, with a later hand adding a different message.

People: Huang the Third, called the Cloudpiercing Arrow, gives the tours at Yilong Wharf. Wen the Fourth, the Snowstriding Sword, is gloomy that, after a thousand years of heritage, the clan's head doorkeeper (Huang) must cheat visitors to get by. Other members include Little Que'er, Sun Yu and Wakamatsu; Xingqiu holds the title of Guhua Guru of Feiyun Fame.

Huang the Third and Wen the Fourth are the clan's last elders. Huang asks Wen what will happen to the clan's books once the last elders are gone and nobody is left to test those who might join; Wen has no answer. After the quests he says earnest guests have contributed to the repair fund, though they left little Mora.

Governance: The Guhua Clan's base. The clan has shrunk to a handful of practitioners, most of whom maintain the hall or try to restore the clan's former reputation.

History: In its heyday the Guhua Brotherhood had hundreds of followers and was famed for chivalrous deeds across Liyue. Over time it declined, changed names several times and shrank to a few practitioners. In the Traveler's visit, Huang the Third lures them in with a story of treasure, then is exposed by Paimon (who serves him a burnt, over-salted steak) and, begging not to be reported to the Millelith, hands over the Wangshan Hall Backup Key. He says they were honest compared with others and that the hall's books are better off with them. The key opens the real hidden area, which had been submerged in water, and Guhua's notes and trials beyond.

The Guhua teaching centres on the Three Guhua Greats: Light Piercer for polearms, Rain Cutter for swords and Life Ender for those who master both. Guhua himself used a claymore, Rainslasher, according to weapon text.

Atmosphere: A run-down hall kept going by a few elders; Huang's tours are a bit of theatre, and the depths hold a waterlogged archive.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the hall is still in disrepair, with a few Guhua disciples keeping it going.

Huang the Third is again found at Yilong Wharf by day, and says the earnest guests he brings have added to the repair fund.

319.content: The Guhua Clan teaches three techniques, the Three Guhua Greats: Light Piercer (polearms), Rain Cutter (swords) and Life Ender (for those who master both). Guhua's notes describe devising Rain Cutter after sitting hungry in a courtyard and falling while practising it, which led him to dig a pond and raise fish.

320.content: Huang the Third is a Guhua disciple who tours Yilong Wharf visitors through Wangshan Hall to raise repair funds. He is theatrical and polite, begs Paimon and the Traveler not to report him and later admits they were more honest than his usual guests. He gave them the backup key to the hall.

321.content:
Wangshu Inn: Wangshu Inn is a tall inn built on a giant stone pillar at the southern end of Dihua Marsh, on the main road through Liyue's Bishui Plain toward Liyue Harbor. Travelling merchants rest and trade at its stalls, and its top floor has one of the best views in Liyue. Its boss is Verr Goldet, who insists she is the boss and not merely the boss's wife; her husband Huai'an is the innkeeper. Secretly, the whole staff are Qixing agents, and the inn exists to support the Vigilant Yaksha Xiao, who often stands watch on its top floor and is fond of its Almond Tofu.

Its name means the moon; originally it names the goddess who drives the moon's chariot.

Geography: The inn rises from a massive rock pillar among the reeds and water of Dihua Marsh. From the top, in good weather, one can see as far as Mt. Qingce and Jueyun Karst; to the southeast lies the Guyun Stone Forest. Zhongli explains that it was built tall to survey the terrain and placed on one of the main roads into the region, making it a strategic point that must be defended.

Places: - Lower level: stalls and trading space for travelling merchants, porters, guards for hire and sailors.
- Upper level: the reception and guest rooms, where Huai'an greets guests, and the kitchen of the chef Smiley Yanxiao.
- Top floor: a balcony and viewing deck where Xiao is usually found.

A calligraphy painting called the Witness Sigil, said by Verr Goldet to have circulated for over a thousand years, hangs in the inn; its pattern matches a rock formation outside. A decorative rockery on the topmost floor bears a mark matching a peak near the Statue of the Seven in the Sea of Clouds.

The regular crowd includes travelling merchants such as Great Merchant Huang, a hired guard, sailors, a porter, a poet, and a waitress named Yuhua on the lower level; upstairs are more merchants, the researcher Soraya and other guests.

People: Verr Goldet runs the inn, sells its dishes (from both Mondstadt and Liyue) and insists she is "the boss", not the boss's wife. Huai'an, the friendly innkeeper, is a skilled martial artist; Verr says she and the kitchen staff also train, as a hiring requirement. Smiley Yanxiao is the gruff chef who makes Xiao's Almond Tofu. Xiao, the last Guardian Yaksha, stays at the inn between battles.

Verr claims to come from Mondstadt, and she reads strangers' backgrounds from small details, though one guest notes that no one from Mondstadt seems to know her. Huai'an jokes that he reversed the old rhyme about Liyue girls marrying into "a winery town". Smiley Yanxiao admits he was once a thief who tried to steal from the boss, took a beating and was locked up, and was then taken on in the kitchen; he is terrified of ghosts, once lost narrowly to Xiangling in a Masterful Chefs contest, and Zhongli says he took second prize representing Dihua Marsh in a Moonchase cooking contest in the harbour. A stray cat, Wei, invited itself to stay, and a dog, Richie, is named for good luck. Dusky Ming, the harmless ghost of a little girl, lives at the inn: Xiao found her while hunting demons, and since she was not yet able to move on, he asked the couple to keep her there for a time.

Governance: The inn needs the Qixing's approval to operate, which Verr admits while dismissing the rest as rumour. In truth it is a front: Ningguang revealed to the Traveler that everyone at Wangshu Inn is one of her people, and that she tracked the Traveler's movements through it. Its real task is to quietly assist Xiao in his fight against the lingering evil of fallen gods.

Culture: Official descriptions call the inn a haven for lovers' moonlit meetings, and folk stories say even the adepti sometimes bask in the moonlight here. Stall-keepers also whisper that the tower hides a mysterious secret, a rumour no one has verified. The couple play cards with their guests.

History: The inn is old: Yelan says her clan's elders taught that their ancestor's madness eased for a while only when passing Wangshu Inn, which she credits to the Yaksha's presence. The wiki dates the inn on this basis to at least the years after the cataclysm, about 500 years ago; canon gives no founding date.

During the Archon Quest the Traveler came here with Moon Carver's message after Rex Lapis' "death", calmed Dusky Ming, and brought Xiao a meal with Almond Tofu; Xiao then went to gather the other adepti. Ningguang later revealed that her agents at the inn had been watching the Traveler.

Atmosphere: A busy roadside stop: traders' stalls at the foot of the pillar, guests coming and going, kitchen smells, and above it all a quiet, windy top floor overlooking silver reeds and water. Folk tales make the place romantic and moonlit; staff stay polite and alert, and say little about one particular "young gentleman".

Dangers: Monsters roam Dihua Marsh, and Huai'an often asks travellers to clear hilichurls from the roads so guests and deliveries can get through; they rarely dare approach the inn itself. Some of the night-time damage the staff blame on rowdy "guests" is really the overflow of Xiao's battles, which they discreetly cover for.

Travel: The inn sits on the main route between Stone Gate and Liyue Harbor. Zhongli notes that Xiao travels often between here and the Guyun Stone Forest, where sealed gods breed monster activity.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the inn operates normally under Verr Goldet and Huai'an and remains Xiao's usual base.

After the 7.1 Celestial Nail anomaly, Rex Lapis tasked Xiao with monitoring the Chasm, because he travels swiftly and can report at once; how long this keeps him away from the inn is not stated.

322.comment: Wangshu Inn: Xiao and the Inn
322.content:
Xiao, the Vigilant Yaksha, lodges at Wangshu Inn and is usually found on its top floor. The Qixing keep the inn as a base for him, and its staff quietly support his fight against the residue of fallen gods. He rarely eats human food, but Almond Tofu is an exception, because its texture reminds him of the dreams he was once forced to devour. Few guests know he is an adeptus; a bulletin-board message asks about the youth standing on the top floor.

Each Lantern Rite he battles the year's worst surge of evil, and the couple worry about him during the festival.

323.content: In the Archon Quest part "Wangshu", the Traveler came to the inn seeking Xiao on Moon Carver's behalf. Xiao warned them off, so Verr Goldet suggested Almond Tofu and a dish of the Traveler's own. The frightened chef refused to cook until the "ghost" in his kitchen was dealt with; using the Witness Sigil, the Traveler found Dusky Ming, who promised to stop teasing guests. Xiao, hearing of Rex Lapis' death, resolved to consult Moon Carver, Mountain Shaper and Cloud Retainer.

324.comment: Wangshu Inn: Events at Wangshu Inn
324.content:
During limited-time events the inn has played small roles. During Unreconciled Stars (1.1), when meteorites spread a sleeping sickness, it set rooms aside for victims. During Moonlight Merriment (2.1), all its rooms were booked by moon-watchers. During the Lantern Rite of 2.4, Zhongli visited the viewing deck hoping to comfort Xiao, and Xiao watched the fireworks from atop the inn.

During the Lantern Rite of 6.3, Hu Tao advised the Traveler to rest at the inn; they flew there by chariot with the White Horse Adeptus Zibai, who mused on the name (Xiao explained its meaning), shared a meal with Xiao, for which Zibai cooked the Lang-Gan dish Flavor of Spring, and stayed the night before returning to Liyue Harbor.

325.content:
Wanmin Restaurant (also: Wanmin): Wanmin Restaurant is a well-known restaurant on Chihu Rock in Liyue Harbor, run by Chef Mao, whose daughter Xiangling is its head chef. It sells simple dishes and cooking ingredients and teaches recipes, and its menu is known for unusual dishes. Its map text says some believe it aims to keep everyone fed, others that it wants to unite the world's regional cuisines.

It is the sort of place where Liyue Harbor residents and travellers eat and where a hungry visitor can pick up takeout. Chef Mao, a renowned chef, runs it, and Xiangling is its head chef. Its poster declares a new twist on an old classic and welcomes everyone.

Places: The restaurant stands on Chihu Rock, in the harbour, marked on the map with a restaurant icon. A poster outside advertises "a new twist on an old classic" and says Wanmin Restaurant welcomes you. The shop is open at all hours of the day.

Its map description calls it a famous restaurant in the Chihu Rock area and suggests that anyone short of time can grab takeout. In play terms Chef Mao sells food, ingredients and cooking recipes; stock refreshes on different timers, recipes are sold once each, and a permanent 10% discount applies from Liyue Reputation Rank 4. These are gameplay details.

People: Chef Mao runs the restaurant and serves customers at the counter. His daughter Xiangling is the head chef according to her official page, and the restaurant sells recipes such as Grilled Tiger Fish. Shenhe works there as a server after Ganyu recommended her, and Ningguang has financed the restaurant in the past, as she mentions in her voice-overs about Xiangling.

Xiangling's character entry carries her personality and cooking passions; this entry only notes that she is the restaurant's head chef and that the family's name is attached to its reputation.

Culture: Wanmin Restaurant sells simple food. Among the recipes Chef Mao teaches are Grilled Tiger Fish, Honey Char Siu and Rice Buns.

In the Hereafter quest series the Traveler walks past Wanmin Restaurant, smells Grilled Tiger Fish and buys three servings, one of them to take to the temple of the late Yaksha Pervases. The restaurant is thus where the Traveler gets the food for that visit.

Atmosphere: A busy harbour-side eatery; in the Hereafter quests the smell of Grilled Tiger Fish draws the Traveler in from the street. A scene here is most naturally one of ordering food, trying a new dish and chatting with Xiangling or Chef Mao.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Wanmin Restaurant is open, run by Chef Mao with Xiangling as head chef.

Shenhe works there as a server. No closure or change of ownership is recorded.

326.comment: Wanmin Restaurant: Wanmin Restaurant Staff and Patrons
326.content: Chef Mao is the proprietor and Xiangling's father. Xiangling is the head chef. Shenhe, referred by Ganyu, works there as a server. Ningguang once financed the restaurant. The poster outside says: "A new twist on an old classic."

327.content:
Wanwen Bookhouse (also: Wanwenjishe, Wanwen Bookstore, 万文集舍): Wanwen Bookhouse is a bookshop on Feiyun Slope in Liyue Harbor. Jifang is the owner. Its books are sold one copy of each, and a notice by her table lays down firm rules for readers.

Books on the tables and shelves can be read freely, among them Verses of Equilibrium, a Customs of Liyue volume, a Records of the Gallant volume and a Tales From the Waves volume. Others are for sale at Jifang's counter, including Rex Incognito, Moonlit Bamboo Forest, Records of Jueyun and Mt. Lingmeng Gossip volumes.

Places: A single shop with tables and shelves where certain books can be picked up and read, plus Jifang's counter for the books on sale.

People: Jifang is the boss. Gao Fei and Mu Chen are also present in the daytime. Jifang's spouse is Langqing, according to the wiki's infobox.

Culture: A notice beside Jifang's table sets the house rules: no running, shouting, folly, noise-making, dirty hands or dog-earing books. A second line reads 'Pay first, read later'.

The shop's stock does not refresh, so a title bought is gone. Titles on offer include volumes of Rex Incognito, Moonlit Bamboo Forest, String of Pearls, Legend of the Lone Sword, Tales From the Waves, Customs of Liyue and Records of Jueyun.

Atmosphere: Quiet and orderly, with a proprietress who expects readers to be careful.

Travel: On Feiyun Slope in Liyue Harbor.

Talking to Jifang once may earn a free copy of Records of Jueyun, Vol. I.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

328.content: Jifang owns Wanwen Bookhouse. She sells books at a fixed price and expects readers to follow the shop's rules about care and payment.

329.content:
Wanyou Boutique (also: Wanyou Puzi, All-Having Shop, 万有铺子): Wanyou Boutique is a shop in Liyue Harbor run by Bolai, who sells cooking ingredients. Its stock is mostly fruit and fish, restocked every few days. Bolai speaks in whispers as if his goods were contraband, though they are not.

The wiki says the shop once saw the patronage of Morax. After the Rite of Parting, Bolai speaks of Rex Lapis' death with sorrow.

Places: A store near the northern wharf of Liyue Harbor.

Items on sale include apples, sunsettias, fish and starconches, according to the wiki's list of stock.

People: Bolai is the owner. He acts secretive in manner. Before the quest Of the Land Amidst Monoliths, a second, non-interactive Bolai also stands near the Main Plaza, according to the wiki.

After Rex Lapis' death, Bolai says he is honored to have supplied the silk flowers for the Rite of Parting. He is no Qixing and has no Vision, so that was the only help he could give.

Atmosphere: Furtive and a little comic: a man whispering about perfectly ordinary produce.

Travel: On Feiyun Slope according to the wiki, with Bolai himself found beneath the northern wharf.

History: Bolai is a bit player in Liyue's story: he names the Rite of Parting as his one contribution, and a Character Tale about Zhongli on the wiki is linked from his page.

Bolai is among those listed as present in the Archon Quest opening in Liyue Harbor, where the player is prompted to talk to locals including him, Linlang and Guanhai.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

330.content: Bolai owns Wanyou Boutique. He whispers when selling goods and maintains that discretion is key to business. His dialogue changes after the events of Farewell, Archaic Lord.

331.content:
Wuwang Hill (also: Wuwang Slope, Prudence Slope): Wuwang Hill is a hill in Bishui Plain, Liyue, north of Mt. Qingce. A permanent grey fog and drifting blue ghost lights make it eerie in any weather. The Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula domain stands atop it, and the Wuwang Hill Disaster happened here.

The name means "prudence": locals say it is the hill where even the prudent are punished.

Geography: A wooded hill with a ruined village at its foot and a pond among statues on the peak. A Geo monument, Ruins Torches and Seelie are found about. Cor Lapis, Noctilucous Jade, Qingxin and Violetgrass are local specialties.

The statues on the peak face towards Stormterror's Lair, Dragonspine, Mt. Aocang and Liyue Harbor.

Places: The Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula is a ritual labyrinth where, according to its description, an evil chi was sealed by the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method; rumor says it is still sealed.

Opening the palace means lighting four Ruins Torches and activating the Geo monument.

History: Wuwang Hill was an ordinary place until the Wuwang Hill Disaster over a decade ago. Fetor was leaking from the boundary between life and death, so Old Hu and Hu Tao's father performed the Art of Homa there to burn it away. The rite went wrong: Hu Tao's father died at once from the fetor, and a flood ravaged a nearby village. Old Hu contained the fallout at the cost of much of his lifespan and died before sixty.

Hu Tao later attributed her father's failure to lost focus caused by his worldly attachments. The folk tale in Records of Jueyun says young villagers followed a whale-like song into the Bishui River and vanished, leaving only the elderly, and that the ley lines now recreate the dead villagers' dreams as spirits that lure trespassers.

The Hidden Palace's Chinese name is translated by the wiki as roughly the palace that takes responsibility for Wuwang, which it links to the seal on the evil there. In Chongyun's hangout quest Test of Courage (a hangout event), the hill is used as the venue for a courage test while Chongyun looks for signs of evil spirits.

Dangers: Ghost lights and spirit voices lure travellers off the path towards rivers and ambushes. Hilichurls, Cicin mages, Mitachurls and Tainted Water-Splitting Phantasms also roam, and Rhodeia of Loch lives in the nearby water.

Atmosphere: Cold grey light, thick mist, rotting trees and whispers. In Chongyun's hangout event the hill hosts a test of courage.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the hill remains eerie and abandoned.

332.content: A Homa rite meant to burn off leaking fetor failed, killing Hu Tao's father and flooding a nearby village. Old Hu spent much of his remaining life containing the damage.

333.content:
Xigu Antiques (also: Xigu-ju, 希古居): Xigu Antiques is an antiques shop on Feiyun Slope in Liyue Harbor. It is run by Linlang and opens only at night. It is also the setting of the Rex Incognito storybooks, whose first owner, Min'gui, tries to sell a forgery to the Geo Archon in disguise.

During the day the shop stands untended. The shop sells 2-star versions of the five Traveling Doctor artifacts and its stock is refreshed every seven days.

Places: A single antique shop on Feiyun Slope. Its stock is replenished weekly, and the same sources list another NPC, Qiming, in connection with it.

People: Linlang owns it at present. By day she browses the stalls at the northern end of the harbor and returns to tend the shop at night. The Rex Incognito books name its first owner as Min'gui.

Linlang will buy certain quest items from players for Mora, and each sale can only be done once. These are the three Nameless Treasures, the Dull Ring from the Nine Pillars of Peace quest and the Dragonbone Orb from a Hidden Exploration quest.

History: The Rex Incognito series is a fantasy novel, but it sets its scene here: the shop's first owner Min'gui passes off a fake as genuine to a disguised Rex Lapis. The wiki doubts that these events are real.

The shop is also named in the description of a furnishing item, Fine Brushwork: Bowl of Blossoms.

Atmosphere: A shop of old curios that opens only after dark; by day it stands untended.

Travel: On Feiyun Slope. It is only tended at night.

Status as of 7.1: Open at night as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

334.content: Linlang runs Xigu Antiques. She is seen browsing stalls in the north of the harbor by day and keeps shop at night. She buys certain quest items as one-time sales.

335.comment: Xigu Antiques: Rex Incognito and Xigu Antiques
335.content: In the Rex Incognito storybooks, Min'gui, the shop's first owner, tries to pass a counterfeit off as genuine to a disguised Rex Lapis. Since the series is labelled a fantasy novel, whether it really happened is doubtful.

336.content:
Xinyue Kiosk (also: Xinyue-xuan, New Moon Pavilion, 新月轩): Xinyue Kiosk is a famous restaurant in Liyue Harbor, across from Mingxing Jewelry. It is considered the most authentic place for Yue cuisine and is correspondingly expensive: the wiki says it has a waitlist of about three months. Its dishes are mostly seafood.

Yueshu, the waitress at the door, offers dishes to take away. Notable dishes include Crystal Shrimp, Golden Crab and Fullmoon Egg, according to the character Francis.

Places: Entered through the door next to Yueshu on Feiyun Slope. The upstairs section faces Northland Bank and stands above Heyu Tea House, though there is no way between them from inside.

People: Yueshu is the waitress outside, Heli is inside, and Francis is inside at night. Clerk Zhao is upstairs at night.

Yueshu tells customers without a reservation that the kiosk has a limited number of tables at specific hours of the day and so tends to be fully booked.

Culture: The kiosk is to Yue cuisine what Liuli Pavilion is to Li cuisine. Its specialty is seafood.

Quests: In the quest Know Thyself, Know Thy Enemy, Gentry Maocai meets a Fatui Pyro Agent at the kiosk.

Atmosphere: Elegant, busy and exclusive: a restaurant people book months ahead.

Travel: Across from Mingxing Jewelry on Feiyun Slope.

The Chinese name, Xinyue-xuan, means 'New Moon Pavilion'. Yueshu's food stock includes Stir-Fried Fish Noodles, Golden Shrimp Balls, Fullmoon Egg and Golden Crab, and she also sells recipes for some of them.

Status as of 7.1: Open and still booked up as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

337.content: Yueshu is the waitress at Xinyue Kiosk's door. She sells food to take away, and recipes to higher-ranked adventurers, and is proud of the kiosk's name for classic Yue dishes.

338.content:
Yanshang Teahouse (also: Yanshang Chashi, 岩上茶室): Yanshang Teahouse looks like a teahouse in Liyue Harbor but is actually a casino. It sells high-quality tea and 'other goods'. It first served only wealthy patrons and required a deposit to enter. Tartaglia exposed the original owner, and Yelan now runs it as a secret base.

Under Yelan its rules are relaxed. Chuyi, the hostess, was unfriendly to ordinary visitors and drops that manner afterward.

People: Chuyi is the hostess. Two guards, called the Halberd and the Fang, stand at the door. Guanhai plays cards inside at night. Yelan manages the house and is said to be notorious among its patrons for her gambling skill, with people warned not to play against her.

In the Chinese version the two guards say only a single syllable each, which the wiki reads as a nod to the gate-god generals Heng and Ha.

History: Shortly before the Traveler arrived in Liyue, Tartaglia and Javert confronted the owner over a debt to Northland Bank. After incapacitating those inside, Tartaglia took the owner's Sigil of Permission for himself and exposed his fraud, and the owner was imprisoned.

After Osial's defeat, Yelan took over the teahouse as a secret base.

Chuyi appears as a silhouette in the Character Tale about the confrontation, discussing the teahouse's finances with its owner.

Culture: The teahouse trades on an air of exclusivity. Its original policy kept ordinary people out, and Chuyi's rudeness helped.

Atmosphere: A teahouse on the surface, with cards played behind it.

Travel: On a street above Chihu Rock in Liyue Harbor, with a cliff behind the building.

The name may mean 'on a cliff' (there is a cliff behind the shop) or 'above the Rock', per the wiki.

Status as of 7.1: A casino under Yelan's management, as of 7.1.

339.content: Chuyi is the hostess of Yanshang Teahouse. Her manner toward the Traveler is rude until Yelan takes over, after which it relaxes.

340.comment: Yanshang Teahouse: Sigil of Permission at the teahouse
340.content: According to the Character Tale, Tartaglia found a Sigil of Permission in the original owner's possession and took it for the Fatui.

341.content:
Yaodie Valley (also: Valley of Vibrant Butterflies): Yaodie Valley (the "Valley of Vibrant Butterflies") is a mountain valley in Chenyu Vale, in the southern mountains of Liyue. It holds the abode of the adeptus called the Herblord, hidden behind butterflies and a cave, and locals say it is not welcoming to outsiders.

It lies south of Teatree Slope and north of Mt. Xuanlian. Lingshu Courtyard, where the Herblord lived, is reached from here, and the valley's colourful butterflies are tied to her adeptal energy. Village elders speak of it only by hearsay.

Geography: A butterfly-filled valley in Chenyu Vale: Southern Mountain, between Teatree Slope to the north and Mt. Xuanlian to the south. A cave in the valley leads to Lingshu Courtyard, a cavern-garden of Seelie, stalagmites, hanging jars and stone stands. Its viewpoint is titled "Valley of Vibrant Butterflies".

Lingshu Courtyard holds Clearwater Jade and Glaze Lily as local specialties, with Grounded Geoshrooms and Whirling Electro Fungus as common enemies. Adeptus's Repose, the Herblord's former abode, can be entered through the courtyard's quest or by clearing the Miasma at its entrance. Teatree Slope next door was once part of the Herblord's lands and has the first tea tree of Chenyu Vale.

People: No living resident is named. The only occupants are stone simulacra: a talkative Carefree Simulacrum that scares off intruders, and a Sacred Simulacrum that has to be set on its stand. Xuanfu, a herb gatherer in the vale, tells the Traveler the valley is full of butterflies and not welcoming to outsiders, and that he knows it only from village elders.

The Herblord, an adeptus, once lived here. She is the one who later became Changsheng, Baizhu's snake companion, after the Archon War, according to the Herblord's wiki page; the quest text only calls her the Herblord. Her friends in legend were Fujin, a golden carp adeptus who loves humans, and Lingyuan, a suanni.

The Carefree Simulacrum still guards the abode, saying the Herblord did not like her peace disturbed. It admits it said the butterflies would revive the withered tree on a whim and is surprised when it works.

History: In the distant past, according to the viewpoint text, ancestral peoples who had lost their homes to war were taken in by the adeptus Fujin, who sheltered them here from the disaster raging outside, so that the flame of civilisation survived the great floods. In the Chenyu Vale lore, early settlements in the vale were founded by refugees from the Chasm's cataclysm.

During the Archon War the Herblord and Fujin served the unnamed Mistress of Chenyu Vale. When that goddess tried a flood against Morax that would have destroyed the vale, the Herblord fought her, Lingyuan evacuated the people and Fujin cast the Votive Rainjade into the water. The Herblord was left greatly diminished, and the abode has been empty since.

Notes left in Adeptus's Repose show the Herblord's private side: she grumbles about Fujin's chatter about the "Motive Mainjade", and made slimming tea for Lingyuan while pointing out that an adeptal human form can never gain weight. A third note says she feared something from talking to the Mistress and put some of her adeptal energy into the butterflies, so that the mortals of Chenyu Vale might follow them to the formulae she left behind.

Atmosphere: A hushed, hazy valley full of coloured butterflies, far from the noise of mortal affairs. The quest dialogue is comic with the Carefree Simulacrum's pretended menace; the notes are warm and a little melancholy.

Dangers: Hilichurls and a Rock Shieldwall Mitachurl guard parts of the valley's cave, and Miasma can block the entrance of Adeptus's Repose. In Lingshu Courtyard Grounded Geoshrooms and Electro Fungus are the common foes.

Travel: Yaodie Valley lies in Chenyu Vale's southern mountain, reached past Teatree Slope (added in 4.4). The Carefree Simulacrum says a branch from the revived tree placed in the broken jar outside the abode opens the stone gate.

Quests: "Silently the Butterfly Crosses the Valley" (world quest, 4.4) starts by entering a cave in the valley. The Traveler chases five coloured butterflies back into a medicine jar, which revives the withered adeptal tree, then uses a branch to open the stone gate and reads three ancient texts left by the Herblord.

Completion grants a Luxurious Chest and an achievement, and unlocks the Herb-Housing Hall viewpoint.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the valley is open and unchanged; the Herblord's abode remains empty, and her current life as Changsheng continues with Baizhu elsewhere.

342.content: The Herblord's abode is a cave garden entered from Yaodie Valley, containing a medicine jar that holds a young tree and drives a door mechanism with adeptal energy. Her notes record how the branch she planted was growing, how the door-opening jar was damaged long ago, and her private worry about the Mistress of Chenyu Vale. The Carefree Simulacrum guards it, claims it can stay asleep, and cheerfully admits when it has invented something.

343.content:
Yaoguang Shoal (also: Yaoguang Beach): Yaoguang Shoal is a shallow stretch of coast in Liyue's Qiongji Estuary, south of Mingyun Village and east of Guili Plains. In the local language it was named for the glowing sea creatures that used to wash ashore after dusk like fallen stars.

Those creatures have all been taken by visiting lovers, so the namesake sight can no longer be seen, though the beach still gives up small finds to a patient searcher.

Geography: Low beach and shallow water with Hydro and Pyro elemental monuments, Ruins Torches and a windmill mechanism. Cor Lapis, Qingxin and Starconch are the local specialties.

At the far eastern edge lies an unnamed hidden spot players call Heart Island, for a heart-shaped puzzle that requires two players in co-op to open its chest; the name is a community one and not used in-game.

The name Yaoguang is the Chinese name of Alkaid, a star of the Big Dipper, which is also why it matches a Qixing seat name. The creatures that once glowed in the shallows were taken by lovers who visited, according to the expedition description.

Dangers: Hilichurls, samachurls and Geo slimes roam the sand; tougher foes are Hydro Abyss Mages, Fatui Pyro Agents and Electro Cicin Mages, Blazing Axe Mitachurls, Ruin Guards and Ruin Hunters.

Atmosphere: Calm and romantic by day; the lantern-like glow of the old legend lives on only in the story.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shoal is a peaceful beach with no later canon changes.

344.content:
Yilong Dais: Yilong Dais is a lookout in Chenyu Vale: Upper Vale, Liyue, where visitors light Crane Crown Incense for good luck so their wishes might come true. The tea-stall owner Pingshan tends it, and the tourist Wanjing is met nearby.

A stone hanging over the cliff resembles a crane's head, and the censer sits on it. Pingshan says the adepti will hear a wish made there. Because many guests lose their nerve looking down, a proxy service exists: for about the price of two cups of tea, Pingshan lights the incense for the visitor.

People: Pingshan owns the tea stall and cleans the dais every day, having taken the job over from a master almost twenty years ago. Pingshan laments that crowds are smaller than they used to be and plans to recruit an apprentice and have writers promote the dais. Wanjing, a traveller short of Mora and afraid of heights, treats it as the last stop of a sightseeing trip.

Asked whether Chenyu Vale's people truly believe in the Crane Adepti, Pingshan repeats the master's view that any adepti who protect the people are good adepti, be they Carp, Crane or Deer, and calls them legends nobody can prove or disprove.

Visitors: Wanjing says nearby Qiaoying Village and Yilong Wharf are cheap for food and lodging, and that the Upper Vale's famous sights are what drew the trip. The Chinese name is Yilong-tai.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains a small pilgrimage and sightseeing spot in the Upper Vale.

345.content:
Yilong Wharf (also: Yilong Port): Yilong Wharf, also called Yilong Port, is a prosperous commercial port in Chenyu Vale, Liyue, across the sea from Fontaine and southeast of Lumidouce Harbor. People and goods come and go. Its closeness to Fontaine makes it a convenient place for busy Fontainians to sample Liyue culture without travelling all the way to Liyue Harbor.

Chenyu Vale's people hold an ancestral ceremony here, and its artisans still carve simple jade ornaments such as the Symbol of Felicitation.

Geography: The wharf sits in the Upper Vale of Chenyu Vale, on three levels: an upper level of shops and teahouses, a lower level of food stalls and fishers, and outskirts where researchers and Millelith stand watch. Its viewpoint is titled "The Clouds Cascade Around the Wharf".

Violetgrass is its local specialty. After the quest Our Chenyu Vale Trek, photos from the "Our Chenyu Vale Trek" album are displayed in the central courtyard.

Places: The Jiulue Teahouse, owned by Baishu, has a stage for performances and an outdoor dining area. Fengtai runs the general goods store and Lianfang a street-food stall. A communications office and a Millelith presence serve the port.

Tea merchants such as Fryslan, Hermanson and Jiuguan do business here. Guards for hire, including Dip Yeuk, Hanqian, Yongzan and Yougui, wait for work. The storyteller Jiewu performs at the teahouse. Chan Baatjan is the chef; the angler is Wangjuan and the hydrologist is Woliu; the researcher Ctesiphon works in the outskirts.

People: Baishu (teahouse boss), Quezhi (waitress), Fengtai, Lianfang, Sergeant Lin and the Millelith Xuanzhu and Keshen. Hautemontagne appears here as a random visitor.

Huang the Third, known as "The Cloudpiercing Arrow", is seen by day. The brand image consultant Vert Jr. and the staff of the communications office, Fangju and Lixing, also work here, as does Lixin, the Feiyun Commerce Guild messenger.

Culture: The people of Chenyu Vale go to Yilong Wharf to worship ancestors and the dead. They once threw carved jade into the water in sacrifice; this continued even after the ancient god who ruled the vale perished and Morax took over Liyue's order.

Yilong jade is blue-green and lustrous, and herb gatherers still occasionally find it in ruins in the mountains and valleys. The old art of carving the offering ornaments was lost, but artisans at the wharf still make simple ornaments. The tradition reflects the vale's cultural difference from Liyue Harbor.

History: Sacrificial Jade's text recounts that when Rex Lapis arrived, the vale's ancestors lived as scattered hill tribes, and that over time they merged with Liyue migrants. The ancestral ceremony has survived to the present. Elsewhere, tales of the jade slab that summoned rain and sank into the river explain the vale's name.

During Lantern Rite events the wharf is festively decorated: Vibrant Harriers Aloft in Spring Breeze (4.4) and Springtime Charms (5.3), the latter involving the Jiulue Teahouse. Both are limited-time.

Atmosphere: Bustling, with cloud cascading around the wharf, merchants haggling and travellers from Fontaine strolling the stalls.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Yilong Wharf is a thriving port.

Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 disrupts it.

346.content: A teahouse owned by Baishu, with a stage and an outdoor dining area, at Yilong Wharf. Quezhi waits tables and Jiewu tells stories. The indoor dining area, private seats and rooms are described as under renovation.

347.comment: Yilong Wharf: Yilong Jade and the Ancestral Rite
347.content: Blue-green Yilong jade was once thrown into the vale's waters in sacrifice. The custom faded, but the ceremony at the wharf survives. The Symbol of Felicitation (artifact text) ties the carved ornaments to a pact with a deity and legends of the Herblord.

348.content:
Yiyan Temple (also: Yiyan-dian, Rock-Reliant Temple, 倚岩殿): Yiyan Temple is a temple in Liyue Harbor dedicated to the Geo Archon, Morax. His worshippers go there to offer incense and prayers. Before the events of Of the Land Amidst Monoliths, the yearly Rite of Descension took place here.

The Chinese name, Yiyan-dian, translates as the 'Rock-Reliant Temple'.

Places: A temple on the higher parts of Liyue Harbor, near Yujing Terrace.

People: Fengyan, a Millelith sergeant, is posted near it, as is Bu'yun, a guide at the Jade Chamber, and Musheng during the day.

Fengyan is known for unarmed combat and teaches martial arts to Millelith soldiers. He patrols the area around the temple to see that the Rite of Descension is safe and properly done.

Religion: Prayer and incense offerings to Morax. The yearly Rite of Descension was the occasion on which Rex Lapis gave guidance on the economic direction Liyue should follow in the coming year, per the quest description.

Atmosphere: A place of worship with a Millelith presence.

Travel: In the upper part of Liyue Harbor, around Yujing Terrace.

In the Archon Quest, the player is sent to pray and wish at Yujing Terrace and to wait for the Rite to begin with the crowd; the wiki's Yiyan Temple page places the Rite at the temple itself.

Status as of 7.1: Still a temple to Morax as of 7.1, though the Rite no longer takes place there as before.

349.comment: Yiyan Temple: Rite of Descension at Yiyan Temple
349.content: The Rite of Descension was an annual event at the temple, where Rex Lapis gave guidance on the economic path Liyue should follow in the coming year. The Millelith patrolled the area to keep it safe.

350.content:
Youwang Cauldron (also: Youwang-fu): The Youwang Cauldron is a large tea cauldron at Qiaoying Village, in Chenyu Vale's Upper Vale, said to be a treasure granted by an adeptus. Its sediment-choked interior becomes a battleground in the world quest "Threefold Expectations".

Tea-making in the village has changed, so the cauldron no longer serves its old key function, but it remains a symbol for the villagers.

Places: The cauldron stands near Qiaoying Village. Three connected mechanisms in the surrounding mountains, which locals call monoliths, are tied to it; a technician explains they were designed to stabilise elemental flow.

The technician, Hautemontagne, calls them "Three-Phase Asynchronous Elemental Tuners" and relates their principle to dampeners credited to Alain Guillotin of Fontaine. Uncle Luo holds that mountain Ley Lines wind through here and must be tamed by sacred stones; Hautemontagne politely says the mechanisms are not directly connected to the Ley Lines.

People: Uncle Luo of Qiaoying Village worries over the cauldron and hopes it may draw tourists. Hautemontagne, a Fontaine technician temporarily away from the aquabus project at Lumidouce Harbor, examines and repairs it.

History: Villagers say it came from the Cloud Retainer of Jueyun Karst. They no longer rely on it for tea. In the quest the technician finds that Elemental Sedimentation built up over many years and spawned elemental creatures, so that the cauldron could not run normally.

Quests: In "Threefold Expectations", after fixing the three tuners, the Traveler and Paimon are drawn into the cauldron's inner space, fight Pyro, Hydro and Anemo slimes and a boss called the Eye of the Storm, and clear the sediment. Afterwards plain water flows from it.

Atmosphere: Homely and comic rather than mysterious: village pride mixed with a cheerful technician's jargon.

Status as of 7.1: Repaired at the end of the quest; unchanged as of 7.1.

The quest also contains a bit of dry wit: Hautemontagne quotes the saying that there is always someone better and teapots you have not been to, from Little Mao, and the quest grants an achievement for the tea-in-a-cauldron episode. Hautemontagne was sent to Liyue by the person in charge at Lumidouce Harbor while the aquabus project there was paused.

351.content:
Yujing Terrace (also: Yuehai Pavilion): Yujing Terrace is the westernmost and wealthiest district of Liyue Harbor, built into the cliffside of Mt. Tianheng above the bustling port. It is where the Liyue Qixing and their staff work at Yuehai Pavilion, where Bubu Pharmacy stands on a small island, and where the great public rites of Liyue, the Rite of Descension and later the Rite of Parting, have been held. It is quiet, orderly and wealthy compared with the lower districts.

The viewpoint text describes it as far from the harbor's din, rising with Mt. Tianheng, where the Qixing and the leaders of many enterprises work tirelessly for Liyue's prosperity and stability. The Chinese name is rendered literally as "Jade-Capital Tower".

Geography: Yujing Terrace is the westernmost part of the city, along the cliffs of Mt. Tianheng and overlooking the harbor. Its entrance is at the north, where a crossroads links it with Feiyun Slope, the small island that Bubu Pharmacy stands on and the road leaving the city toward the Guizhong Ballista.

Inside the district are Yuehai Pavilion, the Yiyan Temple with its altar and censers where public rites are held, and Bubu Pharmacy's island; the district's viewpoint is on the pharmacy's roof. A fish pond lies nearby. The Jade Chamber floats in the air above Liyue and the Golden House is in the Mt. Tianheng area.

Places: - Yuehai Pavilion: the seat of the Liyue Qixing and the place they meet to discuss official matters. Their secretaries and the Millelith work from here.
- Yiyan Temple: a temple with an altar in front of it where large public ceremonies take place; a guide named Bu'yun stands here for visitors to the Jade Chamber.
- Bubu Pharmacy: renowned as the finest pharmacy in Liyue, run by Baizhu, with Qiqi as an employee and Herbalist Gui at the counter. It is busiest during and after Lantern Rite.

- Yuehai Pavilion also houses Ganyu, the Qixing's general secretary, and the secretary Huixin. Madame Ping spends her days there, and the Millelith sergeant Fengyan and soldiers such as Jinzhong and Tieshan guard it.
- A fish pond near the terrace is where Madame Ping and Xianyun are seen talking.
- The district's approach road leads past the Guizhong Ballista, an ancient crossbow on Mt. Tianheng.

Other named people listed for the district include Sturdy Wu and Musheng at the pavilion and Hongdou, Chenxiang and Ren'yu near the pharmacy.

People: The Qixing: Ningguang (Tianquan), Keqing (Yuheng) and Uncle Tian (Tianshu), who can be met at the harbor in daytime, along with their general secretary Ganyu. Madame Ping, an adeptus who lives among mortals, keeps company there by day. Baizhu and Qiqi run the pharmacy.

Ganyu supports the whole of the Qixing as general secretary and has done so since the organisation began. Ningguang employs her own secretaries, Baiwen, Baishi and Baixiao, and keeps a private palace on the Jade Chamber.

Governance: The Qixing are seven merchants who govern Liyue; the Tianquan keeps the book of laws and handles foreign relations, and the Yuheng manages land and construction. After Rex Lapis' apparent death they announced that he had died in a divine trial and took full governance. The adepti accepted mortal rule.

Since then the Qixing have begun re-examining the old laws, and have had to deal with the fallout of the crisis, including relations with the Fatui.

Culture: This is where Liyue's official ceremonies and prayers are held. During the Rite of Descension people gathered here to make wishes at censers before an altar; the belief was that a wish made at this time received the blessing of the adepti and Rex Lapis.

Under custom, one Qixing member presides over the Rite each year, and Rex Lapis' dragon-qilin form appears to deliver business predictions. The Rite of Parting, a funeral rite for adepti or gods that uses Glaze Lily, Cleansing Bell and Everlasting Incense as offerings, was held before Yiyan Temple for Rex Lapis.

History: In the Archon Quest (1.0) Ningguang opened the Rite of Descension on the terrace and Rex Lapis' lifeless body dropped onto the offering table. She called for the exits to be sealed and the Millelith swept the crowd, arresting those near the altar. The Traveler and Paimon escaped with Childe's help. The body, the Exuvia, was later moved to the Golden House.

After the Osial crisis the Rite of Parting was held at the altar before Yiyan Temple (1.1). Ningguang spoke of the god's passing as the end of the contract and of an era, asked whether the people would stand with the Qixing as they built a new age of prosperity, and the crowd signalled agreement. Ganyu acted as announcer. The Qixing's public statement was that Rex Lapis had passed in a trial.

The Jade Chamber, which Madame Ping says Ningguang began as a small room built from savings in her early business days, was dropped on Osial in the crisis and rebuilt in 2.4.

Atmosphere: Calm, orderly and well kept, with the harbor spread out below. Officials, secretaries and soldiers move between pavilions, and wish-makers gather around the censers before ceremonies.

Dangers: Few. The danger is mostly political and security-related: when Rex Lapis' body fell, the Millelith sealed the terrace and treated anyone near the altar as a suspect.

Travel: From Feiyun Slope a crossroads leads to the terrace. The same crossroads also gives access to Bubu Pharmacy's island and the road out of the city toward the Guizhong Ballista.

Quests: - Of the Land Amidst Monoliths (Archon Quest, 1.0): the Rite of Descension and the discovery of Rex Lapis' body.
- A New Star Approaches (Archon Quest, 1.1): the Rite of Parting.
- A Thousand Moonlit Miles (Xianyun's story quest, 4.4): Ganyu and Huixin meet Xianyun at Yuehai Pavilion.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Yujing Terrace is still the seat of the Qixing, who govern Liyue without Rex Lapis. No content from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes it.

Ningguang, Keqing and Uncle Tian remain the Qixing; the Jade Chamber, destroyed in the Osial crisis, was rebuilt in 2.4.

352.content: Yuehai Pavilion is the Qixing's working seat on Yujing Terrace. They meet here to settle official matters, though there are days when all seven are elsewhere. Ganyu works as its general secretary, supported by the secretary Huixin. Madame Ping, Millelith soldiers and clerks come and go. Keqing often works away from it at the wharves and the Chasm, and Ningguang retreats to the Jade Chamber to decide hard matters.

353.comment: Yujing Terrace: The Rite of Descension
353.content: The Rite of Descension is the yearly event at which, in the public story, Rex Lapis descends to give business predictions for Liyue, presided over by one Qixing member. In the year the Traveler attended, Ningguang called the god down, dark clouds gathered, and the Archon's lifeless body fell onto the offering table. She ordered the exits sealed. The Traveler fled with Childe's help. In truth the death was staged by Rex Lapis, who lives on as Zhongli.

354.comment: Yujing Terrace: The Rite of Parting
354.content: After the Osial crisis the Qixing and the Ministry of Civil Affairs organised the funeral of Rex Lapis. The Millelith announced that he had passed in a divine trial and asked people not to spread rumours. At the altar before Yiyan Temple Ningguang and Keqing spoke to the crowd, with Ganyu announcing them. The rite was held without any adepti attending, and Zhongli, who had helped organise it, was elsewhere, at the Northland Bank.

355.comment: Yujing Terrace: Xianyun and Ganyu at Yuehai Pavilion
355.content: In A Thousand Moonlit Miles, Xianyun comes to Yuehai Pavilion in her human form and wants to speak to Ganyu alone, worried that an announced visit would make Ganyu insist she has no work for her and quietly make up for it later. Ganyu recognises her anyway and sends Huixin away, surprised to see her in human form. Xianyun later chats with Madame Ping by the pond near the terrace.
